objects.definition: typedef long long int qpdf_offset_t;
objects.description: Signed integer typedef used by qpdf to represent file offsets; intended to be at least as wide as off_t on most systems. Actual width is that of long long int on the target platform.
Exit codes used by QPDFJob and the qpdf CLI. Note that some values intentionally alias others for specific subcommands. Values must remain stable across releases.

objects.definition:
enum qpdf_error_code_e {
    qpdf_e_success = 0,
    qpdf_e_internal,      /* logic/programming error -- indicates bug */
    qpdf_e_system,        /* I/O error, memory error, etc. */
    qpdf_e_unsupported,   /* PDF feature not (yet) supported by qpdf */
    qpdf_e_password,      /* incorrect password for encrypted file */
    qpdf_e_damaged_pdf,   /* syntax errors or other damage in PDF */
    qpdf_e_pages,         /* erroneous or unsupported pages structure */
    qpdf_e_object,        /* type/bounds errors accessing objects */
    qpdf_e_json,          /* error in qpdf JSON */
    qpdf_e_linearization, /* linearization warning */
};
objects.description: Error/warning categories returned by qpdf APIs. Values are ordered and stable; consumers may switch on them.
Type codes for PDF objects represented by QPDFObjectHandle (C++ API) and qpdf_oh (C API). Used to identify the runtime type of a PDF object or internal sentinel states.
Policy for handling object streams when writing PDFs. See QPDFWriter.hh for behavior.
Policy for compression of stream data when writing PDFs.
Bit flags controlling behavior when encoding stream data (e.g., pipeStreamData).
Decoding level to apply to stream filters, ordered from least to most aggressive.
How to represent stream data in JSON output: omit, inline, or reference external file.
Printing permission levels for R3 (PDF 1.4/Acrobat 5) encryption settings.
Edit permission levels for R3 encryption, matching Acrobat 5 menu options. Superseded by newer granular APIs but retained for compatibility.

objects.definition:
enum pdf_form_field_flag_e {
    /* flags that apply to all form fields */
    ff_all_read_only = 1 << 0,
    ff_all_required = 1 << 1,
    ff_all_no_export = 1 << 2,

    /* flags that apply to fields of type /Btn (button) */
    ff_btn_no_toggle_off = 1 << 14,
    ff_btn_radio = 1 << 15,
    ff_btn_pushbutton = 1 << 16,
    ff_btn_radios_in_unison = 1 << 17,

    /* flags that apply to fields of type /Tx (text) */
    ff_tx_multiline = 1 << 12,
    ff_tx_password = 1 << 13,
    ff_tx_file_select = 1 << 20,
    ff_tx_do_not_spell_check = 1 << 22,
    ff_tx_do_not_scroll = 1 << 23,
    ff_tx_comb = 1 << 24,
    ff_tx_rich_text = 1 << 25,

    /* flags that apply to fields of type /Ch (choice) */
    ff_ch_combo = 1 << 17,
    ff_ch_edit = 1 << 18,
    ff_ch_sort = 1 << 19,
    ff_ch_multi_select = 1 << 21,
    ff_ch_do_not_spell_check = 1 << 22,
    ff_ch_commit_on_sel_change = 1 << 26
};
objects.description: Bit flags from the PDF spec for AcroForm fields. Values map to /Ff entries in form field dictionaries.

objects.definition:
enum pdf_annotation_flag_e {
    an_invisible = 1 << 0,
    an_hidden = 1 << 1,
    an_print = 1 << 2,
    an_no_zoom = 1 << 3,
    an_no_rotate = 1 << 4,
    an_no_view = 1 << 5,
    an_read_only = 1 << 6,
    an_locked = 1 << 7,
    an_toggle_no_view = 1 << 8,
    an_locked_contents = 1 << 9
};
objects.description: Bit flags from the PDF spec controlling annotation behavior and visibility.

objects.definition: enum qpdf_encryption_status_e { qpdf_es_encrypted = 1 << 0, qpdf_es_password_incorrect = 1 << 1 };
objects.description: Bitmask status for encryption/password checks used by QPDFJob.
Page labeling styles for section number formatting: numeric, alphabetic, or Roman, upper or lower case.
Result code space for C API calls with ranges for 'no warnings', 'success with warnings', and failure. Mask constants help classify codes.
Enumerated parameter keys for configuring global options and limits in the C API. Values are partitioned into numeric ranges; see qpdf/global.cc for semantics.

A small movable, non-copyable buffer wrapper that stores binary data. It can either own its memory (allocated internally or from an rvalue std::string) or reference caller-owned memory (from raw pointer or lvalue std::string). Provides accessors for size and data, copying via copy() that deep-copies, and move() that transfers out owned content into a std::string. Implementation uses Pimpl pattern via an opaque inner class Members stored in a unique_ptr.

Abstract base class for qpdf input sources. Provides a uniform interface for reading bytes and lines, seeking/telling, and efficient single-character unread across various backing stores (files, memory, etc.). Also offers pattern-finding helpers and internal fast-read buffering. Derived classes must implement the pure virtual methods. Note: inline/internal methods are intended for qpdf internals. qpdf_offset_t comes from qpdf/Types.h and represents byte offsets.

Abstract helper used by InputSource::findFirst/findLast to validate candidate positions while scanning. Implementations define check() to inspect the current InputSource state and advance it as needed to confirm a match.

A concrete InputSource that reads bytes from a C stdio FILE* or from a file specified by pathname. It can take ownership of the FILE* (via close_file) and provides standard InputSource operations (seek, tell, read, unread, rewind, EOL scanning). Copying is disabled; instances manage a single underlying FILE*. Construction and destruction semantics (opening/closing) are managed internally by the class based on how it was constructed or configured. Details of InputSource base class behavior are defined elsewhere.
direct_api_constructors: FileInputSource(char const* description, FILE* filep, bool close_file)

objects.description: Concrete InputSource that accesses a file but opens and closes the underlying file around each operation to minimize open file descriptor usage. It can temporarily keep the file open between operations via stayOpen(true) ... stayOpen(false). Copying is disabled. It tracks current offset and holds a shared_ptr to an internal FileInputSource helper. Details of lifetime and file management are handled in before()/after().

Concrete InputSource implementation that reads from an in-memory Buffer or from a provided std::string. It supports typical stream operations (seek, tell, read, rewind, unreadCh) and optional ownership of the underlying Buffer. When constructed with a Buffer* and own_memory=true, the instance will delete the Buffer upon destruction; otherwise the caller retains ownership. The string-based constructor copies contents into internal storage. It exposes name/description via getName(). Details like qpdf_offset_t and InputSource behavior are defined elsewhere.
direct_api_constructors: BufferInputSource(std::string const& description, Buffer* buf, bool own_memory = false)
BufferInputSource(std::string const& description, std::string const& contents)

objects.description: Represents a PDF version, including major, minor, and optional extension level (for ISO 32000: PDF 1.7 extension levels). Supports comparison (<, ==), conditional update to the greater of two versions, and extraction of version information as a string and extension integer suitable for QPDFWriter APIs. Default-constructible and copyable. No ownership semantics beyond value type; fields are integers.
direct_api_constructors: PDFVersion(int major, int minor, int extension = 0)

objects.description: Public tokenizer class for qpdf. Provides push and pull tokenization of PDF syntax, including an option to surface EOF and to include ignorable whitespace/comments, and special handling for inline images. Manages an internal implementation object qpdf::Tokenizer (not defined here).

Value object representing a single token produced by QPDFTokenizer, including token type, normalized value, raw source text, and an optional error message. Provides helpers for comparisons and type checks.

objects.definition:
enum token_type_e {
        tt_bad,
        tt_array_close,
        tt_array_open,
        tt_brace_close,
        tt_brace_open,
        tt_dict_close,
        tt_dict_open,
        tt_integer,
        tt_name,
        tt_real,
        tt_string,
        tt_null,
        tt_bool,
        tt_word,
        tt_eof,
        tt_space,
        tt_comment,
        tt_inline_image,
    };
objects.description: Enumeration of all token types emitted by QPDFTokenizer, including structural delimiters, literals, identifiers, EOF, whitespace/comment tokens, and inline-image data marker.
Forward declaration of an internal implementation class used by QPDFTokenizer via a unique_ptr. Definition is not present in this header.

Represents a PDF object identifier composed of an object number and a generation number. Provides comparison operators for use in associative containers, helpers to query components, an unparse/ostream interface, and a nested convenience set type for loop detection that tracks seen object-generation pairs while ignoring the non-indirect sentinel (0,0).

Nested convenience container type derived from std::set<QPDFObjGen> with added helpers: add() inserts and reports whether the object was newly added (ignores the sentinel (0,0)); erase() is a guarded erase that ignores (0,0). Intended for loop detection when traversing objects.

Represents a single PDF cross-reference (xref) entry. Supports three PDF-defined entry types: 0 (free), 1 (uncompressed with byte offset), and 2 (compressed with object stream number and index). Provides constructors for each kind and accessors for the stored fields. No dynamic allocation for members; fields stored inline for performance.
direct_api_constructors: QPDFXRefEntry(int type, qpdf_offset_t field1, int field2)

objects.description: Exception type for reporting system-level errors within qpdf. Inherits from std::runtime_error and captures an error description and the corresponding errno value. what() (from std::exception) returns a formatted message created via createWhat; getDescription() and getErrno() provide access to the original inputs. Intended to be thrown when system calls fail (e.g., file I/O). Destruction is noexcept. No additional ownership semantics beyond standard C++ exception handling.

Abstract base class for stream decoding filters within qpdf. Implementations accept /DecodeParms via setDecodeParms, and must provide a decode pipeline with getDecodePipeline. Also exposes flags indicating specialized or lossy compression. Copy and assignment are disabled; lifetime must ensure the returned Pipeline is owned and deleted by the filter instance.

Abstract base class representing a data processing pipeline stage in qpdf. Each Pipeline can forward written data to an optional next Pipeline. Users must call finish() before destruction to ensure all buffered data is flushed. Subclasses implement write() and finish(), and may be reusable or single-use. The constructor takes an identifier string and a pointer to the next stage, but ownership is not transferred; the creator manages lifetimes. Convenience methods support writing C strings, std::string, and numeric types via operator<<. getNext() returns the next stage (optionally allowing null); next() is a noexcept accessor. Copy and assignment are disabled.

A Pipeline implementation that accumulates all written data into an internal memory buffer. Each call to finish() finalizes the current accumulation. After finish() and before any subsequent write(), callers may extract the accumulated data via getBuffer(), getBufferSharedPointer(), getMallocBuffer(), or getString(). Each extraction resets the internal buffer state for subsequent accumulation. The pipeline may optionally forward all written data to a downstream Pipeline (next).

Pipeline stage that suppresses normal finish() propagation to the downstream Pipeline, allowing multiple upstream streams to be concatenated into a single downstream consumer that cannot handle multiple finishes (e.g., Pl_Flate). Data is forwarded via write(); finish() is intentionally dropped. Call manualFinish() once at the very end to finish the downstream pipeline. Construct with an identifier and the next Pipeline*. Owned member is an opaque implementation class Members managed via unique_ptr.

A reusable Pipeline subclass that counts the number of bytes written through it. It tracks the total byte count and the last character seen. After finish(), write() can be called again. Construction requires an identifier and the next Pipeline in the chain. Destruction and lifetime are managed by the caller; the class owns internal implementation details via a private Members pimpl.

A Pipeline-derived filter implementing JPEG DCT compression and decompression for image data within qpdf. Provides constructors for both decompressing incoming JPEG data and compressing raw image data, static global options for resource limits and error handling, and write/finish overrides to process stream data. Internally uses libjpeg (jpeglib). Details of internal state are hidden via a pimpl Members class. Deletion via virtual destructor; constructed by calling one of the public constructors.
direct_api_constructors: Pl_DCT(char const* identifier, Pipeline* next, JDIMENSION image_width, JDIMENSION image_height, int components, J_COLOR_SPACE color_space, CompressConfig* config_callback = nullptr)

objects.description: Abstract configuration strategy for JPEG compression used by Pl_DCT. Implementations customize a jpeg_compress_struct prior to compression (e.g., quality, chroma subsampling). Lifetime is managed by caller; Pl_DCT may be passed a pointer to an instance for the compressing constructor. A convenience maker is available to build an implementation from a std::function.

A Pipeline implementation that discards all written data. It is an end-of-line (no next pipeline) sink and is reusable, meaning write() may be called again after finish(). Useful when output should be ignored while still exercising pipeline semantics.

A Pipeline-derived filter that performs zlib-based inflate (decompression) or deflate (compression) on a byte stream. It supports configurable output buffer size, global compression level, optional warning callback, and optional zopfli-based compression when available. Instances are used within a Pipeline chain; memory usage can be globally limited via static methods.

objects.definition: enum action_e { a_inflate, a_deflate };
objects.description: Enumeration selecting the operation mode of Pl_Flate: a_inflate for decompression and a_deflate for compression. Used by Pl_Flate constructor and internals.

A Pipeline subclass that forwards incoming data chunks to a user-supplied callback function on each write(). Optionally forwards data to a downstream Pipeline (next) and forwards finish(). It can be reused and may omit finish() if there is no next. Safe to continue calling write() after an exception if the delegated function permits.
direct_api_constructors: Pl_Function::Pl_Function(char const* identifier, Pipeline* next, writer_t fn)
Pl_Function::Pl_Function(char const* identifier, Pipeline* next, writer_c_t fn, void* udata)
Pl_Function::Pl_Function(char const* identifier, Pipeline* next, writer_c_char_t fn, void* udata)

objects.definition: typedef std::function<void(unsigned char const*, size_t)> writer_t;
objects.description: Type alias for a C++ callable that accepts a pointer to data and its length; used as the high-level write callback for Pl_Function.

objects.definition: typedef int (*writer_c_t)(unsigned char const*, size_t, void*);
objects.description: C-style function pointer type for a write callback receiving byte data, length, and a user data pointer; non-zero return indicates error and triggers a runtime exception in Pl_Function.

objects.definition: typedef int (*writer_c_char_t)(char const*, size_t, void*);
objects.description: C-style function pointer type similar to writer_c_t but with char-typed buffer pointer; non-zero return indicates error and triggers a runtime exception in Pl_Function.

Concrete end-of-line Pipeline that forwards written data to an externally managed std::ostream. It does not own or close the stream; it only writes and flushes. Reusable across operations; supports write and finish overrides from Pipeline.

A Pipeline subclass that tokenizes incoming bytes using QPDFTokenizer and forwards each token to a QPDFObjectHandle::TokenFilter. All input bytes belong to exactly one token, and any output emitted by the filter is written to the downstream Pipeline (if provided). Uses a pImpl (Members) for internal state.

A pipeline filter that performs run-length encoding or decoding within the qpdf Pipeline framework. Constructed with an identifier, a downstream Pipeline*, and an action (encode/decode). Provides write/finish to process data, and a static memory limit affecting all instances. Internals are hidden via a private Members class and state machine enums.

objects.definition: enum action_e { a_encode, a_decode };
objects.description: Enumeration selecting whether the Pl_RunLength pipeline instance operates in encoding or decoding mode.
Concrete Pipeline that writes output bytes to a provided stdio FILE*. The FILE* is owned by the caller; this class only writes/flushes and will not close it. Reusable pipeline per comment.

A Pipeline subclass that appends all data written through it into a supplied std::string. The string reference is provided at construction and accumulates across multiple uses. If a downstream Pipeline (next) is provided, data is also forwarded to it, and finish() is propagated. It is permissible to omit finish() when no next is set, enabling convenient capture in front of another pipeline.

objects.definition: enum typed : std::uint8_t { strict = 0, any_flag = 1, optional = 2, any = 3, error = 4 };
objects.description: An enumeration used to represent typing/validation options or states within qpdf (e.g., strict typing, optional values, or error state). Exact semantics are not documented here but can be inferred as flags controlling how strictly a type is interpreted or whether any value is acceptable.

Abstract base class for lightweight handle types that wrap QPDF objects. Provides common conversions to QPDFObjectHandle and QPDFObjGen, size/empty queries, array/dictionary access helpers, copying, disconnecting from a QPDF, type/indirection queries, and warning utilities. Intended for internal qpdf and as a base for QPDFObjectHandle-like classes. Lifetime is managed through an internal std::shared_ptr<QPDFObject>.

Abstract provider used by QPDFObjectHandle to supply stream data on demand to a Pipeline. Supports optional retry-aware interface and reporting of success. Implement at least one provideStreamData overload; set supports_retry in ctor if using the boolean-returning overloads.

Abstract lexical filter for PDF content stream tokens. Subclasses implement handleToken to inspect/transform tokens and may emit data via write/writeToken. Used with addTokenFilter/addContentTokenFilter and parse/filter helpers.
Abstract helper used during parsing to decrypt string values in objects containing encrypted strings. Provide decryptString to mutate input buffer in place.

Callback interface for parsePageContents/parseAsContents. Override handleObject (and optionally the offset/length variant) to receive parsed QPDFObjectHandle tokens, handleEOF for end, and contentSize for total size. terminateParsing can be called to stop early.
Convenience POD-like rectangle with lower-left (llx,lly) and upper-right (urx,ury) coordinates. Used for array conversions and helpers.
Simple 6-parameter transformation matrix (a,b,c,d,e,f). Convenience type for creating matrix arrays; default ctor initializes all zeros (contrast with QPDFMatrix identity).
Helper to iterate over dictionary entries of a QPDFObjectHandle. Provides bidirectional iterator yielding pairs of key string and value handle.
Helper to iterate over array items of a QPDFObjectHandle with a bidirectional iterator yielding QPDFObjectHandle values.

Primary handle type for all PDF objects in qpdf. Wraps a shared_ptr<QPDFObject> via qpdf::BaseHandle and exposes rich inspection, construction, mutation, stream handling, JSON serialization, and content parsing APIs. Many nested helper/iterator and utility types are defined inside. Lifecycle is value-semantics with shared underlying object.

Primary public class representing a PDF document within qpdf. It owns parsing state, object tables, encryption handling, page manipulation helpers, JSON import/export, and writing helpers. Construct via constructor or preferred factory create(). Instances are non-copyable and manage their private data via a pimpl Members object.

Nested helper class holding parameters from a PDF encryption dictionary. Used by legacy static helpers like compute_encryption_key and to carry V/R/key length, permissions, owner/user values, and metadata flag. Marked for removal from public API in qpdf 13.
direct_api_constructors: QPDF::EncryptionData::EncryptionData(int,int,int,int,const std::string&,const std::string&,const std::string&,const std::string&,const std::string&,const std::string&,bool)

objects.definition: class Doc;
objects.description: Forward-declared nested class for qpdf internal use. No definition provided in this header.

objects.definition: enum encryption_method_e { e_none, e_unknown, e_rc4, e_aes, e_aesv3 };
objects.description: Enumeration of encryption algorithms detected in a PDF for streams/strings/file. Values indicate none/unknown/RC4/AES variants.

Exception class signaling incorrect usage of the qpdf API or command-line interface. It derives from std::runtime_error and is constructed with a message string. Destructor is noexcept and defaulted. No additional members are defined in this header.

Main writer class for emitting a QPDF as a new PDF file. Provides configuration for output destination, object/stream handling, PDF versioning, encryption, linearization, progress reporting, and retrieval of written object mappings. The destructor is defaulted; lifetime of resources is owned by internal Members. Some nested helper types are declared but not defined here.
Abstract callback interface for receiving progress updates (0..100) during writing. Implement reportProgress(int). Virtual dtor provided.
Concrete ProgressReporter that forwards progress to a provided std::function<void(int)> handler. Useful for C-API or functional-style callbacks.

objects.definition: struct Object;
objects.description: Forward declaration of an internal helper struct used by QPDFWriter. No definition provided in this header; details are private implementation.

objects.definition: struct NewObject;
objects.description: Forward declaration of an internal helper struct representing a newly created object in the writer. No definition here.

objects.definition: class ObjTable;
objects.description: Forward declaration of an internal helper class for object table management. Not defined in this header.

objects.definition: class NewObjTable;
objects.description: Forward declaration of an internal helper class for managing newly created object tables during writing. Not defined here.

Exception class for qpdf operations. Captures an error code, source filename, object descriptor, file offset, and a message; inherits std::runtime_error so what() returns a composed message. Two constructors allow specifying whether a zero offset is valid. Accessors return the original components; only code and message are guaranteed to be set. Details of qpdf_error_code_e and qpdf_offset_t come from other headers. Destruction is noexcept and defaulted.
direct_api_constructors: QPDFExc(qpdf_error_code_e, std::string const&, std::string const&, qpdf_offset_t, std::string const&)
QPDFExc(qpdf_error_code_e, std::string const&, std::string const&, qpdf_offset_t, std::string const&, bool)

objects.description: Primary logging facility for qpdf. Provides configurable pipelines for info, warning, error, and binary save output, plus helpers for standard output/error and a discard sink. Instances are created via create() or defaultLogger(); methods allow routing messages or retrieving/assigning Pipeline objects. Construction/destruction specifics are not visible here; pipelines may need finish() called if custom. Thread-safety: individual QPDFLogger objects are not stated as thread-safe; intended to be used per thread if needed.

Represents a PDF 2D transformation matrix using six parameters (a, b, c, d, e, f) corresponding to the 3x3 affine matrix [[a b 0],[c d 0],[e f 1]]. Provides construction from components or from QPDFObjectHandle::Matrix, string unparsing, conversion back to Matrix, concatenation (left-multiply by another matrix), scale/translate/rotate-by-90° helpers, point transformation, and rectangle transformation. Public data members expose the six coefficients directly. Equality operators compare coefficients exactly (no epsilon).
direct_api_constructors: QPDFMatrix(double a, double b, double c, double d, double e, double f)

objects.description: Base class for QPDF document helper classes, providing a common interface and storage for a reference to the underlying QPDF object. It offers non-const and const accessors to the referenced QPDF. The destructor is virtual and declared (but not defined) here, implying out-of-line definition elsewhere and enabling polymorphic deletion. Construction requires an existing QPDF object reference; this class does not own the QPDF.

Base class for QPDF object helper classes, providing a higher-level API wrapper around a QPDFObjectHandle while inheriting from qpdf::BaseHandle. It stores and exposes the underlying object handle (via getObjectHandle and protected oh() helpers). Destructor is virtual and DLL-exported; constructor initializes the BaseHandle with the underlying object pointer from the provided QPDFObjectHandle. One protected member QPDFObjectHandle oh_ is declared but not used in this header (likely for future/ABI reasons).

Helper class that wraps a PDF Embedded File Stream (ISO-32000 §7.11.4) providing higher-level getters/setters for EF dictionary entries (creation/mod dates, size, subtype/MIME, checksum) and factory methods to create EF streams from data or a provider. It owns an internal pimpl (Members). Construction requires an existing QPDFObjectHandle referencing a stream; static createEFStream helpers allocate new EF streams inside a QPDF instance and return helpers bound to them.

Helper class that wraps document-level embedded files (PDF EmbeddedFiles name tree) for a QPDF document. Provides accessors to query, retrieve, add/replace, and remove embedded files with caching/validation. Owns an internal implementation object (pimpl) via std::shared_ptr<Members>. Details of Members are private and not defined in this header.

Helper class around PDF File Specification dictionaries (ISO-32000 §7.11). Wraps a QPDFObjectHandle that is expected to be a File Spec dictionary and provides higher-level getters/setters, and factory methods to create file specs with embedded file streams. Uses pimpl via private nested class Members stored in a shared_ptr.
direct_api_constructors: createFileSpec(QPDF& qpdf, std::string const& filename, std::string const& fullpath)
createFileSpec(QPDF& qpdf, std::string const& filename, QPDFEFStreamObjectHelper)

objects.description: Forward declaration of a helper class for PDF annotations. Only a declaration is present in this header; the full definition is elsewhere.

Helper class for manipulating interactive form fields in a PDF (AcroForm) within qpdf. It wraps a QPDFObjectHandle representing a form field dictionary and provides methods to query hierarchy, inherited attributes, values, flags, and to set values/attributes and generate appearances. Lifetime is managed via an internal pimpl (Members) held by std::shared_ptr.

High-level job orchestrator for qpdf. Encapsulates configuration, parsing, transformation, and output writing of PDFs and related JSON output. Provides a fluent configuration API through nested Config helper classes and manages execution via run(), or split createQPDF()/writeQPDF() stages. Also exposes enums for password parsing and unreferenced resource handling. Details of some helpers are defined elsewhere.

Fluent sub-configurator for adding a single attachment to the job. Constructed via QPDFJob::Config::addAttachment(). Holds parameters in a private AddAttachment struct until finalized with endAddAttachment().
Fluent sub-configurator for copying attachments from another file/source. Created via QPDFJob::Config::copyAttachmentsFrom(). Finalize with endCopyAttachmentsFrom().
Fluent sub-configurator for building page selection and ordering specifications (merge, select, or range-based operations). Created via QPDFJob::Config::pages() and finalized with endPages().
Fluent sub-configurator for underlay/overlay operations on pages. Created via QPDFJob::Config::overlay() or underlay() and finalized with endUnderlayOverlay().
Fluent sub-configurator for encryption and permissions options. Created via QPDFJob::Config::encrypt(...) and finalized with endEncrypt().
Fluent sub-configurator for page label specifications. Created via QPDFJob::Config::setPageLabels(...) and finalized with endSetPageLabels().
Fluent sub-configurator for global options affecting the overall job (verbosity, general flags, etc.). Created via QPDFJob::Config::global() and finalized with endGlobal().
Primary fluent configuration builder for QPDFJob. Exposes methods corresponding to qpdf CLI options and creates specialized sub-config objects. Instances are obtained via QPDFJob::config().

Helper class for manipulating PDF name trees within a QPDF file. Provides validation, iteration, lookup, insertion, removal, and conversion to map. It owns shared internal state via Members and relies on QPDF/QPDFObjectHandle for operations. Construction requires a QPDFObjectHandle to the underlying tree and a QPDF reference; an optional validator and auto-repair behavior can be supplied.

Nested bidirectional iterator over entries in the name tree. Dereferences to pair<string, QPDFObjectHandle>. Supports forward/backward iteration, equality, removal, and an optimized insertAfter for sorted bulk construction. Backed by an internal NNTreeIterator. Created by QPDFNameTreeObjectHelper begin/end/last/find/insert methods; not directly user-constructible.

objects.definition: class NNTreeImpl;
objects.description: Forward-declared internal class, not defined in this header. Likely implements underlying name/number tree structure. No additional information available here.

objects.definition: class NNTreeIterator;
objects.description: Forward-declared internal iterator type backing QPDFNameTreeObjectHelper::iterator. Only referenced via shared_ptr; no definition present here.

objects.definition: class NNTreeDetails;
objects.description: Forward-declared internal helper/details class for name/number trees. Not defined in this header.

Helper class for manipulating PDF number trees (ISO 32000 §7.9.7) within qpdf. Wraps a QPDFObjectHandle representing a number tree and provides validation, search, iteration, insertion, removal, and conversion to a map. Supports optional auto-repair and value validation. Lifetime is managed by users; contains internal shared state (Members).

Bidirectional iterator over entries in a QPDFNumberTreeObjectHelper. Exposes map-like interface of pair<numtree_number, QPDFObjectHandle>. Supports safe traversal; insertAfter and remove mutate the underlying tree relative to current position. Constructed and returned by QPDFNumberTreeObjectHelper; not intended for standalone construction.

objects.definition: typedef long long int numtree_number;
objects.description: Integral index type used for keys in the number tree. 64-bit signed integer suitable for PDF number tree indices.

objects.definition: typedef std::map<numtree_number, QPDFObjectHandle> idx_map;
objects.description: Convenience typedef representing the full contents of a number tree as an ordered map from numtree_number to QPDFObjectHandle.
Forward declaration only in this header. Internal implementation class for number/name tree mechanics. Definition is not present here.
Forward declaration only. Internal iterator implementation used by QPDFNumberTreeObjectHelper::iterator to traverse the tree.
Forward declaration only. Internal details/helper type for number/name tree structure. Not defined in this header.

Document helper that manages PDF outlines (bookmarks) for a QPDF. Provides cached traversal/validation of the document's Outlines structure, mapping between pages and outline items, resolving named destinations, and retrieving outlines at various scopes. It inherits QPDFDocumentHelper and uses an internal pimpl (Members). Details of Members are not exposed here.

A nested helper class granting QPDFOutlineObjectHelper friend access to call checkSeen for cycle/visited-state checks during outline traversal. Not intended for public construction; contains only a static method.

Helper class representing a single PDF outline (bookmark) item. Instances are created only via QPDFOutlineDocumentHelper (not defined here). Provides accessors for parent, children, destination, destination page, count/open-state, and title. Holds a shared Members structure for internal state and to avoid circular references (parent cleared in destructor). Construction is private; lifetime and creation details are managed externally.

Document helper that operates on a QPDF’s page tree. It provides cached validation/repair of the /Pages structure and utilities for enumerating, inserting, removing pages, pushing inherited attributes, removing unreferenced resources, and flattening annotations. Constructed for a specific QPDF and retrievable via the shared-helper accessor get(QPDF&).

Document helper that validates, queries, and generates PDF /PageLabels (number tree) data for a QPDF document. Provides utilities to build page-label dictionaries, compute labels for pages, and generate entries for ranges when copying/merging pages. It inherits from QPDFDocumentHelper. Destructor is defaulted. Note: relies on other qpdf types (QPDF, QPDFObjectHandle, qpdf_page_label_e) defined elsewhere.

Helper class for operating on PDF page objects (and many form XObjects) within qpdf. Provides APIs to query and manipulate page attributes, bounding boxes, content streams, XObjects, images, resources, transformations, rotation flattening, and annotation copying. Constructed from a QPDFObjectHandle that must refer to a page or form XObject dictionary. Lifetime is managed by user; many methods mutate underlying QPDF objects. No custom destructor work (defaulted).

Primary JSON value wrapper used by qpdf to build, serialize, parse, and validate JSON structures. It is a reference-counted handle class whose underlying value is a polymorphic JSON_value. Provides constructors for all JSON types, writer helpers for incremental output, schema checking, parsing (including a SAX-like Reactor), and offset tracking for parsed input.
direct_api_constructors: static JSON parse(InputSource&, Reactor* reactor = nullptr)

objects.description: SAX-like callback interface for incremental JSON parsing. Parser invokes these methods when entering/exiting containers and when encountering items. Returning true from item methods consumes the item, preventing it from being stored in the built JSON tree.

objects.definition: class Writer;
objects.description: Forward declaration of an internal helper used for writing JSON. Not part of the public API; no definition present in this header.
Bitmask flags controlling schema checking behavior for JSON::checkSchema. f_optional marks schema dictionary keys as optional; f_none selects default behavior.
RAII helper that closes a FILE* when the FileCloser instance is destroyed. Construct with an already-open FILE*. Do not use as a temporary; keep it alive for the desired scope.
Portable time point structure with second precision and an explicit time-zone offset in minutes before UTC. Provides default, copy, and memberwise constructors.

Singleton-like registry and accessor for pluggable cryptographic implementations used by qpdf. Provides static APIs to register provider factories by name, select a default provider, and retrieve instances of QPDFCryptoImpl. Non-copyable; manages internal state via a private Members struct held by shared_ptr.

objects.definition: typedef std::function<std::shared_ptr<QPDFCryptoImpl>()> provider_fn;
objects.description: Alias for a factory function that constructs and returns a shared_ptr to a QPDFCryptoImpl. Used by QPDFCryptoProvider to register and instantiate crypto implementations.

Abstract base class for pluggable cryptographic providers in qpdf. Implement this interface and register it via QPDFCryptoProvider to supply custom RNG, hashing (MD5 and SHA-2), and symmetric cipher (RC4 and AES/Rijndael) operations used by qpdf. All methods are pure virtual; subclasses must implement lifecycle for each algorithm family (init/update/finalize) and buffers per the specified semantics.

objects.definition: typedef unsigned char MD5_Digest[16];
objects.description: Typedef defined inside QPDFCryptoImpl for a 16-byte MD5 digest buffer. Used as the output parameter type for MD5_digest(). Note: this is an array type alias; it decays to unsigned char* in most APIs. Construction is by allocation of a 16-byte buffer.

Abstract interface for supplying cryptographically suitable random bytes to qpdf. Users implement this class and override provideRandomData to fill the provided buffer with len bytes of random data. The default constructor is protected (and marked private for DLL purposes), enforcing creation only via subclassing. Copy and assignment are disabled.

objects.definition: typedef struct _qpdf_data* qpdf_data;
objects.description: Opaque handle to library-managed state for a qpdf processing session. It represents the C wrapper around an internal C++ QPDF instance and caches object handles, strings, buffers, warnings, and errors. Must be created with qpdf_init and ultimately destroyed with qpdf_cleanup. Not thread-safe per instance.

objects.definition: typedef struct _qpdf_error* qpdf_error;
objects.description: Opaque handle describing a single error or warning captured by the qpdf C API. Instances are obtained from qpdf_get_error or qpdf_next_warning and are owned by the qpdf_data that produced them. Their memory becomes invalid after the next error/warning retrieval or qpdf_cleanup.

objects.definition: typedef int QPDF_ERROR_CODE;
objects.description: Integer error/status bitmask returned by many API calls. Bits include QPDF_WARNINGS and QPDF_ERRORS; 0 indicates success. Values may be ORed. Not an opaque handle; typedef provided for clarity.

objects.definition: typedef int QPDF_BOOL;
objects.description: Integer boolean type used by this C API. Values are QPDF_TRUE (1) and QPDF_FALSE (0).

objects.definition: typedef int (*qpdf_write_fn_t)(char const* data, size_t len, void* udata);
objects.description: Callback function pointer type used by qpdf_write_json to stream JSON output. Should return 0 on success. The implementation is provided by the caller; the library does not allocate or free it.

objects.definition: typedef unsigned int qpdf_oh;
objects.description: Value-type handle (nonzero unsigned int) that identifies a specific QPDFObjectHandle within a qpdf_data instance. Two calls returning the same underlying PDF object will still yield distinct handle values. Handles can be released early with qpdf_oh_release to reduce memory footprint; objects persist if referenced elsewhere in the document structure.

objects.definition: typedef struct _qpdfjob_handle* qpdfjob_handle;
objects.description: Opaque handle type for a QPDFJob instance. The actual struct is not defined here (incomplete type); the handle is used with the qpdfjob_* API to configure and run a QPDF job. Lifetime: obtain with qpdfjob_init and release with qpdfjob_cleanup. Do not dereference; treat as opaque.

objects.definition: typedef struct _qpdflogger_handle* qpdflogger_handle;
objects.description: Opaque handle type for a QPDF logger instance in the C API. It is a pointer to an incomplete struct, serving as a handle to the underlying C++ QPDFLogger. The handle itself is reference-counted/shared; cleaning up the handle does not destroy the underlying logger object.
Enumeration specifying logging destinations for the QPDF logger: default behavior, stdout, stderr, discard output, or a custom callback.

objects.definition: typedef int (*qpdf_log_fn_t)(char const* data, size_t len, void* udata);
objects.description: Function pointer type for custom log handlers. The function receives a data buffer and length along with a user data pointer and should return 0 on success (nonzero indicates failure).

functions.name: QIntC::IntConverter<From, To, false, false>::convert
functions.signature: template <typename From, typename To> static To QIntC::IntConverter<From, To, false, false>::convert(From const& i)
functions.description: Converts an unsigned integer value i of type From to an unsigned integer of type To with range checking. Throws std::range_error if i exceeds std::numeric_limits<To>::max(). Intended for safe casts between unsigned integral types.
requirements: From and To must be unsigned integral types compatible with std::numeric_limits and static_cast.
Argument i must be representable in type To (i <= std::numeric_limits<To>::max()).
On failure, the function throws std::range_error; callers must be prepared to handle this exception.

functions.name: QIntC::IntConverter<From, To, false, false>::error
functions.signature: template <typename From, typename To> static void QIntC::IntConverter<From, To, false, false>::error(From i)
functions.description: Helper that constructs a diagnostic message and throws std::range_error for unsigned-to-unsigned conversion overflow. It never returns.
requirements: This function always throws std::range_error; callers should not expect it to return.
From must be an unsigned integral type (matches the specialization context).

functions.name: QIntC::IntConverter<From, To, true, true>::convert
functions.signature: template <typename From, typename To> static To QIntC::IntConverter<From, To, true, true>::convert(From const& i)
functions.description: Converts a signed integer value i of type From to a signed integer of type To with range checking. Throws std::range_error if i is outside [std::numeric_limits<To>::min(), std::numeric_limits<To>::max()].
requirements: From and To must be signed integral types compatible with std::numeric_limits and static_cast.
Argument i must be representable in type To (within To's min/max).
On failure, the function throws std::range_error; callers must be prepared to handle this exception.

functions.name: QIntC::IntConverter<From, To, true, true>::error
functions.signature: template <typename From, typename To> static void QIntC::IntConverter<From, To, true, true>::error(From i)
functions.description: Helper that constructs a diagnostic message and throws std::range_error for signed-to-signed conversion overflow/underflow. It never returns.
requirements: This function always throws std::range_error; callers should not expect it to return.
From must be a signed integral type (matches the specialization context).

functions.name: QIntC::IntConverter<From, To, true, false>::convert
functions.signature: template <typename From, typename To> static To QIntC::IntConverter<From, To, true, false>::convert(From const& i)
functions.description: Converts a signed integer value i of type From to an unsigned integer of type To with range checking. Throws std::range_error if i < 0 or if the unsigned magnitude exceeds std::numeric_limits<To>::max().
requirements: From must be a signed integral type; To must be an unsigned integral type.
Argument i must be non-negative and its value must be <= std::numeric_limits<To>::max().
On failure, the function throws std::range_error; callers must be prepared to handle this exception.

functions.name: QIntC::IntConverter<From, To, true, false>::error
functions.signature: template <typename From, typename To> static void QIntC::IntConverter<From, To, true, false>::error(From i)
functions.description: Helper that constructs a diagnostic message and throws std::range_error for signed-to-unsigned conversion errors (negative input or overflow). It never returns.
requirements: This function always throws std::range_error; callers should not expect it to return.
From must be a signed integral type (matches the specialization context).

functions.name: QIntC::IntConverter<From, To, false, true>::convert
functions.signature: template <typename From, typename To> static To QIntC::IntConverter<From, To, false, true>::convert(From const& i)
functions.description: Converts an unsigned integer value i of type From to a signed integer of type To with range checking. Throws std::range_error if i exceeds the maximum positive value representable by To.
requirements: From must be an unsigned integral type; To must be a signed integral type.
Argument i must be <= static_cast<make_unsigned<To>::type>(std::numeric_limits<To>::max()).
On failure, the function throws std::range_error; callers must be prepared to handle this exception.

functions.name: QIntC::IntConverter<From, To, false, true>::error
functions.signature: template <typename From, typename To> static void QIntC::IntConverter<From, To, false, true>::error(From i)
functions.description: Helper that constructs a diagnostic message and throws std::range_error for unsigned-to-signed conversion overflow. It never returns.
requirements: This function always throws std::range_error; callers should not expect it to return.
From must be an unsigned integral type (matches the specialization context).

functions.name: QIntC::to_char
functions.signature: template <typename T> inline char QIntC::to_char(T const& i)
functions.description: Safely converts i to char using IntConverter<T, char>::convert with overflow/underflow checks. Throws std::range_error if i is not representable as char.
requirements: T must be an integer-like type usable with std::numeric_limits and static_cast to char.
Argument i must be representable in char's range (implementation-defined signedness).
On failure, the function throws std::range_error; callers must be prepared to handle this exception.

functions.name: QIntC::to_uchar
functions.signature: template <typename T> inline unsigned char QIntC::to_uchar(T const& i)
functions.description: Safely converts i to unsigned char using IntConverter with range checking. Throws std::range_error if out of range.
requirements: T must be an integer-like type usable with std::numeric_limits and static_cast to unsigned char.
Argument i must be in [0, UCHAR_MAX] for the platform.
On failure, the function throws std::range_error.

functions.name: QIntC::to_short
functions.signature: template <typename T> inline short QIntC::to_short(T const& i)
functions.description: Safely converts i to short with overflow/underflow checks. Throws std::range_error on out-of-range.
requirements: T must be an integer-like type usable with std::numeric_limits and static_cast to short.
Argument i must be within short's representable range.
On failure, the function throws std::range_error.

functions.name: QIntC::to_ushort
functions.signature: template <typename T> inline unsigned short QIntC::to_ushort(T const& i)
functions.description: Safely converts i to unsigned short with range checking. Throws std::range_error if out of range.
requirements: T must be an integer-like type usable with std::numeric_limits and static_cast to unsigned short.
Argument i must be within [0, USHRT_MAX].
On failure, the function throws std::range_error.

functions.name: QIntC::to_int
functions.signature: template <typename T> inline int QIntC::to_int(T const& i)
functions.description: Safely converts i to int with overflow/underflow checks. Throws std::range_error on out-of-range.
requirements: T must be an integer-like type usable with std::numeric_limits and static_cast to int.
Argument i must be within int's representable range.
On failure, the function throws std::range_error.

functions.name: QIntC::to_uint
functions.signature: template <typename T> inline unsigned int QIntC::to_uint(T const& i)
functions.description: Safely converts i to unsigned int with range checking. Throws std::range_error if out of range.
requirements: T must be an integer-like type usable with std::numeric_limits and static_cast to unsigned int.
Argument i must be within [0, UINT_MAX].
On failure, the function throws std::range_error.

functions.name: QIntC::to_size
functions.signature: template <typename T> inline size_t QIntC::to_size(T const& i)
functions.description: Safely converts i to size_t with range checking. Throws std::range_error if out of range.
requirements: T must be an integer-like type usable with std::numeric_limits and static_cast to size_t.
Argument i must be within size_t's representable range (implementation- and platform-dependent).
On failure, the function throws std::range_error.

functions.name: QIntC::to_offset
functions.signature: template <typename T> inline qpdf_offset_t QIntC::to_offset(T const& i)
functions.description: Safely converts i to qpdf_offset_t (a qpdf-defined integer type) with range checking. Throws std::range_error if out of range.
requirements: T must be an integer-like type usable with std::numeric_limits and static_cast to qpdf_offset_t.
Argument i must be within qpdf_offset_t's representable range (as defined in qpdf/Types.h).
On failure, the function throws std::range_error.

functions.name: QIntC::to_long
functions.signature: template <typename T> inline long QIntC::to_long(T const& i)
functions.description: Safely converts i to long with overflow/underflow checks. Throws std::range_error on out-of-range.
requirements: T must be an integer-like type usable with std::numeric_limits and static_cast to long.
Argument i must be within long's representable range.
On failure, the function throws std::range_error.

functions.name: QIntC::to_ulong
functions.signature: template <typename T> inline unsigned long QIntC::to_ulong(T const& i)
functions.description: Safely converts i to unsigned long with range checking. Throws std::range_error if out of range.
requirements: T must be an integer-like type usable with std::numeric_limits and static_cast to unsigned long.
Argument i must be within [0, ULONG_MAX].
On failure, the function throws std::range_error.

functions.name: QIntC::to_longlong
functions.signature: template <typename T> inline long long QIntC::to_longlong(T const& i)
functions.description: Safely converts i to long long with range checking. Throws std::range_error if out of range.
requirements: T must be an integer-like type usable with std::numeric_limits and static_cast to long long.
Argument i must be within long long's representable range.
On failure, the function throws std::range_error.

functions.name: QIntC::to_ulonglong
functions.signature: template <typename T> inline unsigned long long QIntC::to_ulonglong(T const& i)
functions.description: Safely converts i to unsigned long long with range checking. Throws std::range_error if out of range.
requirements: T must be an integer-like type usable with std::numeric_limits and static_cast to unsigned long long.
Argument i must be within [0, ULLONG_MAX].
On failure, the function throws std::range_error.

functions.name: QIntC::range_check_error
functions.signature: template <typename T> void QIntC::range_check_error(T const& cur, T const& delta)
functions.description: Checks whether adding delta to cur would overflow or underflow type T. Throws std::range_error with a diagnostic message if the addition would exceed std::numeric_limits<T>::max() or go below std::numeric_limits<T>::min(). No-op if safe.
requirements: T must be an integer type compatible with std::numeric_limits, comparisons, and arithmetic.
cur and delta are treated as current value and increment to add; they must be representable as T.
On detection of overflow/underflow, the function throws std::range_error; callers must handle the exception.

functions.name: QIntC::range_check
functions.signature: template <typename T> inline void QIntC::range_check(T const& cur, T const& delta)
functions.description: Optimized pre-check for adding delta to cur. Quickly returns when signs of cur and delta guarantee no overflow, otherwise delegates to range_check_error to perform full limits checks and potentially throw std::range_error.
requirements: T must be an integer type compatible with std::numeric_limits, comparisons, and arithmetic.
cur and delta are interpreted as current value and increment; both must be T.
May throw std::range_error via range_check_error; callers must handle exceptions if they rely on it for safety.

functions.name: QIntC::range_check_subtract_error
functions.signature: template <typename T> void QIntC::range_check_subtract_error(T const& cur, T const& delta)
functions.description: Checks whether subtracting delta from cur (i.e., cur - delta) would overflow or underflow type T. Throws std::range_error if the result would be outside [std::numeric_limits<T>::min(), std::numeric_limits<T>::max()].
requirements: T must be an integer type compatible with std::numeric_limits, comparisons, and arithmetic.
cur and delta are treated as current value and amount to subtract; they must be representable as T.
On detection of overflow/underflow, the function throws std::range_error; callers must handle the exception.

functions.name: QIntC::range_check_subtract
functions.signature: template <typename T> inline void QIntC::range_check_subtract(T const& cur, T const& delta)
functions.description: Optimized pre-check for subtracting delta from cur. Quickly returns when signs of cur and delta guarantee no overflow, otherwise delegates to range_check_subtract_error for full bounds checking and potential std::range_error.
requirements: T must be an integer type compatible with std::numeric_limits, comparisons, and arithmetic.
cur and delta must be T; interpreted as current value and amount to subtract.
May throw std::range_error via range_check_subtract_error; callers must handle exceptions if they rely on it for safety.

functions.name: QTC::TC_real
functions.signature: QPDF_DLL void QTC::TC_real(char const* const scope, char const* const ccase, int n = 0);
functions.description: Core QTC event/test-case marker. Records or signals a QTC event identified by a textual scope and case name, with an optional integer parameter. Intended for instrumentation/coverage-style hooks inside qpdf and for use by end users linking against the library. Details of persistence, logging, or counters are not documented here; the integer n’s exact meaning is unknown from this header and likely used for counting or variant tagging.
requirements: scope must be a valid pointer to a null-terminated C string; behavior for nullptr or non-terminated data is unspecified.
ccase must be a valid pointer to a null-terminated C string; behavior for nullptr or non-terminated data is unspecified.
n is an integer and may be omitted; no range constraints are documented.
This function is available regardless of whether QPDF_DISABLE_QTC is defined (the symbol is exported). No-op behavior is not indicated here; callers should assume it performs the QTC action.

functions.name: QTC::TC
functions.signature: inline void QTC::TC(char const* const scope, char const* const ccase, int n = 0);
functions.description: Convenience inline wrapper for QTC::TC_real. When QPDF_DISABLE_QTC is not defined, it forwards to TC_real; when QPDF_DISABLE_QTC is defined, calls are compiled out and have no effect. Use this in instrumented code to mark QTC events without introducing a link-time dependency when QTC is disabled.
requirements: scope must be a valid pointer to a null-terminated C string; behavior for nullptr or non-terminated data is unspecified.
ccase must be a valid pointer to a null-terminated C string; behavior for nullptr or non-terminated data is unspecified.
n is an integer and may be omitted; no range constraints are documented.
If QPDF_DISABLE_QTC is defined at compile time, calling QTC::TC becomes a no-op (the call is elided). If you need the call to occur regardless of that macro, call QTC::TC_real directly.

functions.name: PointerHolder::PointerHolder
functions.description: Constructs a PointerHolder<T> from an existing std::shared_ptr<T>, preserving ownership semantics. Intended to ease transition from PointerHolder to std::shared_ptr and allow interop.
requirements: PointerHolder<T> is only defined when POINTERHOLDER_TRANSITION < 4 at include time.
The std::shared_ptr<T> passed must manage a T allocated with a deleter appropriate for its lifetime; ownership is shared.
T must be a complete type at the point of destruction (standard shared_ptr requirement).

functions.name: PointerHolder::~PointerHolder
functions.description: Virtual defaulted destructor. Destroys the PointerHolder<T> and releases shared ownership of the managed object/array, deleting it when the last owner releases.
requirements: PointerHolder<T> is only defined when POINTERHOLDER_TRANSITION < 4 at include time.
T must be complete at the point where the last shared owner is destroyed.

functions.name: PointerHolder::getPointer
functions.description: Returns the underlying raw T* (same as get()). Historically provided by PointerHolder; may be deprecated in some transition levels. Non-const overload returns T*.
requirements: PointerHolder<T> is only defined when POINTERHOLDER_TRANSITION < 4 at include time.
Returned pointer may be nullptr; callers must check before dereferencing.
The returned pointer is non-owning; do not delete it. Lifespan is tied to the shared ownership.

functions.name: PointerHolder::getRefcount
functions.description: Returns the current shared ownership count (use_count()) cast to int. Provided for backward compatibility; may be deprecated depending on transition level.
requirements: PointerHolder<T> is only defined when POINTERHOLDER_TRANSITION < 4 at include time.
The value is a snapshot; it may change due to concurrent copies/resets of shared_ptr elsewhere.
Return value may truncate on very large counts due to int cast.

functions.name: PointerHolder::operator=
functions.description: Assigns nullptr to the PointerHolder<T>, resetting it to an empty state (equivalent to std::shared_ptr<T>::operator=(nullptr)).
requirements: PointerHolder<T> is only defined when POINTERHOLDER_TRANSITION < 4 at include time.
After assignment, previous managed object may be destroyed if this was the last owner.

functions.name: PointerHolder::operator*
functions.description: Dereferences the managed pointer and returns a reference to T. Non-const overload.
requirements: PointerHolder<T> is only defined when POINTERHOLDER_TRANSITION < 4 at include time.
The holder must not be empty; get() (or getPointer()) must return non-null, otherwise behavior is undefined.

functions.name: PointerHolder::operator->
functions.description: Arrow operator providing pointer-like access to the managed object. Non-const overload.
requirements: PointerHolder<T> is only defined when POINTERHOLDER_TRANSITION < 4 at include time.
The holder must not be empty; get() (or getPointer()) must return non-null before using operator->(), otherwise behavior is undefined.

functions.name: make_pointer_holder
functions.description: Factory function that constructs a new T using the provided arguments and returns a PointerHolder<T> owning it (analogous to std::make_shared but implemented with new T(...)).
requirements: PointerHolder<T> is only defined when POINTERHOLDER_TRANSITION < 4 at include time.
T must have a constructor matching the forwarded arguments and that constructor must be accessible.
Construction may throw; if allocation or construction fails, standard exceptions (e.g., std::bad_alloc) propagate.
Ownership of the newly created object is managed by the returned PointerHolder; caller must not delete it.

functions.name: make_array_pointer_holder
functions.description: Allocates an array of n elements using new T[n] and returns a PointerHolder<T> that owns it with an array deleter (std::default_delete<T[]>()), enabling safe shared ownership of arrays.
requirements: PointerHolder<T> is only defined when POINTERHOLDER_TRANSITION < 4 at include time.
n must be a valid allocation size for new T[n]; if n is 0, behavior follows compiler/platform rules for new T[0].
T must be default-constructible (for new T[n]) and the constructor must not throw for the requested n, or exceptions may propagate.
Returned PointerHolder assumes array ownership; caller must not delete the array.

functions.name: Buffer::Buffer
functions.description: Default-constructs an empty Buffer. The buffer does not contain any data and typically does not own any memory until populated.

functions.name: Buffer::Buffer
functions.description: Constructs a Buffer that allocates and owns a block of memory of the specified size, which will be freed when the Buffer is destroyed.
requirements: size specifies the number of bytes to allocate; it may be 0.
Callers must not assume the memory is initialized; initialize before reading.
Pointers obtained via getBuffer()/data() remain valid until the Buffer is destroyed or moved.

functions.name: Buffer::Buffer
functions.description: Constructs a Buffer that takes ownership of the storage of the provided rvalue std::string. The Buffer will free this memory when destroyed.
requirements: The argument must be an rvalue (e.g., std::move(str)).
After construction, the moved-from std::string must not be used to access the old content.
The Buffer’s content size equals content.size() at the time of construction.

functions.name: Buffer::Buffer
functions.description: Constructs a Buffer that references externally owned memory. The Buffer does not take ownership and will not free the memory on destruction.
requirements: buf must point to a contiguous memory block of at least size bytes when size > 0.
If size == 0, buf may be null; callers must handle that getBuffer() may return nullptr.
The pointed-to memory must remain valid and unmodified in lifetime-sensitive ways for at least as long as this Buffer is used.
Callers are responsible for managing the lifetime and deallocation of buf; the Buffer will not free it.
Reading/writing through getBuffer()/data() must not exceed size bytes.

functions.name: Buffer::Buffer
functions.description: Constructs a Buffer that references the storage of the provided std::string without taking ownership. The Buffer will not free the memory.
requirements: content’s storage must remain valid and unchanged in lifetime-sensitive ways for at least as long as this Buffer is used (do not destroy or reallocate content).
Modifying content in ways that reallocate its storage (e.g., growth) may invalidate pointers/views from the Buffer and must be avoided while the Buffer is in use.
The Buffer reflects content.size() at construction; subsequent changes to content’s size or capacity may not be reflected and may invalidate access.

functions.name: Buffer::Buffer
functions.description: Move-constructs a Buffer, transferring any owned memory from the source. If the source owned its memory, it becomes empty after the move; otherwise, the source remains unchanged.
requirements: The moved-from Buffer must not be used except for destruction, reassignment, or queries explicitly documented as safe on moved-from objects.
Any pointers, views, or references obtained from the source Buffer before the move may be invalid after the move if the source owned its memory.

functions.name: Buffer::operator=
functions.description: Copy assignment is explicitly deleted. The Buffer cannot be copy-assigned.
requirements: This overload must not be used; attempting to copy-assign a Buffer will not compile.

functions.name: Buffer::~Buffer
functions.description: Destroys the Buffer, freeing its memory only if it owns it. For Buffers that reference external memory, no deallocation is performed.
requirements: Callers must not access pointers, views, or references from this Buffer after destruction.
For Buffers referencing external memory, callers remain responsible for deallocating that memory if needed.

functions.name: Buffer::getSize
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes in the Buffer. Synonymous with size().

functions.name: Buffer::getBuffer
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the buffer’s data (read-only). Unlike data(), this may be nullptr when the Buffer is empty.
requirements: Callers must check for nullptr when the Buffer is empty before dereferencing.
Do not read beyond getSize() bytes.
The returned pointer becomes invalid if the Buffer is destroyed, moved (when it owns memory), or otherwise modified in ways that reallocate memory.

functions.name: Buffer::getBuffer
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the buffer’s data (writable). Unlike data(), this may be nullptr when the Buffer is empty.
requirements: Callers must check for nullptr when the Buffer is empty before dereferencing.
Do not read or write beyond getSize() bytes.
If the Buffer references external memory, writes modify the external storage; ensure such writes are safe.
The returned pointer becomes invalid if the Buffer is destroyed, moved (when it owns memory), or otherwise modified in ways that reallocate memory.

functions.name: Buffer::copy
functions.description: Creates and returns a new Buffer that owns an independent copy of this Buffer’s data.
requirements: Sufficient memory must be available to allocate a copy of the data.

functions.name: Buffer::move

functions.name: Buffer::view

functions.name: Buffer::data
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the buffer’s data (writable). Unlike getBuffer(), this is guaranteed to be a valid (non-null) pointer even when the Buffer is empty.
requirements: Even when non-null for empty buffers, callers must not read or write beyond size() bytes.
If the Buffer references external memory, writes modify the external storage; ensure such writes are safe.
The returned pointer becomes invalid if the Buffer is destroyed, moved (when it owns memory), or otherwise modified in ways that reallocate memory.

functions.name: Buffer::empty

functions.name: Buffer::size

functions.name: InputSource::InputSource
functions.description: Default constructor for the abstract InputSource base class. Creates an instance with initial internal state (e.g., last_offset = 0). Usually constructed only by derived classes.

functions.name: InputSource::~InputSource

functions.name: InputSource::Finder::Finder
functions.description: Default constructor for the nested abstract Finder helper used by findFirst/findLast to test candidate matches.

functions.name: InputSource::Finder::~Finder
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the nested Finder interface. Allows safe destruction via base pointer.

functions.name: InputSource::Finder::check
functions.description: Pure virtual predicate invoked by findFirst/findLast when the input is positioned at the start of a candidate sequence. Should examine the source starting at that position and return true if a desired pattern is found. If it returns true, the caller (findFirst/findLast) will leave the input positioned wherever check() left it at the end of the matching pattern.
requirements: Must be overridden by concrete Finder implementations.
When returning true, it should leave the InputSource positioned at the end of the matched pattern (per the class comment).
May read from the current position as needed; exact reading limits are not specified in this header.

functions.name: InputSource::setLastOffset

requirements: Argument must be a valid qpdf_offset_t value; no range is specified in this header.

functions.name: InputSource::getLastOffset
functions.description: Returns the internally stored last_offset value previously set via setLastOffset or initialized by the implementation.

functions.name: InputSource::readLine
functions.description: Reads and returns a single line from the input source up to a maximum length. Exact line-termination handling is not described here; typical behavior would stop at end-of-line or when max_line_length is reached.

functions.name: InputSource::findFirst
functions.signature: bool InputSource::findFirst(char const* start_chars, qpdf_offset_t offset, size_t len, InputSource::Finder& finder)
functions.description: Searches forward for the first occurrence of a sequence beginning with any of the characters in start_chars, within the range [offset, offset+len) (or until EOF if len == 0). For each candidate start, positions the input there and invokes finder.check(). If check() returns true for a candidate, returns true and leaves the input positioned wherever check() left it at the end of the matching pattern; otherwise continues searching. Returns false if no qualifying pattern is found.
requirements: start_chars must point to a valid, null-terminated C-string of starting characters; the header implies a character set but does not explicitly state null-termination.
offset specifies the starting search position; no explicit constraints are documented.
If len is 0, the search proceeds until EOF; otherwise the search is limited to len bytes from offset.
finder must be a valid object whose check() can be called with the input positioned at a candidate start and may advance the input as needed.
finder.check() should position the input at the end of the matching pattern when it returns true, as the caller will preserve that position.

functions.name: InputSource::findLast
functions.signature: bool InputSource::findLast(char const* start_chars, qpdf_offset_t offset, size_t len, InputSource::Finder& finder)
functions.description: Searches within the specified range for the last qualifying occurrence of a sequence that begins with any character from start_chars such that finder.check() returns true when invoked at that position. If found, returns true and leaves the input positioned wherever check() left it at the end of the matching pattern. If len is 0, the search extends until EOF.
requirements: start_chars must point to a valid set of starting characters (conventionally a null-terminated C-string).
offset is the start of the search range; no additional constraints are specified.
If len is 0, search until EOF; otherwise search within [offset, offset+len).
finder must implement check() and tolerate being called at candidate positions, advancing the input as needed.
When check() returns true, it should have left the input positioned at the end of the match.

functions.name: InputSource::findAndSkipNextEOL
functions.description: Pure virtual function expected to locate the next end-of-line from the current position and advance past it, returning an offset. Exact EOL rules (LF/CRLF/CR) and return semantics are not documented here.
requirements: Must be implemented by derived InputSource classes.
Behavior regarding what offset is returned (e.g., position after EOL or position of EOL) is not specified in this header and should be consulted in the implementation.

functions.name: InputSource::getName
functions.description: Pure virtual accessor that returns a human-readable name/identifier for the input source (e.g., filename, descriptor label). Returned reference must remain valid for the lifetime of the InputSource instance.
requirements: Must be implemented by derived classes to return a stable reference valid as long as the InputSource object exists.

functions.name: InputSource::tell

requirements: Must be implemented by derived classes. The meaning of the returned offset must be consistent with seek().

functions.name: InputSource::seek

offset semantics must align with tell() and unreadCh() (the latter notes that seek(-1, SEEK_CUR) is equivalent to unread a single character).

functions.name: InputSource::rewind
functions.description: Pure virtual function to reset the current position to the beginning of the input source.

functions.name: InputSource::read

functions.name: InputSource::read

count specifies the maximum bytes to read; behavior for very large counts depends on implementation.
If at is not -1, it indicates a position to read from; precise semantics are not documented here.

functions.name: InputSource::read
functions.signature: inline std::string InputSource::read(size_t count, qpdf_offset_t at = -1)
functions.description: Inline overload that returns a string containing up to count bytes read from the source, optionally starting at absolute position 'at' if at != -1; otherwise reads from the current position.
requirements: count specifies the maximum number of bytes to read.
If at is not -1, it requests reading starting at that position; exact seeking side effects are not specified in this header.

functions.name: InputSource::unreadCh
functions.description: Pure virtual function to unread a single character. Intended only to unread the most recently read character; semantically equivalent to seek(-1, SEEK_CUR) but potentially much more efficient. Some implementations ignore the ch value and the implementation does not enforce correct usage.
requirements: May only be used to unread the character that was just read (as per the note in the header).

Equivalent to seek(-1, SEEK_CUR) but preferred for efficiency.

functions.name: InputSource::read_line

count limits the number of bytes read for the line; exact handling of EOL and truncation is unspecified.
If at is not -1, reading starts at that position.

functions.name: InputSource::read_line
functions.description: Reads and returns a line as a string, up to count bytes, optionally starting at absolute position 'at' if provided. EOL handling specifics are not documented in this header.
requirements: count limits the number of bytes to read.
If at is not -1, reading starts at that position.

functions.name: InputSource::fastTell

Caller must pass a boolean flag as required by the internal buffering protocol; exact meaning is unspecified in this header.
