requirements: Only type and value are considered; callers must not rely on raw_value or error_message for equality semantics.
Comparison involving a token with type tt_bad will return false unless both the early check and equality semantics change in future; treat tt_bad as not equal for program logic.

functions.name: QPDFTokenizer::Token::isInteger
functions.description: Convenience check for whether the token's type is tt_integer.
requirements: None beyond a valid Token instance.

functions.name: QPDFTokenizer::Token::isWord
functions.description: Checks whether the token's type is tt_word.
requirements: None beyond a valid Token instance.

functions.name: QPDFTokenizer::QPDFTokenizer
functions.description: Constructs a tokenizer instance. Supports both push and pull tokenization modes, configurable via allowEOF() and includeIgnorable().
requirements: No additional preconditions.
Configure behavior (allowEOF/includeIgnorable) before tokenization as needed.

functions.name: QPDFTokenizer::~QPDFTokenizer
functions.description: Destructor for the tokenizer; releases internal resources.
requirements: Do not use the tokenizer after destruction.
Ensure no further presentCharacter/presentEOF/readToken calls occur post-destruction.

functions.name: QPDFTokenizer::allowEOF
functions.description: Enables EOF to be returned as a distinct tt_eof token instead of being treated as an error. Useful when tokenizing content streams.
requirements: Call before encountering EOF to ensure EOF is reported as tt_eof.
Call from the same tokenizer instance whose tokens you plan to read.

functions.name: QPDFTokenizer::includeIgnorable
functions.description: Configures the tokenizer to return ignorable tokens for whitespace and comments (tt_space and tt_comment).
requirements: Call before tokenization if you need to receive tt_space/tt_comment tokens; otherwise such tokens may be skipped.
Behavior referenced applies to readToken and push-mode tokens per documentation.

functions.name: QPDFTokenizer::presentCharacter
functions.description: Push-mode API: present a single input character to the tokenizer. Use with presentEOF() and getToken() to stream tokens from an incoming character pipeline.
requirements: Only call when a token is not currently available; calling when a token is available will throw an exception.
Feed the complete byte stream in order; do not skip characters.
Use getToken() repeatedly to extract tokens; coordinate unread handling as indicated by getToken().

functions.name: QPDFTokenizer::presentEOF
functions.description: Push-mode API: signal end-of-input to the tokenizer after all characters have been presented via presentCharacter().
requirements: Only call when a token is not currently available; calling when a token is available will throw an exception.
Must be called exactly once at end-of-input for push mode to complete the stream.
If allowEOF() was enabled, downstream may observe tt_eof; otherwise EOF without complete token may be considered an error.

functions.name: QPDFTokenizer::getToken
functions.signature: bool QPDFTokenizer::getToken(QPDFTokenizer::Token& token, bool& unread_char, char& ch)
functions.description: Push-mode API: attempts to retrieve the next token. Returns true when a complete token has been formed, providing the token and, if unread_char is true, the character that must be unread/pushed back to the upstream source.
requirements: Call repeatedly after feeding input via presentCharacter()/presentEOF() until it returns true for each token.
When the function returns true, check unread_char; if true, the caller must unread/push back the character ch to the upstream input source.
Do not call presentCharacter() or presentEOF() while a token is available; doing so will throw an exception.
token, unread_char, and ch must be valid lvalue references.

functions.name: QPDFTokenizer::betweenTokens
functions.description: Deprecated push-mode helper: indicates whether the current character is between tokens (whitespace not part of a string) or within a comment, allowing filters to decide whether to output the character.
requirements: Function is deprecated; prefer updated APIs per the cited release notes.
May be used by tokenizing filters only in push mode; semantics rely on the tokenizer’s current state.

functions.name: QPDFTokenizer::readToken
functions.signature: QPDFTokenizer::Token QPDFTokenizer::readToken(InputSource& input, std::string const& context, bool allow_bad = false, size_t max_len = 0)
functions.description: Pull-mode API: reads and returns the next token from the given InputSource. The context string is used to annotate exceptions. On success, input.tell() is positioned just after the token and input.getLastOffset() points to the token's start. If allow_bad is true, tokenization anomalies may be returned as tt_bad tokens instead of throwing. If max_len is nonzero, token length may be limited.
requirements: input must reference a valid, readable InputSource positioned at the start of a token or inter-token whitespace.
context should describe the reading context; it will appear in any thrown exceptions.
If tt_inline_image tokens are desired, expectInlineImage() must have been called just prior (after reading the character following ID).
If includeIgnorable() has been called, tt_space and tt_comment tokens may be returned; callers should handle them if needed.
If allowEOF() was enabled, EOF may be returned as tt_eof instead of error.
Callers should be prepared to receive tt_bad when allow_bad is true and inspect token.getErrorMessage() for details.

functions.name: QPDFTokenizer::readToken
functions.signature: QPDFTokenizer::Token QPDFTokenizer::readToken(std::shared_ptr<InputSource> input, std::string const& context, bool allow_bad = false, size_t max_len = 0)
functions.description: Pull-mode API overload: reads the next token from a shared InputSource, with the same behavior and postconditions as the reference overload.
requirements: input must be a non-null shared_ptr to a valid, readable InputSource positioned at the start of a token or inter-token whitespace.
context should describe the reading context; it will appear in any thrown exceptions.
If tt_inline_image tokens are desired, expectInlineImage() must have been called just prior (after reading the character following ID).
If includeIgnorable() has been called, tt_space and tt_comment tokens may be returned; callers should handle them if needed.
If allowEOF() was enabled, EOF may be returned as tt_eof instead of error.
When non-null, upon return input->tell() points just after the token and input->getLastOffset() points to the token start.
Callers should be prepared to receive tt_bad when allow_bad is true and inspect token.getErrorMessage() for details.

functions.name: QPDFTokenizer::expectInlineImage
functions.description: Signals the tokenizer that an inline image is expected on the provided InputSource. After this call, the next readToken will return a tt_inline_image token (containing all data up to but not including the next EI) or tt_bad on error. This is the only way readToken returns tt_inline_image.
requirements: Call after reading the character following the ID operator in a content stream.
input must be a non-null shared_ptr to the same InputSource that will be used with subsequent readToken calls.
Do not call from push mode; this is for pull-mode operation with InputSource.
After calling, the very next readToken should be consumed and handled as inline image data or error.

functions.name: QPDFTokenizer::expectInlineImage
functions.description: Signals the tokenizer that an inline image is expected on the provided InputSource (reference overload). Subsequent readToken will return tt_inline_image (data up to but not including the next EI) or tt_bad. This is the only way readToken returns tt_inline_image.
requirements: Call after reading the character following the ID operator in a content stream.
input must be the same InputSource instance that will be passed to the next readToken call.
Do not call from push mode; this is for pull-mode operation with InputSource.
After calling, the very next readToken should be consumed and handled as inline image data or error.

functions.description: Stream insertion operator that writes the QPDFObjGen as "obj,gen" using a comma separator to the provided output stream. Useful for logging and debugging.

og is passed by value; no additional constraints documented.

functions.name: QPDFObjGen::set::add
functions.description: Adds og to the set if it is indirect (og.isIndirect() == true) and not already present. Returns false if og was already present; returns true otherwise. Attempts to insert QPDFObjGen(0, 0) are ignored but the function returns true.
requirements: If og.isIndirect() is true and og is already in the set, the function returns false and does not modify the set.
If og.isIndirect() is true and og is not in the set, the function inserts og and returns true.
If og.isIndirect() is false (e.g., og == QPDFObjGen(0, 0)), the function performs no insertion and returns true.

functions.name: QPDFXRefEntry::QPDFXRefEntry
functions.description: Default constructor. Creates a type 0 (free) cross-reference entry as defined by the PDF spec. Useful for initializing or representing unused/free xref slots.
requirements: Constructs an entry of type 0 (free). No fields need to be provided.
No explicit postconditions or error handling are documented.

functions.name: QPDFXRefEntry::QPDFXRefEntry
functions.signature: QPDFXRefEntry(int type, qpdf_offset_t field1, int field2);
functions.description: General constructor for a cross-reference (xref) entry. The type must be one of the PDF cross-reference stream types: 0 (free), 1 (uncompressed object), or 2 (compressed object). The meaning of field1 and field2 depends on type: for type 1, field1 is the byte offset of the object; for type 2, field1 is the object stream number and field2 is the index within that object stream. For type 0, the entry is free and the fields are not used.
requirements: type must be 0, 1, or 2 per the PDF spec comment in this header.
If type == 1 (uncompressed), field1 must represent the object’s file offset (qpdf_offset_t).
If type == 2 (compressed), field1 must be the object stream number and field2 must be the index within that object stream.
If type == 0 (free), field values are not used by consumers.
No documented validation or error signaling on bad inputs; caller must ensure consistency between type and fields.

functions.name: QPDFXRefEntry::QPDFXRefEntry
functions.description: Convenience constructor for a type 1 (uncompressed) xref entry, where the entry directly stores the byte offset of the object in the file.
requirements: offset is interpreted as the object’s byte offset for an uncompressed object (type 1).
Results in an entry with getType() == 1.
No documented range checking or error handling; caller must ensure the offset is appropriate for the underlying file.

functions.name: QPDFXRefEntry::QPDFXRefEntry
functions.description: Convenience constructor for a type 2 (compressed) xref entry, identifying an object stored inside an object stream by its stream number and index within that stream.
requirements: stream_number is interpreted as the object stream number; index is the index of the object within that stream.
Results in an entry with getType() == 2.
No documented range checking or error handling; caller must ensure stream_number and index are valid for the target PDF.

functions.name: QPDFXRefEntry::getType
functions.description: Returns the xref entry type: 0 (free), 1 (uncompressed with offset), or 2 (compressed in an object stream). Use this to determine how to interpret the other fields.
requirements: None beyond having a properly constructed QPDFXRefEntry instance.

functions.name: QPDFXRefEntry::getOffset
functions.description: Returns the byte offset of an uncompressed (type 1) object. Only valid for entries with type 1.
requirements: Must only be called when getType() == 1; otherwise the value is not meaningful and behavior is unspecified by this header.
Caller is responsible for handling entries of other types appropriately before calling.

functions.name: QPDFXRefEntry::getObjStreamNumber
functions.description: For compressed (type 2) entries, returns the object stream number that contains the object. Only valid for type 2 entries.
requirements: Must only be called when getType() == 2; otherwise the value is not meaningful and behavior is unspecified by this header.

functions.name: QPDFXRefEntry::getObjStreamIndex
functions.description: For compressed (type 2) entries, returns the index of the object within its object stream. Only valid for type 2 entries.
requirements: Must only be called when getType() == 2; otherwise the value is not meaningful and behavior is unspecified by this header.

functions.name: QPDFSystemError::QPDFSystemError
functions.description: Constructs a QPDFSystemError exception describing a system-level error. Typical usage is to throw this exception with a human-readable description and the errno value captured at the time of failure. The exception’s what() message (from std::runtime_error) combines the description and the system error. Details of the formatting are internal.
requirements: description may be any valid string; it is copied internally, so the argument does not need to outlive the constructor call.
system_errno may be any int; typically this is the value of errno at the time of the error (exact expected range/values are not specified).
May be constructed and thrown like any std::runtime_error; no additional preconditions are documented.
Thread-safety or reentrancy guarantees are not specified (unknown).

functions.name: QPDFSystemError::getDescription
functions.description: Returns the original human-readable description that was supplied when the QPDFSystemError was constructed. Use this to retrieve the caller-provided text without the formatted system error message. For a full combined message, call what().
requirements: Must be called on a valid QPDFSystemError instance (e.g., inside a catch block or while the object is alive).
The returned reference remains valid only for the lifetime of the exception object; do not use it after the exception is destroyed.
No side effects or additional preconditions are documented.

functions.name: QPDFSystemError::getErrno
functions.description: Returns the system errno value that was supplied when the QPDFSystemError was constructed. This enables callers to inspect or branch on the underlying system error code directly.
requirements: Must be called on a valid QPDFSystemError instance (e.g., inside a catch block or while the object is alive).
Returned value is exactly the stored int; no range or semantic guarantees beyond what was passed to the constructor are documented.

functions.name: QPDFStreamFilter::QPDFStreamFilter
functions.description: Default constructor for the abstract QPDFStreamFilter base class. Intended to be subclassed to implement custom PDF stream decoding filters. The base type enforces that derived classes at least implement getDecodePipeline() and typically override setDecodeParms() as needed.
requirements: This class is abstract; do not attempt to instantiate for use unless a concrete subclass implements getDecodePipeline().
Copy construction and copy assignment are deleted for this type; callers must not attempt to copy instances (store and pass by pointer/reference instead).
Callers should follow the contract that setDecodeParms() will be called before getDecodePipeline() when using instances through the QPDF API.

functions.name: QPDFStreamFilter::~QPDFStreamFilter
functions.description: Virtual destructor for QPDFStreamFilter. Ensures proper cleanup of resources in derived filters. Implementations are expected to manage the lifetime of any Pipeline they create so that the pipeline is deleted when the filter instance is destroyed.
requirements: Do not use any Pipeline previously returned by getDecodePipeline() after the filter instance is destroyed (avoid use‑after‑free).
Callers should not delete the Pipeline returned by getDecodePipeline() if ownership is with the filter (per the contract, the filter implementation must delete it on destruction).
Ensure destruction order does not leave dangling references to the filter‑owned Pipeline in other components.

functions.name: QPDFStreamFilter::setDecodeParms
functions.description: Supplies the /DecodeParms for this filter prior to pipeline creation. Returns true if the filter can proceed with the given parameters. The default implementation only accepts a null object and rejects all other values. Typical usage is to call this exactly once before calling getDecodePipeline(), storing any needed state from decode_parms for pipeline construction.
requirements: Must be called before getDecodePipeline().
Callers must check the boolean return value and proceed to getDecodePipeline() only if true.
decode_parms may be a null object; the default implementation accepts null and rejects non‑null.
decode_parms should represent the PDF stream’s /DecodeParms (e.g., a dictionary or array) when non‑null; specific structure requirements are filter‑specific and not defined here.
If a subclass overrides this method, callers must still honor its return value semantics (true means acceptable, false means unusable with the provided parameters).

functions.name: QPDFStreamFilter::getDecodePipeline
functions.description: Creates and returns a Pipeline that decodes data for this filter, chaining to the provided downstream pipeline ‘next’. Implementations must ensure the returned Pipeline is deleted when the filter instance is destroyed. QPDF guarantees it will call setDecodeParms() before this method.
requirements: Must only be called after setDecodeParms() has been called and returned true.
The returned Pipeline’s lifetime must be managed by the filter implementation; callers should not delete it unless explicitly documented by a specific implementation.
The next parameter must be a valid downstream Pipeline pointer suitable for chaining; whether null is permitted is not specified in this header (unknown).
Callers must not assume thread‑safety or reentrancy; such properties are not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: QPDFStreamFilter::isSpecializedCompression
functions.description: Indicates whether the filter uses specialized (non‑lossy) compression intended for specific data types rather than general‑purpose data. The default implementation returns false; override in derived classes if applicable. QPDFWriter may avoid re‑encoding streams using specialized compression.
requirements: No specific input requirements; pure query method.
Return value semantics: true means specialized compression; false otherwise.

functions.name: QPDFStreamFilter::isLossyCompression
functions.description: Indicates whether the filter uses lossy compression. The default implementation returns false; override in derived classes if the filter is lossy. QPDFWriter may handle lossy streams differently (e.g., avoid decode/re‑encode).
requirements: No specific input requirements; pure query method.
Return value semantics: true means lossy compression; false otherwise.

functions.name: Pl_Buffer::Pl_Buffer
functions.signature: Pl_Buffer(char const* identifier, Pipeline* next = nullptr);
functions.description: Constructs a buffering pipeline that accumulates written data in memory. Optionally forwards all data to a downstream Pipeline ("next") if provided. The identifier is typically used by the Pipeline base class for diagnostics/logging. When used, you usually write() data, call finish(), then retrieve the accumulated data via one of the get* methods, after which the buffer is reset for reuse.
requirements: next may be null; if provided, this pipeline will also pass the data through to it (explicit).
If a next Pipeline* is provided, it must be valid and able to accept write() and finish() calls for the lifetime of this Pl_Buffer instance (inferred from typical Pipeline patterns).
identifier should be a valid, null-terminated string; whether nullptr is allowed is unknown (not stated).

functions.name: Pl_Buffer::~Pl_Buffer
functions.description: Destructor for the buffering pipeline. Cleans up resources associated with the pipeline and its internal buffer state. Does not delete any externally provided next pipeline.
requirements: No specific caller requirements are documented.
If a next pipeline was provided, its lifetime remains the caller’s responsibility (inferred).

functions.name: Pl_Buffer::write
functions.signature: void write(unsigned char const*, size_t) override;
functions.description: Appends the provided bytes to the internal buffer. If a next pipeline was provided at construction, the same data is also forwarded to that pipeline. Typically called zero or more times before finish().
requirements: If size > 0, the data pointer must reference at least size readable bytes (inferred from signature).
It is valid to call with size == 0; behavior with a null pointer when size == 0 is unspecified (unknown).
May be called multiple times prior to finish(); do not call getBuffer()/getBufferSharedPointer()/getMallocBuffer()/getString() until after finish() (see get* requirements).

functions.name: Pl_Buffer::finish
functions.description: Signals the end of input for the current accumulation cycle. After calling finish(), you may retrieve the accumulated data via one of the get* methods. The internal buffer is reset by the subsequent get* call, allowing reuse for a new cycle of write()/finish()/get*.
requirements: Must be called before calling getBuffer(), getBufferSharedPointer(), getMallocBuffer(), or getString() (explicit via get* docs).
Should be called after the last write() in the current cycle (inferred).

functions.name: Pl_Buffer::getBuffer
functions.description: Returns the accumulated data as a newly allocated Buffer object and resets the internal buffer. Ownership of the returned Buffer is transferred to the caller, who must delete it. Usage: write()...; finish(); Buffer* b = getBuffer(); ...; delete b; After this call, the pipeline is reset and may be reused for new writes.
requirements: May be called only after calling finish() and before any subsequent write() (explicit).
Each call resets this object’s internal buffer (explicit).
The caller is responsible for deleting the returned Buffer (explicit).
Whether the return can be nullptr is unknown (not stated).

functions.name: Pl_Buffer::getBufferSharedPointer
functions.description: Same as getBuffer() but returns the result wrapped in a std::shared_ptr for automatic lifetime management. Calling this resets the internal buffer just like getBuffer().
requirements: Same timing requirement as getBuffer(): call only after finish() and before any subsequent write() (explicit via "Same as getBuffer").
Each call resets this object’s internal buffer (inherited from getBuffer).
No manual delete is required; manage via the returned shared_ptr (inferred).

functions.name: Pl_Buffer::getMallocBuffer
functions.signature: void getMallocBuffer(unsigned char** buf, size_t* len);
functions.description: Provides the accumulated data via a malloc-allocated buffer suitable for foreign-language interfaces. If there is no data, *buf is set to nullptr and *len to 0; otherwise, *buf points to a malloc()’d buffer of size *len. The internal buffer is reset after this call.
requirements: Call only after finish() and before any subsequent write() (same timing as getBuffer) (explicit).
On success, if there is data, the caller must call free() on *buf (explicit).
If there is no data, *buf is set to null and *len to 0 (explicit).
buf and len must be non-null output pointers writable by the function (inferred from signature).
Each call resets this object’s internal buffer (inherited from getBuffer behavior).

functions.name: Pl_Buffer::getString
functions.description: Same as getBuffer() but returns the accumulated data as a std::string. After returning the string, the internal buffer is reset, allowing reuse.
requirements: Call only after finish() and before any subsequent write() (explicit via "Same as getBuffer").
Each call resets this object’s internal buffer (inherited from getBuffer behavior).

functions.name: Pl_Concatenate::Pl_Concatenate
functions.description: Constructs a concatenating pipeline stage that suppresses regular finish() propagation to the downstream pipeline. Use this when feeding multiple upstream streams into a downstream stage that cannot accept multiple finish() calls; call manualFinish() once at the very end to actually finish the downstream chain.
requirements: identifier is a C string used for identification/logging; content requirements are unknown.
next should point to the next Pipeline in the chain if downstream forwarding is desired; whether null is allowed is unknown.
The constructed object must outlive any writes routed through it.

functions.name: Pl_Concatenate::~Pl_Concatenate
functions.description: Destructor for the concatenating pipeline. It cleans up internal resources. It does not substitute for manualFinish(); callers should ensure manualFinish() has been called if downstream finalization is required before destruction.
requirements: Do not use the object after destruction.
If downstream completion is required, ensure manualFinish() was called before destruction (finish() is intentionally suppressed).

functions.name: Pl_Concatenate::write
functions.signature: void Pl_Concatenate::write(unsigned char const* data, size_t len)
functions.description: Writes len bytes from data to this pipeline stage, forwarding the bytes to the downstream pipeline without altering finish semantics. Intended for streaming multiple inputs before a single finalization via manualFinish().
requirements: If len > 0, data must point to a valid buffer containing at least len bytes.
The pipeline must be properly constructed and not yet destroyed when write is called.
May be called multiple times; ordering is preserved.

functions.name: Pl_Concatenate::finish
functions.description: Overrides Pipeline::finish() to drop/suppress the finish signal instead of passing it to the downstream pipeline. Use manualFinish() to actually finalize the downstream chain.
requirements: Callers should not rely on finish() to flush or close the downstream pipeline when using Pl_Concatenate.
Use manualFinish() at the very end to finish downstream processing.

functions.name: Pl_Concatenate::manualFinish
functions.description: Explicitly finishes the remainder of the pipeline by forwarding the finish signal downstream. Use this once after all upstream streams have been written and any suppressed finish() calls have occurred.
requirements: Call exactly once at the very end, after all data has been written and any upstream components have issued their (suppressed) finish() calls.
Do not call after the object has been destroyed.
Do not interleave manualFinish() with further write() calls; additional writes after manualFinish() are not supported (behavior unspecified).

functions.name: Pl_Count::Pl_Count
functions.description: Constructs a Pl_Count pipeline stage that counts the number of bytes written through it and tracks the last byte written, while forwarding data to the next Pipeline in the chain. The identifier is typically used by the Pipeline framework for diagnostics or tracing. Usage: create this as a stage in a Pipeline chain and feed data via write(), then optionally call finish(). This pipeline is reusable; it is safe to call write() after finish(). Notes: ownership/lifetime rules for next and valid values for identifier are not documented here.
requirements: identifier: unknown constraints (not documented); typically a null-terminated C string used for identification/logging
next: unknown constraints (not documented); intended to be the downstream Pipeline to receive forwarded data
The constructed object must outlive any subsequent calls to its member functions (inferred from standard C++ object lifetime)

functions.name: Pl_Count::~Pl_Count
functions.description: Destructor for the Pl_Count pipeline stage. Cleans up internal resources. Usage: allow automatic destruction when the object goes out of scope, or delete it when allocated dynamically.
requirements: Must not call member functions (e.g., write, finish, getCount, getLastChar) after destruction (standard C++ object lifetime requirement)
Thread-safety of destruction is unknown; do not destroy concurrently with active calls to other methods (inferred best practice)

functions.name: Pl_Count::write
functions.signature: void Pl_Count::write(unsigned char const* data, size_t len)
functions.description: Feeds data into the Pl_Count stage. The call forwards the bytes to the next pipeline stage and updates the internal byte count and the last byte written. Usage: call repeatedly with buffers of data. This pipeline is reusable; it is safe to call write() after a prior call to finish().
requirements: If len > 0, data must point to a valid buffer of at least len bytes (inferred from typical write(buffer,len) semantics)
If len == 0, data may be null or non-null; no bytes are read (inferred)
Do not call on a destroyed object (standard C++ object lifetime requirement)
Thread safety is not specified; do not call concurrently from multiple threads unless externally synchronized (inferred)

functions.name: Pl_Count::finish
functions.description: Signals end-of-data to the pipeline and forwards the finish to the next stage. This pipeline is reusable; it is safe to call write() after calling finish(). Usage: call when no more data will be written in the current stream/phase.
requirements: May be called even if no data has been written (typical pipeline finish behavior; not explicitly documented)
It is safe to call write() after finish(); behavior regarding multiple consecutive finish() calls is not documented (unknown)
Do not call on a destroyed object (standard C++ object lifetime requirement)
Thread safety is not specified; avoid concurrent calls without external synchronization (inferred)

functions.name: Pl_Count::getCount
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes written through this Pl_Count instance. Usage: query after one or more write() calls or after finish() to obtain the total bytes observed so far. Note: The header does not specify whether finish() resets the count; given that the pipeline is reusable, whether the count is cumulative across reuse cycles is unknown.
requirements: Callable at any time after construction; returns 0 if no bytes have been written (implied by getLastChar() comment)
Thread safety is not specified; avoid calling concurrently with write()/finish() without external synchronization (inferred)

functions.name: Pl_Count::getLastChar
functions.description: Returns the last byte value written via write(). If no bytes have been written, returns '\0' (and in that case getCount() returns 0). Usage: call to inspect the most recently written byte.
requirements: If no data has been written, the function returns '\0' and getCount() is 0 (explicit)
Callable at any time after construction; behavior during concurrent writes is not specified (unknown)
Thread safety is not specified; avoid calling concurrently with write()/finish() without external synchronization (inferred)

functions.name: Pl_DCT::Pl_DCT
functions.description: Constructor for setting up a DCT (JPEG) decompression pipeline stage. Use this when you want Pl_DCT to decode incoming JPEG-compressed image bytes and forward decompressed data to the next Pipeline.
requirements: Applies to decompression use only (per comment).
Parameter identifier is expected to be a stable C string used to identify this pipeline stage (exact semantics not documented).
Parameter next must refer to a valid Pipeline instance that will receive decompressed output (inferred from Pipeline chaining pattern).
Must be followed by zero or more calls to write() and then a single call to finish() to complete processing (inferred from Pipeline interface semantics).

functions.name: Pl_DCT::Pl_DCT
functions.signature: Pl_DCT::Pl_DCT(char const* identifier, Pipeline* next, JDIMENSION image_width, JDIMENSION image_height, int components, J_COLOR_SPACE color_space, CompressConfig* config_callback = nullptr)
functions.description: Constructor for setting up a DCT (JPEG) compression pipeline stage. Use this to encode raw image data into JPEG, writing compressed bytes to the next Pipeline. Accepts image dimensions, component count, color space, and an optional configuration callback.

Parameter identifier is expected to be a stable C string used to identify this pipeline stage (exact semantics not documented).

components should match the number of components for the specified color_space (e.g., 1 for grayscale, 3 for RGB/YCbCr) (inferred from libjpeg conventions).
color_space must be a valid J_COLOR_SPACE value supported by libjpeg (inferred).
If provided, config_callback must remain valid for the duration of initialization where it is applied; ownership/lifetime semantics are not documented (unknown specifics).
Must be followed by zero or more calls to write() with raw pixel data in the expected format, then a single call to finish() to complete compression (inferred).

functions.name: Pl_DCT::setMemoryLimit
functions.description: Globally limit the memory used by jpeglib when decompressing data. Affects all Pl_DCT instances (static option). Call before or during use to constrain decompressor memory usage.

Intended to affect decompression paths only (explicit).

functions.description: Globally limit the number of scans used by jpeglib when decompressing progressive JPEGs. Affects all Pl_DCT instances (static option).
requirements: This limit applies process-wide to all Pl_DCT instances (explicit).
Only affects decompression of progressive JPEG images (explicit).
Behavior for non-positive limits is not documented; callers should pass a positive integer (inferred).
May be set prior to decompression to ensure the limit is honored for all subsequent operations (inferred).

functions.name: Pl_DCT::setThrowOnCorruptData
functions.description: Controls how corrupt JPEG data is handled during decompression. When true (default in qpdf), corrupt data is treated as a runtime error; when false, the decompressor may attempt to recover and continue. Affects all Pl_DCT instances (static option).
requirements: This setting applies process-wide to all Pl_DCT instances (explicit).
Only affects decompression behavior (explicit).
Set prior to starting decompression to uniformly control error handling (inferred).

functions.name: Pl_DCT::CompressConfig::CompressConfig
functions.description: Default constructor for a compression-configuration callback object used to configure a jpeg_compress_struct before compression. Intended to be subclassed or created via make_compress_config.

functions.name: Pl_DCT::CompressConfig::~CompressConfig
functions.description: Virtual destructor for CompressConfig to allow safe deletion through base pointers.
requirements: Objects derived from CompressConfig must ensure any resources acquired for configuration are released in the destructor (inferred).

functions.name: Pl_DCT::CompressConfig::apply
functions.description: Pure-virtual hook to apply caller-defined configuration to a jpeg_compress_struct prior to starting compression. Implementations should set fields such as quality, sampling, or Huffman tables as needed.
requirements: cinfo points to a valid, initialized jpeg_compress_struct provided by Pl_DCT prior to starting compression (inferred from type and purpose).
Implementations must not destroy or outlive the provided cinfo; only configure it (inferred).

functions.name: Pl_DCT::make_compress_config
functions.description: Factory that wraps a std::function callback into a CompressConfig implementation. The callback is invoked with a jpeg_compress_struct* so the caller can set compression parameters without defining a subclass.
requirements: The provided function must be callable with a non-null jpeg_compress_struct* and should only configure fields (inferred).
The function should be safe to invoke during Pl_DCT construction or initialization of compression (inferred).

functions.name: Pl_DCT::~Pl_DCT
functions.description: Destructor for the Pl_DCT pipeline stage. Ensures any compressor/decompressor state is cleaned up and underlying resources are released.
requirements: Call finish() before destruction to flush and finalize processing (inferred from Pipeline semantics).

functions.name: Pl_DCT::write
functions.signature: void Pl_DCT::write(unsigned char const* data, size_t len) override
functions.description: Feeds a chunk of data into the Pl_DCT stage. In decompression mode, data should be JPEG-compressed bytes; in compression mode, data should be raw image samples matching the constructor-specified format. Output is forwarded to the next Pipeline stage.
requirements: The Pl_DCT instance must have been constructed for the intended mode (compression or decompression) (explicit via constructors).
data must point to a buffer of at least len bytes; interpretation depends on mode (inferred).
May be called zero or more times before a final call to finish() (inferred).
Do not call after finish() (inferred).

functions.name: Pl_DCT::finish
functions.description: Signals end of input to the Pl_DCT stage. Flushes any buffered data and finalizes compression or decompression, forwarding any remaining output to the next Pipeline.
requirements: Must be called exactly once after the last write() to complete processing (inferred).
After finish(), no further calls to write() should be made (inferred).

functions.name: Pl_Discard::Pl_Discard
functions.description: Constructs a Pl_Discard pipeline, an end-of-line Pipeline that discards all data written to it. Intended for cases where output should be ignored while still exercising pipeline semantics. Reusable component per comments.
requirements: No constructor arguments required.
No downstream/next pipeline is attached; this is an end-of-line pipeline (per comment).
Callers should not expect any produced output; all input is discarded.

functions.name: Pl_Discard::~Pl_Discard
functions.description: Destroys the Pl_Discard pipeline. As an end-of-line sink, destruction releases any resources associated with the pipeline (none are observable to callers).
requirements: The object must not be used after destruction (usual C++ object lifetime rules).

functions.name: Pl_Discard::write
functions.signature: void Pl_Discard::write(unsigned char const* data, size_t len);
functions.description: Writes a buffer into the discard pipeline. The data is intentionally ignored; this stage produces no output and has no next pipeline. The pipeline is reusable; per comment it is safe to call write() after finish(). Use to consume data without propagating it.
requirements: This pipeline discards all written data; callers must not rely on any output or side effects.
It is safe to call write() after a prior call to finish() (per comment).
Pointer validity: inferred from common C/C++ conventions—if len > 0, data should point to at least len readable bytes; if len == 0, data may be null.

functions.description: Signals end-of-input for the discard pipeline. As a sink with no downstream stage, this typically performs no observable action. The pipeline is reusable; per comment, write() may be called again after finish().
requirements: May be called to indicate no more data for the current write sequence.
It is safe to call write() after finish() on this pipeline (per comment).
No output or propagation occurs; callers must not expect any produced data.

functions.name: Pl_Flate::Pl_Flate

functions.description: Constructs a flate pipeline stage that either inflates (decompresses) or deflates (compresses) data passing through a Pipeline. requirements: identifier: should be a stable, null-terminated C string used for diagnostics/logging; content not specified by the API.
next: pointer to the downstream Pipeline stage; should remain valid for the entire lifetime of this Pl_Flate instance (typical for chained pipelines).
action: must be either Pl_Flate::a_inflate or Pl_Flate::a_deflate.
out_bufsize: should be a positive integer (> 0); defaults to Pl_Flate::def_bufsize (65536).
Global/static options such as memory_limit and compression level affect all instances.

functions.name: Pl_Flate::~Pl_Flate
functions.description: Destroys the Pl_Flate pipeline stage, releasing any internal resources and terminating any compression/decompression state. Intended to be used at the end of the pipeline stage’s lifetime.
requirements: Do not use the object after destruction.
Ensure finish() has been called if the application requires all buffered output to be flushed before destruction (typical for pipelines).

functions.name: Pl_Flate::memory_limit
functions.description: Returns the global memory limit applied to all Pl_Flate instances. This is a static, process-wide setting used to limit memory usage for flate operations.
requirements: Callable at any time; affects/reflects a global option shared by all Pl_Flate instances.

functions.name: Pl_Flate::memory_limit
functions.signature: static void Pl_Flate::memory_limit(unsigned long long limit)

Affects all existing and future Pl_Flate instances globally.

functions.description: Feeds a block of bytes into the flate pipeline. Depending on the configured action, the data is compressed or decompressed and forwarded to the next pipeline stage. May buffer internally until sufficient data is available or until finish() is called.
requirements: data: must be a valid pointer to at least len bytes unless len == 0; passing nullptr with len > 0 is invalid.
len: size of the input buffer; may be 0 to indicate no data.
Caller should eventually call finish() to flush and finalize compression/decompression state.

functions.description: Signals end of input, flushing any remaining internal buffers and finalizing the compression/decompression stream. Ensures all processed data is forwarded to the next pipeline stage.

functions.name: Pl_Flate::setCompressionLevel
functions.description: Globally sets the zlib compression level used for deflation across all Pl_Flate instances. Valid zlib levels are 1 (fastest, least compression) through 9 (slowest, most compression); use -1 to select zlib’s default. Note: despite an older comment suggesting a fluent instance method, this function is static and returns void in this header.
requirements: Argument must be -1 or an integer in the inclusive range [1, 9]; other values are not supported per the comment.
Setting this affects all Pl_Flate instances globally.
Only affects deflation (compression), not inflation (decompression).

functions.description: Registers a warning callback to be invoked with a message (char const*) and an error code (int) when the flate stage wants to report non-fatal issues. Useful for surfacing zlib/zopfli warnings to the application or logs.

The callable must remain valid for as long as the Pl_Flate instance may invoke it.
Behavior if the callback throws is unspecified in this header; implementations typically expect callbacks not to throw.

functions.name: Pl_Flate::zopfli_supported
functions.description: Returns true if the library was built with zopfli compression support compiled in; otherwise false.

functions.description: Returns true if zopfli is enabled at runtime. Zopfli is considered enabled when it is compiled in and the QPDF_ZOPFLI environment variable is set to a value other than "disabled."

functions.name: Pl_Flate::zopfli_check_env
functions.description: Checks whether zopfli use is acceptable based on build support and the QPDF_ZOPFLI environment variable. If zopfli support is compiled in, returns true. If not compiled in, examines QPDF_ZOPFLI: returns true for "disabled" or "silent"; throws/terminates the process for "force"; for any other value, emits a warning and returns false. If a logger is provided, warnings go there.

May throw or exit on "force" when support is not compiled in, per the comment (qpdf_exit_error/exception). Callers should be prepared to handle exceptions or process termination per library conventions.

functions.name: Pl_StdioFile::Pl_StdioFile
functions.description: Constructs a pipeline that writes its input bytes directly to a provided stdio FILE*. The FILE* is owned and managed by the caller; this class writes to it and flushes it but never closes it. The identifier is typically used for diagnostics/tracing in the qpdf pipeline framework. Use this when you want a Pipeline sink that targets an existing FILE*.
requirements: f must point to a valid, open FILE suitable for writing at the time the constructor is called and for the entire lifetime of the Pl_StdioFile instance.
The FILE* is externally maintained; the caller must not rely on this object to close it and must ensure its lifetime outlives this pipeline’s use.
identifier should be a valid, null-terminated C string; its exact semantics are unspecified (likely for diagnostics).

functions.name: Pl_StdioFile::~Pl_StdioFile
functions.description: Destructor for the pipeline. It does not close the underlying FILE*. Typically used to release internal resources associated with writing to the FILE*.
requirements: The caller remains responsible for closing the FILE* after the pipeline is no longer needed.

Any required finalization (such as calling finish()) should be performed before destruction, following the Pipeline usage pattern; exact error-handling behavior on destruction is unknown from this header.

functions.name: Pl_StdioFile::write
functions.signature: void Pl_StdioFile::write(unsigned char const* buf, size_t len)
functions.description: Writes len bytes from buf to the underlying FILE*. This is the primary data injection point for the pipeline. Can be called multiple times to stream data to the sink. The class may flush the FILE* as part of its operation; it does not close it.
requirements: buf must point to at least len bytes of readable memory when len > 0.
len may be zero; behavior for buf when len == 0 is unspecified—pass a valid pointer to be safe.
Must only be called on a properly constructed Pl_StdioFile instance whose FILE* remains valid and open for writing.
Should follow the Pipeline protocol (i.e., typically call write() zero or more times, then finish()); exact error signaling on I/O failure is unknown from this header.

functions.name: Pl_StdioFile::finish
functions.description: Signals end of input to the pipeline and flushes any buffered data to the underlying FILE*. The FILE* is not closed by this call. This pipeline is documented as reusable; after finish, it may be possible to reuse it, but specific reuse semantics are not detailed here.
requirements: Call after the last write() in a sequence to ensure all data is flushed to the FILE*.
The underlying FILE* must still be valid and open when finish() is called.
Exact rules about multiple calls to finish() or subsequent reuse are not specified; adhere to typical Pipeline usage (finish once per write sequence).

functions.name: Pl_String::Pl_String
functions.signature: Pl_String::Pl_String(char const* identifier, Pipeline* next, std::string& s)
functions.description: Constructs a pipeline that accumulates all written data into the provided std::string (appending across multiple uses) and, if a downstream pipeline is provided via next, also forwards all data to it. The identifier is typically used by the Pipeline base for diagnostics. Use this to capture data written through a pipeline chain without interfering with downstream processing or finish semantics.
requirements: next may be null (explicitly supported).
If next is non-null, it is intended that this pipeline forwards data and finish() to it.
The std::string reference s must remain valid for the entire lifetime of the Pl_String object (inferred from it being stored by reference).
identifier is an optional C string used for identification; no specific format is required (details not specified).
Thread-safety is not specified; assume calls occur from a single thread unless documented otherwise (inferred).

functions.name: Pl_String::~Pl_String
functions.description: Destructor for the string-accumulating pipeline. Cleans up internal resources. If a downstream pipeline was provided, its lifetime is not managed here unless documented elsewhere; this class primarily forwards operations to it.
requirements: No explicit caller requirements on destruction are stated.
Ensure the referenced std::string still exists until this destructor completes (inferred from constructor semantics).
If a downstream pipeline was provided, its lifetime management is the caller’s responsibility unless otherwise documented (inferred from signature; not owned pointer).

functions.name: Pl_String::write
functions.signature: void Pl_String::write(unsigned char const* buf, size_t len) override
functions.description: Appends len bytes from buf to the accumulated std::string. If a downstream pipeline (next) was provided at construction, the same data is also forwarded to it. Can be called multiple times; data is appended across calls.
requirements: buf must point to at least len readable bytes (standard buffer write contract; inferred).
If len is zero, the function performs no append; buf may be null in that case (common pattern; inferred, not explicitly stated).
May be called multiple times; order of calls determines append order (inferred).
If a downstream pipeline was provided, write will forward the data to it (explicit).
Do not call after destruction; ensure the Pl_String object is alive during the call (inferred).

functions.name: Pl_String::finish
functions.description: Signals that no more data will be written to this pipeline. If a downstream pipeline (next) was provided, this method forwards finish() to it. For this pipeline specifically, calling finish() is optional when there is no downstream pipeline, making it convenient to tap into another pipeline without affecting its finish timing.
requirements: If no downstream pipeline (next == nullptr) was provided, it is okay to omit calling finish() (explicit).
If a downstream pipeline was provided, callers should call finish() to ensure the downstream pipeline is finalized (explicit behavior; requirement inferred from forwarding semantics).
Do not call after destruction; ensure the Pl_String object is alive during the call (inferred).

functions.description: Converts the handle to a boolean, indicating whether it refers to a non-null/valid underlying QPDF object. Typical use: if (handle) { ... } to guard use of the handle. functions.description: Return the file’s base PDF version as a string (e.g., "1.7").
requirements: Requires a loaded/created PDF.

functions.name: QPDF::getExtensionLevel
functions.description: Return the PDF extension level, if any.
requirements: Requires a loaded/created PDF.

functions.name: QPDF::getTrailer
functions.description: Return the trailer dictionary object handle for the current PDF.
requirements: Requires a loaded/created PDF.

functions.name: QPDF::getRoot
functions.description: Return the document catalog (/Root) object handle.
requirements: Requires a loaded/created PDF.

functions.name: QPDF::getXRefTable
functions.description: Return the cross-reference table as a map from object-generation to xref entry.
requirements: Requires a loaded/created PDF.

functions.name: QPDF::newStream
functions.description: Create a new empty stream object; caller must later supply data via replaceStreamData().
requirements: After creation, call replaceStreamData() to set stream contents before writing.
May retrieve and modify the stream dictionary via getDict() or replaceDict().

functions.name: QPDF::newStream
functions.description: Create a new stream initialized with the provided Buffer as its data. /Length is set automatically.
requirements: data must be a valid shared Buffer containing the desired bytes.
Additional stream dictionary keys can be set via getDict()/replaceDict() if needed.

functions.name: QPDF::newStream
functions.description: Create a new stream from a string; data is copied internally. /Length is set automatically.
requirements: Suitable for modest-sized data; for large data, consider Buffer to avoid copies.

functions.name: QPDF::newReserved
functions.description: Create a sentinel reserved indirect object for forward references (e.g., cyclic structures). Must later be replaced with replaceReserved().
requirements: Reserved objects cannot be resolved to direct objects and must be replaced before writing with QPDFWriter.
Use replaceReserved(reserved, replacement) to finalize.

functions.name: QPDF::newIndirectNull
functions.description: Create a new indirect null object.
requirements: None.

functions.name: QPDF::makeIndirectObject
functions.description: Install the given (direct) object as an indirect object in this QPDF and return an indirect reference to it.
requirements: obj must be a direct object (may contain references to other indirect objects).

functions.name: QPDF::getObject
functions.description: Retrieve an object by object number and generation, returning an indirect reference.
requirements: og must refer to an existing object; otherwise behavior is to throw or return null-equivalent per qpdf semantics (not explicitly stated—unknown).

functions.name: QPDF::getObject
functions.description: Retrieve an object by object and generation numbers, returning an indirect reference.
requirements: objid/generation must refer to an existing object; error handling as per qpdf (not explicitly stated—unknown).

functions.name: QPDF::getObjectByObjGen
functions.description: Legacy equivalent to getObject(og). No deprecation planned.
requirements: og must refer to an existing object (behavior on missing object is not stated—unknown).

functions.name: QPDF::getObjectByID
functions.description: Legacy equivalent to getObject(objid, generation).
requirements: objid/generation must refer to an existing object (behavior on missing object is not stated—unknown).

functions.name: QPDF::replaceObject
functions.description: Replace the specified indirect object with the given direct object. From 10.2.1, existing QPDFObjectHandle references are updated to the new object. Replacing with newNull() effectively removes the object.
requirements: obj must be a direct object (though it may contain indirect references).
To replace a reserved object, use replaceReserved instead.

functions.name: QPDF::replaceObject
functions.signature: void QPDF::replaceObject(int objid, int generation, QPDFObjectHandle obj)
functions.description: Replace the specified indirect object (by numbers) with the given direct object. Same semantics as the QPDFObjGen overload.
requirements: obj must be a direct object.
Use replaceReserved for reserved objects.

functions.name: QPDF::swapObjects
functions.description: Swap two objects by object-generation. From 10.2.1, existing QPDFObjectHandle references observe the swap.
requirements: Both identifiers must refer to existing objects.

functions.name: QPDF::swapObjects
functions.signature: void QPDF::swapObjects(int objid1, int generation1, int objid2, int generation2)
functions.description: Swap two objects given by object and generation numbers. Same semantics as the QPDFObjGen overload.
requirements: Both (objid,generation) pairs must refer to existing objects.

functions.name: QPDF::replaceReserved
functions.description: Replace a reserved (or null) object with the replacement object. Ensures the underlying object is indeed reserved/null. After the call, the reserved handle references the replacement.
requirements: reserved must reference a reserved or null object; otherwise it is an error.
replacement should be a direct object suitable for installation.

functions.name: QPDF::copyForeignObject
functions.description: Copy an object (and its indirectly referenced graph) from another QPDF into this one, returning an indirect reference to the copy. Designed for non-page objects; use addPage/AddPageAt for pages.
requirements: If the source object is a stream backed by StreamDataProvider, the source QPDF must remain alive until the destination is written unless setImmediateCopyFrom(true) was called on the source prior to copying.
If copying objects that reference pages, copy the pages first with addPage(At) or such references will become null.
Mutation of source objects after copying does not cause them to be recopied; perform all mutations before copying.
Be mindful of RAM usage if setImmediateCopyFrom(true) was used on the source.

functions.name: QPDF::EncryptionData::getV

functions.name: QPDF::EncryptionData::getR
functions.description: Accessor for EncryptionData R (revision).

functions.name: QPDF::EncryptionData::getLengthBytes
functions.description: Accessor for key length in bytes.

functions.name: QPDF::EncryptionData::getU
