functions.name: QPDF::EncryptionData::getOE
functions.description: Accessor for OE (owner encrypted key) for V>=5.

functions.name: QPDF::EncryptionData::getUE
functions.description: Accessor for UE (user encrypted key) for V>=5.

functions.name: QPDF::EncryptionData::getPerms
functions.description: Accessor for Perms (permissions) entry for V>=5.

functions.name: QPDF::EncryptionData::getId1
functions.description: Accessor for first document ID string used in key derivation.

functions.name: QPDF::EncryptionData::getEncryptMetadata
functions.description: Accessor for encrypt_metadata flag.

functions.name: QPDF::EncryptionData::setO
functions.description: Mutator for owner password data (O entry).

functions.name: QPDF::EncryptionData::setU
functions.description: Mutator for user password data (U entry).

functions.name: QPDF::EncryptionData::setV5EncryptionParameters
functions.signature: void QPDF::EncryptionData::setV5EncryptionParameters(std::string const& O, std::string const& OE, std::string const& U, std::string const& UE, std::string const& Perms)
functions.description: Set V5 encryption parameters (O, OE, U, UE, Perms) on the EncryptionData.
requirements: Intended for V>=5 encryption settings.

functions.name: QPDF::isEncrypted
functions.description: Return true if the input PDF is encrypted.
requirements: Requires a loaded/created PDF.

functions.name: QPDF::isEncrypted
functions.description: Return true if encrypted and populate encryption revision (R) and permissions (P).
requirements: Requires a loaded/created PDF.
R and P are output parameters and will be set when true is returned.

functions.name: QPDF::isEncrypted
functions.signature: bool QPDF::isEncrypted(int& R, int& P, int& V, encryption_method_e& stream_method, encryption_method_e& string_method, encryption_method_e& file_method)
functions.description: Return true if encrypted and populate additional fields: R, P, V and encryption methods for streams, strings, and file.
requirements: Requires a loaded/created PDF.
All reference parameters are outputs and will be set on success.

functions.name: QPDF::ownerPasswordMatched
functions.description: Return true if an owner password was supplied and accepted for the file.
requirements: Call after processing an encrypted file.

functions.name: QPDF::userPasswordMatched
functions.description: Return true if a user password was supplied and accepted for the file.
requirements: Call after processing an encrypted file.

functions.name: QPDF::allowAccessibility
functions.description: Return true if accessibility (extract for accessibility) is permitted per encryption flags. Not enforced by qpdf.
requirements: Meaningful only for encrypted files.

functions.name: QPDF::allowExtractAll
functions.description: Return true if extraction is permitted per encryption flags. Not enforced by qpdf.
requirements: Meaningful only for encrypted files.

functions.name: QPDF::allowPrintLowRes
functions.description: Return true if low-resolution printing is permitted per encryption flags. Not enforced by qpdf.
requirements: Meaningful only for encrypted files.

functions.name: QPDF::allowPrintHighRes
functions.description: Return true if high-resolution printing is permitted per encryption flags. Not enforced by qpdf.
requirements: Meaningful only for encrypted files.

functions.name: QPDF::allowModifyAssembly
functions.description: Return true if document assembly is permitted per encryption flags. Not enforced by qpdf.
requirements: Meaningful only for encrypted files.

functions.name: QPDF::allowModifyForm
functions.description: Return true if form filling modification is permitted per encryption flags. Not enforced by qpdf.
requirements: Meaningful only for encrypted files.

functions.name: QPDF::allowModifyAnnotation
functions.description: Return true if annotation modification is permitted per encryption flags. Not enforced by qpdf.
requirements: Meaningful only for encrypted files.

functions.name: QPDF::allowModifyOther
functions.description: Return true if other modifications are permitted per encryption flags. Not enforced by qpdf.
requirements: Meaningful only for encrypted files.

functions.name: QPDF::allowModifyAll
functions.description: Return true if all modifications are permitted per encryption flags. Not enforced by qpdf.
requirements: Meaningful only for encrypted files.

functions.name: QPDF::trim_user_password
functions.description: Helper to trim padding bytes from a user password as stored in the PDF format.
requirements: Pass a modifiable string containing a padded user password.

functions.name: QPDF::compute_data_key
functions.signature: static std::string QPDF::compute_data_key(std::string const& encryption_key, int objid, int generation, bool use_aes, int encryption_V, int encryption_R)
functions.description: Compute the per-object data key for stream/string encryption/decryption using the file encryption key and object identifiers.
requirements: Provide valid encryption_key and correct objid/generation.
use_aes selects AES derivation; specify encryption_V and encryption_R consistent with the file’s encryption dictionary.

functions.name: QPDF::compute_encryption_key
functions.signature: [[deprecated("to be removed in qpdf 13")]] static std::string QPDF::compute_encryption_key(std::string const& password, EncryptionData const& data)
functions.description: Deprecated: compute an encryption key from a password and EncryptionData. To be removed in qpdf 13.
requirements: Prefer newer APIs; this exists for backward compatibility.

functions.name: QPDF::compute_encryption_O_U
functions.signature: static void QPDF::compute_encryption_O_U(char const* user_password, char const* owner_password, int V, int R, int key_len, int P, bool encrypt_metadata, std::string const& id1, std::string& O, std::string& U)
functions.description: Compute O and U values for classic (non-V5) encryption given user/owner passwords and parameters.
requirements: Provide non-null pointers where appropriate; output strings O and U are written by the function.
Parameters V, R, key_len, P, encrypt_metadata, and id1 must match the intended encryption settings.

functions.name: QPDF::compute_encryption_parameters_V5
functions.signature: static void QPDF::compute_encryption_parameters_V5(char const* user_password, char const* owner_password, int V, int R, int key_len, int P, bool encrypt_metadata, std::string const& id1, std::string& encryption_key, std::string& O, std::string& U, std::string& OE, std::string& UE, std::string& Perms)
functions.description: Compute V5 encryption parameters: encryption_key, O, U, OE, UE, and Perms from provided passwords and settings.
requirements: Output parameters (encryption_key, O, U, OE, UE, Perms) will be assigned by the function.
Input parameters must be consistent with V5 encryption settings.

functions.name: QPDF::getPaddedUserPassword
functions.description: Return the full stored user password (padded form) if recoverable (possible for 40/128-bit, not for newer formats).
requirements: Call after opening an encrypted file; availability depends on encryption type.

functions.name: QPDF::getTrimmedUserPassword
functions.description: Return a human-readable trimmed version of the user password, subject to the same recovery limitations as getPaddedUserPassword().
requirements: Call after opening an encrypted file; availability depends on encryption type.

functions.name: QPDF::getEncryptionKey
functions.description: Return the computed or retrieved file encryption key for the current PDF.
requirements: Call after processing a (possibly encrypted) PDF.

functions.name: QPDF::removeSecurityRestrictions
functions.description: Remove security restrictions associated with digitally signed files. Typically invoked via QPDFAcroFormDocumentHelper::disableDigitalSignatures.
requirements: Call on a loaded PDF; primarily useful when coordinating with AcroForm helpers.

functions.name: QPDF::isLinearized
functions.description: Return true if the file begins with a linearization parameter dictionary (no further validation).
requirements: Requires a loaded/created PDF.

functions.name: QPDF::checkLinearization
functions.description: Perform sanity checks on linearization; returns true if no errors/warnings, otherwise false and emits diagnostics to the configured logger. Recommended to treat linearization errors as warnings.
requirements: Requires a loaded PDF.
Logger should be configured to capture output if needed.

functions.name: QPDF::showLinearizationData
functions.description: Print normalized summaries of certain hints tables related to linearization to the default output stream.
requirements: Requires a loaded PDF.
Logger/output streams determine destination of printed data.

functions.name: QPDF::showXRefTable
functions.description: Print the contents of the cross-reference table to the default output stream.
requirements: Requires a loaded PDF.

functions.name: QPDF::fixDanglingReferences
functions.description: Detect and resolve indirect references to non-existent objects by replacing them with null, per PDF spec. Since 11.0, called automatically when needed; caching avoids repeated runs.
requirements: Generally no need to call for user code since 11.0; safe to call if you have modified objects directly.
force parameter is ignored since 11.2.1 per comment; behavior may not re-run if already done.

functions.name: QPDF::getObjectCount
functions.description: Return the approximate number of indirect objects in the PDF (gaps and some losses may make it inexact).
requirements: Requires a loaded/created PDF.

functions.name: QPDF::getAllObjects
functions.description: Return a list of indirect objects for every entry in the xref table, useful to discover unreferenced objects.
requirements: Requires a loaded PDF.

functions.name: QPDF::optimize
functions.signature: [[deprecated("Unused - see release notes for qpdf 12.1.0")]] void QPDF::optimize(std::map<int, int> const& object_stream_data, bool allow_changes = true, std::function<int(QPDFObjectHandle&)> skip_stream_parameters = nullptr)
functions.description: Deprecated: perform optimization support (populate object<->user maps; optionally ensure no changes if allow_changes=false).
requirements: object_stream_data maps compressed objects to their object stream container ids.
If allow_changes is false, an exception is thrown if optimization would change the file.
skip_stream_parameters, if provided, must return 0/1/2 to indicate which stream dict keys to discard.

functions.name: QPDF::getAllPages
functions.description: Traverse the /Pages tree and return all /Page objects, resolving duplicates. Returns a const reference to an internal cache updated by page APIs.
requirements: Safe for read-only uses; direct manipulation of the page tree or inheritable attributes may invalidate the cache until updateAllPagesCache() is called.
For modification workflows, prefer QPDFPageDocumentHelper.

functions.name: QPDF::everCalledGetAllPages
functions.description: Return whether getAllPages() has ever been called on this instance.

functions.name: QPDF::everPushedInheritedAttributesToPages
functions.description: Return whether pushInheritedAttributesToPage() has ever been invoked.

functions.name: QPDF::findPage
functions.description: Return the 0-based index in getAllPages() for the page with the given object-generation. Throws if not found.
requirements: og must refer to a /Page object present in the document.

functions.name: QPDF::findPage
functions.description: Return the 0-based index in getAllPages() for the given page object handle. Throws if not found.
requirements: page must reference a valid /Page object in the document.

functions.name: QPDF::updateAllPagesCache
functions.description: Synchronize QPDF’s internal pages cache with the actual /Pages tree. Also resets state about pushed inheritable attributes.
requirements: Call after direct modifications to /Pages structures or adding inheritable attributes outside the provided page APIs.
After calling, previously returned references from getAllPages() become valid again.

functions.name: QPDF::pushInheritedAttributesToPage
functions.description: Legacy page helper: push inheritable attributes from /Pages nodes down to page objects.
requirements: Prefer QPDFPageDocumentHelper for new code.

functions.name: QPDF::addPage
functions.description: Legacy page helper: add a page at the beginning (first=true) or end (first=false) of the document.
requirements: newpage must be a valid /Page object (or convertible to one as per qpdf semantics—details not specified).

functions.name: QPDF::addPageAt
functions.signature: void QPDF::addPageAt(QPDFObjectHandle newpage, bool before, QPDFObjectHandle refpage)
functions.description: Legacy page helper: insert newpage before or after refpage depending on before flag.
requirements: newpage must be a valid /Page object.
refpage must reference an existing page.

functions.name: QPDF::removePage
functions.description: Legacy page helper: remove the specified page from the document.
requirements: page must reference an existing page in the document.

functions.name: QPDFUsage::QPDFUsage
functions.description: Constructs a QPDFUsage exception object (derived from std::runtime_error) with the provided message. Intended to signal improper usage or similar user-facing errors in qpdf. Typical usage is to create and/or throw this exception and catch it as QPDFUsage or std::runtime_error/std::exception. The message is retrievable via what().
requirements: msg must be a valid std::string reference at the time of construction; no specific content or encoding is required or enforced.
The constructed object can be thrown and caught as an exception; callers should handle exceptions appropriately (e.g., via try/catch) and may inspect the message via what().

functions.name: QPDFWriter::QPDFWriter
functions.description: Constructs a QPDFWriter associated with the given QPDF but without setting any output target. You must set exactly one output target later via setOutputFilename(), setOutputFile(), setOutputMemory(), or setOutputPipeline() before calling write().
requirements: Must call exactly one output-setting method after construction and before write().
Do not attempt to set output more than once.
The provided QPDF reference must remain valid for the lifetime of the QPDFWriter.

functions.name: QPDFWriter::QPDFWriter
functions.description: Constructs a QPDFWriter and immediately sets the output to the specified filename (or stdout if filename is nullptr). Equivalent to the default constructor followed by setOutputFilename(filename).
requirements: If filename is nullptr, output is directed to stdout.
A zero-length output file is created at construction; if write() later fails, the partial/empty file is not deleted by QPDFWriter.
Only one output target is allowed for a QPDFWriter instance.
The provided QPDF reference must remain valid for the lifetime of the QPDFWriter.

functions.name: QPDFWriter::QPDFWriter
functions.signature: QPDFWriter::QPDFWriter(QPDF& pdf, char const* description, FILE* file, bool close_file)
functions.description: Constructs a QPDFWriter and immediately sets the output to the provided FILE*. Equivalent to the default constructor followed by setOutputFile(description, file, close_file).
requirements: Caller must supply an already-open FILE* in binary mode.
The FILE* need not be seekable; output is written in a single pass.
If close_file is true, QPDFWriter will close the FILE*; otherwise the caller must close it.
Only one output target is allowed for a QPDFWriter instance.
The provided QPDF reference must remain valid for the lifetime of the QPDFWriter.

functions.name: QPDFWriter::setOutputFilename
functions.description: Sets the output destination to a file path or stdout (if filename is nullptr). Creates an empty output file immediately. Use when you didn’t set output in the constructor.
requirements: May be called at most once per QPDFWriter instance and only if output was not set in the constructor.
If filename is nullptr, output is to stdout.
If write() later fails, QPDFWriter will not delete the empty/partial file; caller should remove it if undesired.
Must be called before write().

functions.name: QPDFWriter::setOutputFile
functions.signature: void QPDFWriter::setOutputFile(char const* description, FILE* file, bool close_file)
functions.description: Configures QPDFWriter to write to an already-open FILE*. QPDFWriter will call finish() on its internal pipeline; it may close the FILE* depending on close_file.
requirements: Caller must open the FILE* prior to this call and in binary mode.
The FILE* does not need to be seekable; writing is single-pass.
If close_file is true, QPDFWriter will close the FILE*; otherwise the caller must close it.
May be called at most once per QPDFWriter instance and only if output was not set in the constructor.
Must be called before write().
description is a human-readable label for diagnostics; no functional constraints are enforced.

functions.name: QPDFWriter::setOutputMemory
functions.description: Directs QPDFWriter to write the final PDF into an internal memory buffer retrievable via getBuffer() or getBufferSharedPointer().
requirements: May be called at most once per QPDFWriter instance and only if output was not set in the constructor.
Call before write().
Use getBuffer() exactly once after write(), or use getBufferSharedPointer() to obtain a shared_ptr view.

functions.name: QPDFWriter::getBuffer
functions.description: Returns a raw pointer to the internal Buffer that contains the complete PDF file when setOutputMemory() was used. Intended for single retrieval after write(). Caller owns deletion of the Buffer.
requirements: setOutputMemory() must have been called prior to write().
May be called exactly one time, and only after write() has returned.
Caller is responsible for deleting the returned Buffer when finished.
Do not mix raw pointer deletion with shared ownership obtained from getBufferSharedPointer().

functions.name: QPDFWriter::getBufferSharedPointer
functions.description: Returns a shared_ptr to the Buffer containing the final PDF when output was configured for memory. This is the shared-ownership alternative to getBuffer().
requirements: setOutputMemory() must have been called prior to write().
Call only after write() has returned to ensure the buffer is complete.
Use shared ownership semantics; do not also delete a raw Buffer obtained from getBuffer().

functions.name: QPDFWriter::setOutputPipeline
functions.description: Sets a custom output Pipeline to receive PDF bytes. QPDFWriter will write to this pipeline and call pipeline->finish() when done. Memory management of the pipeline remains with the caller.
requirements: Caller must allocate and manage the lifetime of the Pipeline object; QPDFWriter will never delete it.
May be called at most once per QPDFWriter instance and only if output was not set in the constructor.
Must be called before write().
Pipeline must remain valid until after QPDFWriter completes writing and calls finish().

functions.name: QPDFWriter::setObjectStreamMode
functions.description: Controls whether and how object streams are written (disable, preserve, or generate). The default is preserve. Cross-reference output format follows from the presence of object streams.
requirements: Call before operations that depend on versioning or writing (e.g., before getFinalVersion() or write()).
Mode must be one of qpdf_object_stream_e values.

functions.name: QPDFWriter::setStreamDataMode
functions.description: Legacy interface for controlling stream data handling. Prefer setCompressStreams() and setDecodeLevel(). Provides backward-compatible mapping among uncompress/preserve/compress behaviors; default is qpdf_s_compress.
requirements: Call before write() and preferably before getFinalVersion().
Understand that this does not cover the full configuration range; use setCompressStreams and setDecodeLevel for finer control.

functions.name: QPDFWriter::setCompressStreams
functions.description: If true, compresses any uncompressed streams on output (metadata streams are an exception and remain uncompressed). Default is true.
requirements: Call before write() and preferably before getFinalVersion().
Be aware that metadata streams are not compressed even if true.

functions.name: QPDFWriter::setDecodeLevel
functions.description: Sets how aggressively QPDFWriter decodes filters on input streams before writing. Levels: none, generalized (default), specialized, all. Combined with setCompressStreams(true), this can re-encode streams with Flate; see also setRecompressFlate().
requirements: Call before write() and preferably before getFinalVersion().
At qpdf_dl_all, lossy DCTDecode may be applied; avoid repeated lossy recompression cycles if later re-encoding to JPEG.

functions.name: QPDFWriter::setRecompressFlate
functions.description: When true, forces uncompress/recompress of streams that are Flate-compressed on both input and output. Useful with higher compression settings (e.g., via Pl_Flate::setCompressionLevel).
requirements: Call before write() and preferably before getFinalVersion().

functions.name: QPDFWriter::setContentNormalization
functions.description: Enables newline normalization inside content streams. Intended only for debugging/experimentation; may damage content (e.g., inline images) and should not be used in production.
requirements: Use only for debugging; do not use for production files due to potential content damage.
Call before write().

functions.name: QPDFWriter::setQDFMode
functions.description: Enables QDF mode, which pretty-prints objects and adds comments for easier inspection. Resulting files can be edited and then repaired with fix-qdf.
requirements: Call before write().
QDF mode is incompatible with preserving encryption and disables it if selected.

functions.name: QPDFWriter::setPreserveUnreferencedObjects
functions.description: Controls whether unreferenced objects (not reachable from the trailer) are preserved. Default behavior discards unreferenced objects.
requirements: Call before write().

functions.name: QPDFWriter::setNewlineBeforeEndstream
functions.description: Forces a newline before each endstream keyword. Helps with PDF/A compliance (not sufficient by itself).
requirements: Call before write().

functions.name: QPDFWriter::setMinimumPDFVersion
functions.description: Sets a minimum PDF version for output. If the input’s version (or previously set minimum) is lower, the output version is raised to this value; otherwise the higher, existing version is used. QPDFWriter auto-raises to 1.4 for R3 encryption and 1.5 for object streams.
requirements: Call before write(); calling after getFinalVersion() is an error since it prepares for writing.
version must be a valid PDF version string; extension_level is an optional extension level integer.

functions.name: QPDFWriter::setMinimumPDFVersion
functions.description: Overload to set the minimum PDF version using a PDFVersion object. Behaves like the string overload regarding version raising and auto-raise rules for encryption and object streams.
requirements: Call before write(); calling after getFinalVersion() is an error since it prepares for writing.
Provided PDFVersion must represent a valid PDF version.

functions.name: QPDFWriter::forcePDFVersion
functions.signature: void QPDFWriter::forcePDFVersion(std::string const& version, int extension_level = 0)
functions.description: Forces the output PDF version regardless of features present. May create files incompatible with older viewers or with selected features. Forcing below 1.5 disables object streams; forcing to a version too low for configured encryption disables decryption.
requirements: Caller is responsible for ensuring the forced version is appropriate for the file’s features; otherwise output may not work on some viewers.
Calling after getFinalVersion() is an error since that call prepares for writing.
Be aware: forcing below 1.5 disables object streams; forcing to a version too low for the encryption type explicitly disables decryption.

functions.name: QPDFWriter::setExtraHeaderText
functions.description: Inserts arbitrary text near the beginning of the PDF file (e.g., extra comments). No validation is performed. An extra newline is appended if one is not present; for multi-line comments, include '\n' and start each line with '%'.
requirements: Caller must ensure the inserted text is valid for the intended consumer; QPDFWriter does not validate it.
Call before write().

functions.name: QPDFWriter::setDeterministicID
functions.description: Enables deterministic /ID generation by hashing significant content, avoiding time and output filename inputs. Useful for reproducible outputs. Incompatible with encrypted files because encryption requires /ID prior to writing.
requirements: Do not use with encrypted output; deterministic /ID is incompatible with encryption.
Call before write().

functions.name: QPDFWriter::setStaticID
functions.description: Enables a fixed, static /ID value. Intended only for test suites to produce predictable output. See also setDeterministicID().
requirements: Use only for testing; not appropriate for production.
Call before write().

functions.name: QPDFWriter::setStaticAesIV
functions.description: Uses a fixed initialization vector for AES-CBC encryption. This is insecure and intended only for predictable encrypted output in test suites.
requirements: Use only for testing; not secure for production.
Applicable only when AES-CBC encryption is in use.
Call before write().

functions.name: QPDFWriter::setSuppressOriginalObjectIDs
functions.description: Suppresses comments that record original object IDs when writing in QDF mode. Useful for stable diffing in tests.
requirements: Call before write().
Only affects QDF output; has no effect outside QDF mode.

functions.name: QPDFWriter::setPreserveEncryption
functions.description: Controls whether to preserve encryption from the source document. Default is true unless prefiltering, content normalization, or QDF mode are selected, in which case encryption is never preserved. Encryption is also not preserved if explicit encryption parameters are set.
requirements: Call before write().
Has no effect if prefiltering/content normalization/QDF mode is enabled or explicit encryption parameters are set, since those disable preservation.

functions.name: QPDFWriter::copyEncryptionParameters
functions.description: Copies encryption parameters from another QPDF object. If you want to preserve encryption from the QPDF being written, use setPreserveEncryption(true) instead.
requirements: Call before write().
The provided QPDF must contain the desired encryption parameters.
Mutually exclusive in intent with setPreserveEncryption(true) on the same source file.

functions.name: QPDFWriter::setR2EncryptionParametersInsecure

If using QUtil::file_provider(filename), the file's contents will be provided as binary as the stream source.

functions.name: QPDFEFStreamObjectHelper::setCreationDate
functions.description: Set the EF stream's CreationDate parameter. The value must be a PDF date/time string of the form "D:yyyymmddhhmmss<z>" (e.g., "D:20210207161528-05'00'" or "D:20210207211528Z"). Returns a reference to this helper to allow fluent chaining.
requirements: date must conform to the PDF date/time string format "D:yyyymmddhhmmss<z>" as described in the PDF spec.

functions.name: QPDFEFStreamObjectHelper::setModDate
functions.description: Set the EF stream's ModDate parameter. The value must be a PDF date/time string of the form "D:yyyymmddhhmmss<z>". Returns a reference to this helper to allow fluent chaining.
requirements: date must conform to the PDF date/time string format "D:yyyymmddhhmmss<z>" as described in the PDF spec.

functions.name: QPDFEFStreamObjectHelper::setSubtype
functions.description: Set the EF stream's Subtype to a MIME type string (e.g., "text/plain" or "application/pdf"). Returns a reference to this helper to allow fluent chaining.
requirements: mime_type should be a valid MIME type string such as "text/plain" or "application/pdf" (per comments).

functions.name: QPDFEmbeddedFileDocumentHelper::get
functions.description: Return a shared document-helper instance for the given QPDF that manages document-level embedded files. Using this instead of constructing a new helper avoids repeated validation of the EmbeddedFiles structure. Typical usage: obtain the helper once per QPDF and reuse it for querying/altering attachments.
requirements: qpdf must refer to a valid, initialized QPDF document object.
The returned reference remains valid only as long as the underlying QPDF object outlives its helpers; do not destroy the QPDF while using the helper reference.
Thread-safety unknown; avoid sharing a single helper across threads unless documented elsewhere.

functions.name: QPDFEmbeddedFileDocumentHelper::validate
functions.description: Re-validate the EmbeddedFiles structure, optionally attempting to repair it. Call this after you have modified the EmbeddedFiles dictionary in a way that would invalidate cached state. If repair is true, the helper will attempt to repair issues it encounters.
requirements: Call this after directly modifying the EmbeddedFiles dictionary to refresh and re-validate internal caches.
If repair is false, be prepared for validation to report errors (exact error mechanism is unknown from the header).
Must be called on a helper associated with a live QPDF document.

functions.name: QPDFEmbeddedFileDocumentHelper::QPDFEmbeddedFileDocumentHelper
functions.description: Construct a helper bound to the given QPDF to manage document-level embedded files. Prefer using get(QPDF&) to reuse a shared helper and avoid repeated validation unless you explicitly need a new instance.
requirements: qpdf must be a valid, initialized QPDF object that remains alive for at least as long as this helper instance.
Constructing a new helper may trigger validation of the EmbeddedFiles structure (cost/behavior inferred from comments about caching).

functions.name: QPDFEmbeddedFileDocumentHelper::~QPDFEmbeddedFileDocumentHelper
functions.description: Destructor for the embedded-file document helper. Cleans up helper state; the underlying QPDF document is not owned by this helper.
requirements: The associated QPDF object must not already be destroyed while the helper is being destroyed (standard ownership/lifetime requirement).

functions.name: QPDFEmbeddedFileDocumentHelper::hasEmbeddedFiles
functions.description: Return true if the document has any embedded files (attachments), false otherwise. Use this as a quick check before enumerating or fetching attachments.
requirements: Must be called on a helper associated with a valid QPDF document.

functions.name: QPDFEmbeddedFileDocumentHelper::getEmbeddedFiles
functions.description: Return a map from attachment name to file-spec helper for all document-level embedded files. The returned map is a snapshot; modifying it does not alter the PDF.
requirements: Caller should not assume the returned map reflects future changes; call again after modifications.
Each shared_ptr may be null only if no such entry exists; by contract here, present entries correspond to existing embedded files.

functions.name: QPDFEmbeddedFileDocumentHelper::getEmbeddedFile
functions.description: Look up a single embedded file by name. If an embedded file with the given name exists, returns a shared pointer to its file-spec helper; otherwise returns nullptr.
requirements: name is matched against the EmbeddedFiles name tree key; exact matching and encoding are not specified here (assume exact string match).
Caller must check for nullptr to handle the case where no embedded file with the given name exists.
Must be called on a helper associated with a valid QPDF document.

functions.name: QPDFEmbeddedFileDocumentHelper::replaceEmbeddedFile
functions.signature: void QPDFEmbeddedFileDocumentHelper::replaceEmbeddedFile(std::string const& name, QPDFFileSpecObjectHelper const& file_spec)
functions.description: Add a new attachment or replace an existing one under the given name with the provided file-spec. This updates the EmbeddedFiles name tree entry for name to point to file_spec.
requirements: file_spec should refer to a file specification object belonging to the same underlying QPDF document (inferred from library helper patterns).
If an entry with the given name already exists, it will be replaced; callers should be aware of overwriting prior attachments.
Must be called on a helper associated with a valid QPDF document.

functions.name: QPDFEmbeddedFileDocumentHelper::removeEmbeddedFile
functions.description: Remove the embedded file identified by name, if present. Returns true if an entry was present and removed. In addition to removing the name-tree entry, this also nulls out the file specification dictionary so references from file-attachment annotations stop working—effectively removing the attachment from the document.
requirements: Caller should expect that any annotations or references to this file will stop working after removal.
name should correspond to an existing EmbeddedFiles entry to return true; otherwise the function returns false.
Must be called on a helper associated with a valid QPDF document.

functions.name: QPDFFileSpecObjectHelper::QPDFFileSpecObjectHelper
functions.description: Constructor for a helper around a PDF File Specification dictionary. Wraps an existing QPDFObjectHandle that should reference a File Specification (FileSpec) dictionary, enabling higher-level operations on filenames and embedded file streams.
requirements: The QPDFObjectHandle argument should reference a valid File Specification dictionary object as defined by ISO-32000 (section 7.11).
The provided handle should be associated with a live QPDF instance for subsequent operations.
Behavior is undefined if the handle is not a dictionary or not a File Specification dictionary.

functions.name: QPDFFileSpecObjectHelper::getDescription
functions.description: Returns the human-readable description string of the file specification, if present. If not present, returns an empty string.
requirements: The underlying object should be a valid File Specification dictionary.
Callers should handle the possibility of an empty return value when the description is absent.

functions.name: QPDFFileSpecObjectHelper::getFilename
functions.description: Returns the primary filename for the file specification. Resolution order is /UF, then /F, then platform-specific keys /Unix, /DOS, /Mac. Returns an empty string if no filename is available.
requirements: Underlying object should be a valid File Specification dictionary.
Callers should handle the possibility of an empty result when no filename keys are present.

functions.name: QPDFFileSpecObjectHelper::getFilenames
functions.description: Returns any filename entries present in the FileSpec, across the keys /UF, /F, /Unix, /DOS, and /Mac, as a map from key to value.
requirements: Underlying object should be a valid File Specification dictionary.
Callers should not assume all keys are present; the map may be empty or contain a subset of the supported keys.

functions.name: QPDFFileSpecObjectHelper::getEmbeddedFileStream
functions.description: Returns the embedded file stream object corresponding to the provided filename key. If key is empty, resolution order is /UF, /F, /Unix, /DOS, /Mac. Returns a null QPDFObjectHandle if not found. The returned object, when non-null and of stream type, contains the attachment data; use QPDFEFStreamObjectHelper for higher-level access to its parameters.
requirements: Underlying object should be a valid File Specification dictionary.
If key is provided, it should be one of "UF", "F", "Unix", "DOS", or "Mac" (without the slash) to match typical FileSpec keys; an unknown key will yield a null handle.
Callers must check for a null QPDFObjectHandle return to detect absence.
If higher-level parameters are needed, wrap the returned stream in QPDFEFStreamObjectHelper.

functions.name: QPDFFileSpecObjectHelper::getEmbeddedFileStreams
functions.description: Returns the value of the /EF entry from the FileSpec dictionary, which maps filename keys to embedded file streams. May be a null object if /EF is absent.
requirements: Underlying object should be a valid File Specification dictionary.
Callers must be prepared for a null or non-dictionary return if /EF is absent or malformed and should validate before use.

functions.name: QPDFFileSpecObjectHelper::createFileSpec
functions.signature: static QPDFFileSpecObjectHelper createFileSpec(QPDF& qpdf, std::string const& filename, std::string const& fullpath)
functions.description: Creates a new File Specification as an indirect object in the given QPDF. The file identified by fullpath is attached as an embedded file stream. The filename is stored in the FileSpec; see setFilename for customization.
requirements: qpdf must refer to an initialized, open QPDF document into which new objects can be created.
fullpath should reference an existing, readable file; failures to locate or read the file will cause creation to fail (error handling mechanism is library-defined).
filename should be the desired display/storage name to record in the FileSpec; encoding expectations are not explicitly specified here.

functions.name: QPDFFileSpecObjectHelper::setDescription
functions.description: Sets the FileSpec’s description string. Returns a reference to this helper to allow fluent chaining.
requirements: Underlying object should be a valid, mutable File Specification dictionary.
Callers should ensure the string content is appropriate for PDF metadata; no specific encoding constraints are stated.

functions.name: QPDFFileSpecObjectHelper::setFilename
functions.signature: QPDFFileSpecObjectHelper& setFilename(std::string const& unicode_name, std::string const& compat_name = "")
functions.description: Sets the FileSpec’s filename entries. Sets /UF to unicode_name (UTF‑8). If compat_name is empty, also sets /F to unicode_name. If compat_name is provided, it is stored literally in /F without re-encoding to preserve its original byte sequence.
requirements: Underlying object should be a valid, mutable File Specification dictionary.
unicode_name must be UTF-8 encoded.
If compat_name is provided, it may be any byte sequence; it is stored as-is and should already be in the desired legacy encoding if needed.
Callers should use this after construction or createFileSpec if they need to override default filename values.

functions.name: QPDFFormFieldObjectHelper
functions.description: Default-constructs a QPDFFormFieldObjectHelper that wraps a null/empty underlying object. Useful as a sentinel or to be assigned later from another form field handle. Call isNull() to test whether it wraps a real field.

functions.name: QPDFFormFieldObjectHelper
functions.description: Constructs a QPDFFormFieldObjectHelper bound to the supplied QPDFObjectHandle representing a form field dictionary. Enables field inspection and modification methods on that underlying object.
requirements: The provided QPDFObjectHandle should refer to a valid form field dictionary object as defined by the PDF spec (inferred from the class purpose).
If the handle does not refer to a field, behavior of field-specific queries is implementation-defined; callers should be prepared for empty/false/neutral results (inferred from comments throughout).

functions.name: isNull
functions.description: Returns true if this helper’s underlying object is null (i.e., the helper is not bound to a real form field). Use to guard calls that require a valid field.

functions.name: getParent
functions.description: Returns the parent field helper of this field. If there is no parent, returns a QPDFFormFieldObjectHelper whose underlying object is null; check with isNull().

functions.name: getTopLevelField
functions.description: Returns the top-level field corresponding to this field (often the field itself or its parent). If is_different is provided, it is set to true if the returned field differs from this one; otherwise false.
requirements: If is_different is non-null, it must point to valid writable memory.

functions.name: getInheritableFieldValue
functions.description: Looks up a field attribute by key, searching this field and then its ancestors per PDF inheritance rules. Returns the found value as a QPDFObjectHandle, or a null/empty handle if not present.
requirements: name is a PDF dictionary key (without the leading slash), e.g., "FT", "DA" (inferred from typical usage and examples in comments).

functions.name: getInheritableFieldValueAsString
functions.description: Retrieves an inherited field attribute and returns it as a string if the value is a string; otherwise returns the empty string silently.
requirements: name must be the attribute key to look up (without a leading slash).

functions.name: getInheritableFieldValueAsName
functions.description: Retrieves an inherited field attribute of type name and returns the name as a string; if not a name, returns the empty string silently.
requirements: name must be the attribute key to look up (without a leading slash).

functions.name: getFieldType
functions.description: Returns the value of the /FT (field type) entry if present; otherwise returns the empty string. Typical values include Tx, Btn, Ch, etc.

functions.name: getFullyQualifiedName
functions.description: Returns the field’s fully qualified name (concatenation of ancestor partial names).

functions.name: getPartialName
functions.description: Returns the field’s partial name (/T).

functions.name: getAlternativeName
functions.description: Returns the alternative field name (/TU), intended for user display. If absent, falls back to the fully qualified name.

functions.name: getMappingName
functions.description: Returns the mapping name (/TM). If absent, falls back to the alternative name, then to the partial name.

functions.name: getValue
functions.description: Returns the current field value (/V) as a QPDFObjectHandle, or a null/empty handle if not present.

functions.name: getValueAsString
functions.description: Returns the current field value (/V) as a string. If the field’s value is not a string, returns the empty string silently.

functions.name: getDefaultValue
functions.description: Returns the field’s default value (/DV) as a QPDFObjectHandle, or a null/empty handle if not present.

functions.name: getDefaultValueAsString
functions.description: Returns the field’s default value (/DV) as a string. If the default value is not a string, returns the empty string silently.

functions.name: getDefaultAppearance
functions.description: Returns the default appearance string (DA), considering inheritance and falling back to the document-level /AcroForm if not found. Returns the empty string if unavailable or if this is not a variable text field.

functions.name: getDefaultResources
functions.description: Returns the default resource dictionary (from the document-level /AcroForm dictionary). Notes mention that some readers ignore a /DR on the field itself.

functions.name: getQuadding
functions.description: Returns the text quadding (alignment) value, with inheritance and AcroForm fallback. Returns 0 if unspecified.

functions.name: getFlags
functions.description: Returns the field flags (/Ff) as a bitmask (logical OR of pdf_form_field_flag_e values defined in qpdf/Constants.h).

functions.name: isText
functions.description: Returns true if the field is of type /Tx (text field).

functions.name: isCheckbox
functions.description: Returns true if the field is of type /Btn and the flags indicate a checkbox (i.e., not radio and not pushbutton).

functions.name: isChecked
functions.description: Returns true if the field is a checkbox and it is currently checked.

functions.name: isRadioButton
functions.description: Returns true if the field is of type /Btn and flags indicate a radio button.

functions.name: isPushbutton
functions.description: Returns true if the field is of type /Btn and flags indicate a pushbutton.

functions.name: isChoice
functions.description: Returns true if the field is of type /Ch (choice: combo box or list box).

functions.name: getChoices
functions.description: Returns the display strings for the field’s choices (for /Ch fields) as UTF-8 strings.

functions.name: setFieldAttribute
functions.description: Sets an attribute on the field dictionary to the given value. If you need to set a field’s name, prefer QPDFAcroFormDocumentHelper::setFormFieldName.
requirements: key should be a field dictionary key without the leading slash, e.g., "FT", "DA" (inferred from naming).
value must be a QPDFObjectHandle suitable for the attribute being set (type should match PDF spec for that key).

functions.name: setFieldAttribute
functions.signature: void QPDFFormFieldObjectHelper::setFieldAttribute(std::string const& key, std::string const& utf8_value)
functions.description: Sets an attribute on the field dictionary to the given value encoded as a Unicode string (UTF-16BE in the PDF), taking a UTF-8 input string. If you need to set a field’s name, prefer QPDFAcroFormDocumentHelper::setFormFieldName.
requirements: utf8_value must be UTF-8 encoded.
key should be a field dictionary key without the leading slash.

functions.name: setV
functions.description: Sets the field’s value (/V) to the given object. If need_appearances is true and the field is /Tx (text) or /Ch (choice), sets document-level /NeedAppearances to true unless you plan to generate an appearance stream yourself. For /Btn fields (checkboxes, radio buttons, pushbuttons), special handling applies: for checkboxes, any value other than /Off is treated as on, and the stored /V may be adjusted to match the appearance stream’s /N dictionary.
requirements: If you will generate your own appearance stream, pass need_appearances=false to avoid setting /NeedAppearances (per comment).
For checkbox fields, callers should not rely on the exact name they pass being preserved; the implementation may map it to an existing appearance name.

functions.name: setV
functions.signature: void QPDFFormFieldObjectHelper::setV(std::string const& utf8_value, bool need_appearances = true)
functions.description: Sets the field’s value (/V) to the given string, encoding it as a Unicode string. Input must be UTF-8. See setV(QPDFObjectHandle, ...) for /NeedAppearances behavior and button-specific notes.
requirements: utf8_value must be UTF-8 encoded.
If you will generate your own appearance stream, pass need_appearances=false to avoid setting /NeedAppearances.

functions.name: generateAppearance
functions.description: Generates or updates the appearance stream for this field’s widget annotation. qpdf’s generator currently supports only text (/Tx) and choice (/Ch) fields; it uses default parameters and supports ASCII characters only. Quadding is ignored. Intended to refresh the field’s visual appearance when you have set a value.
requirements: annotation should reference the widget annotation associated with this field (inferred from parameter type and purpose).
Appearance generation is limited to text and choice fields; for other types, callers should not expect an appearance to be generated.

functions.name: QPDFJob::QPDFJob
functions.description: Constructs a QPDFJob object used to configure and run high-level qpdf operations similar to the qpdf CLI.
requirements: No arguments.
Object starts with default logger (global) unless overridden via setLogger() or getLogger().
Further configuration is required before run() to perform any action.

functions.name: QPDFJob::initializeFromArgv
functions.signature: void QPDFJob::initializeFromArgv(char const* const argv[], char const* progname_env = nullptr)
functions.description: Initializes this QPDFJob from a null-terminated argv array of null-terminated UTF-8 strings, mirroring qpdf CLI parsing. Optionally uses the progname_env environment variable to override the executable name for completion generation. Throws QPDFUsage (derived from std::runtime_error) on usage-like errors; may throw other exceptions. Mutates the provided arguments.
requirements: argv must be a null-terminated array of pointers to null-terminated UTF-8 encoded C strings.
On Windows wmain callers should convert to UTF-8 before calling (see QUtil::call_main_from_wmain).
progname_env may be nullptr or the name of an environment variable to override program name.
Caller must be prepared to handle QPDFUsage and possibly other exceptions.
Arguments passed may be mutated by this function.

functions.name: QPDFJob::initializeFromJson
functions.signature: void QPDFJob::initializeFromJson(std::string const& json, bool partial = false)
functions.description: Initializes this QPDFJob from a JSON specification conforming to qpdf's job JSON schema. If partial is true, final validation is deferred so multiple JSON fragments or a mix of CLI and JSON can be combined. Throws QPDFUsage on configuration errors; some error messages may be CLI-centric.
requirements: json must be a valid JSON string matching the expected QPDFJob schema (version-specific).
If partial is false, the configuration must be self-contained and valid; otherwise QPDFUsage is thrown.
Caller must be prepared to handle QPDFUsage exceptions.
When using multiple partial initializations, caller must later invoke checkConfiguration() (directly or via run()).

functions.name: QPDFJob::setMessagePrefix
functions.description: Sets the prefix used for verbose/progress and other messages emitted by this job (defaults to "qpdf").
requirements: Prefix string should be a short human-readable label; no specific format is required.

functions.name: QPDFJob::getMessagePrefix
functions.description: Returns the current message prefix used for job-emitted messages.
requirements: Callable at any time; returns the last value set (or the default "qpdf").

functions.name: QPDFJob::getLogger
functions.description: Returns the logger associated with this job. By default, jobs share the global logger. Configure the returned logger to capture or redirect output.
requirements: If a custom logger is desired per job, call setLogger() with a new logger; otherwise this returns the shared global logger.
Any configuration changes made on the returned logger affect this job (and any others sharing that logger).

functions.name: QPDFJob::setLogger
functions.description: Associates a custom logger with this job. The logger is also passed to QPDF objects subsequently created by this job.
requirements: The shared_ptr<QPDFLogger> must point to a valid logger instance; behavior with null is unknown.
Configure the logger (streams, filtering, etc.) via QPDFLogger APIs after setting it here if needed.

functions.name: QPDFJob::setOutputStreams
functions.description: Deprecated: configures a private logger for this job and sets its output/error streams. Superseded by getLogger()/setLogger().
requirements: This method is deprecated; prefer configuring a logger via getLogger() or setLogger().
out_stream and err_stream should be valid std::ostream pointers; behavior with nullptr is not specified.
Be aware this may not capture all output (historical limitation).

functions.name: QPDFJob::registerProgressReporter
functions.description: Registers a callback invoked by QPDFWriter to report progress when progress reporting is enabled via configuration.
requirements: The callable must accept a single int parameter (progress value).
The callback is only invoked if progress reporting is enabled via configuration (e.g., --progress or corresponding config).
The callable should be thread-safe and non-throwing; exception behavior is unspecified.

functions.name: QPDFJob::checkConfiguration
functions.description: Validates the current configuration and throws QPDFUsage on any contradictions or missing required options. Called automatically after initialization and by run().
requirements: Caller should be prepared to handle QPDFUsage exceptions.
May be called manually any time after setting configuration.

functions.name: QPDFJob::createsOutput
functions.description: Returns true if the current job configuration results in creation of an output artifact (e.g., a file).
requirements: No special requirements; reflects current configuration state.

functions.name: QPDFJob::AttConfig::endAddAttachment
functions.description: Ends an add-attachment configuration block and returns the parent Config to continue fluent configuration.
requirements: Must be called after configuring the desired attachment parameters via AttConfig methods such as file() and others included from auto_job_c_att.hh.
Attachment parameters must form a valid combination; invalid combinations will ultimately be rejected during configuration checking.

functions.name: QPDFJob::AttConfig::file
functions.description: Sets the attachment file path (or related parameter) for the current attachment being added. Continues the AttConfig fluent interface.
requirements: parameter should be a valid filesystem path to the file to attach.
Must be called within an active addAttachment() configuration block before endAddAttachment().

functions.name: QPDFJob::CopyAttConfig::endCopyAttachmentsFrom
functions.description: Ends a copy-attachments-from configuration block and returns the parent Config to continue configuration.
requirements: Must be called after specifying required parameters (e.g., file()) in this block.
Invalid or incomplete parameters will cause configuration validation errors later.

functions.name: QPDFJob::CopyAttConfig::file
functions.description: Specifies a source file from which to copy attachments in the current copy-attachments-from configuration block.
requirements: parameter should be a valid filesystem path to the source PDF.
Call within an active copyAttachmentsFrom() block before endCopyAttachmentsFrom().

functions.name: QPDFJob::PagesConfig::endPages
functions.description: Ends a pages selection/assembly configuration block and returns the parent Config.
requirements: Call after specifying desired page selections via PagesConfig methods (e.g., pageSpec(), options from auto_job_c_pages.hh).

functions.name: QPDFJob::PagesConfig::pageSpec
functions.signature: QPDFJob::PagesConfig* QPDFJob::PagesConfig::pageSpec(std::string const& filename, std::string const& range, char const* password = nullptr)
functions.description: Adds a page specification from filename with the given page range (and optional password). From qpdf 11.9.0, file(), range(), and password() may be called; each call to file() starts a new page spec. This helper combines them in one call.
requirements: filename should point to an accessible PDF file.
range must be a valid page range string understood by qpdf (specific syntax not documented here).
password may be nullptr or a valid password if the source is encrypted.
Use within a pages() configuration block; each invocation contributes to the selection.

functions.name: QPDFJob::UOConfig::endUnderlayOverlay
functions.description: Ends an underlay/overlay configuration block and returns the parent Config for continued configuration.
requirements: Call after specifying underlay/overlay parameters via UOConfig methods (from auto_job_c_uo.hh).

functions.name: QPDFJob::EncConfig::endEncrypt
functions.description: Ends an encryption configuration block and returns the parent Config.
requirements: Call after setting encryption parameters via EncConfig methods (from auto_job_c_enc.hh).
Encryption settings must be consistent and valid; otherwise validation will fail.

functions.name: QPDFJob::EncConfig::file
functions.description: Specifies an input file (or related parameter) for an encryption configuration block, typically to read additional settings from a file.
requirements: parameter should be a valid filesystem path. The exact semantics depend on EncConfig options (details in generated header auto_job_c_enc.hh).
Use within an active encrypt() block before endEncrypt().

functions.name: QPDFJob::PageLabelsConfig::endSetPageLabels
functions.description: Ends a page-labels configuration block and returns the parent Config.
requirements: Call after specifying page label settings via methods from auto_job_c_set_page_labels.hh.

functions.name: QPDFJob::GlobalConfig::endGlobal
functions.description: Ends a global-options configuration block and returns the parent Config.
requirements: Use within a global() configuration session; ensure options set are valid in combination.

functions.name: QPDFJob::Config::checkConfiguration
functions.description: Proxy to QPDFJob::checkConfiguration(); validates that the current configuration is consistent and complete. Throws QPDFUsage on errors.
requirements: Caller must handle QPDFUsage exceptions on invalid configuration.

functions.name: QPDFJob::Config::inputFile
functions.description: Specifies the primary input filename for the job.
requirements: filename should be a valid path to a readable input PDF.
Must not conflict with emptyInput(); contradictory options will be rejected during validation.

functions.name: QPDFJob::Config::emptyInput
functions.description: Configures the job to start with an empty input (no initial file).
requirements: Should not be used together with inputFile(); contradictory options will be rejected.

functions.name: QPDFJob::Config::outputFile
functions.description: Specifies the output filename for the job.
requirements: filename should be a valid path; the process must have permission to create/overwrite the file if applicable.
If replaceInput() is used, semantics follow CLI behavior (overwriting input).

functions.name: QPDFJob::Config::replaceInput
functions.description: Indicates that the input file should be replaced by the output (in-place replacement semantics similar to CLI).
requirements: Requires that an input file be specified; behavior with emptyInput() is invalid.
Caller must ensure permissions allow replacing the input file.

functions.name: QPDFJob::Config::setPageLabels
functions.description: Sets page label specifications for the output document.
requirements: specs must contain strings in the page label specification format expected by qpdf (exact syntax not documented here).

functions.name: QPDFJob::Config::copyAttachmentsFrom
functions.description: Begins a block for specifying copying of attachments from another file. Returns a builder for that block.
requirements: Follow with CopyAttConfig methods (e.g., file(), options included from auto_job_c_copy_att.hh) and finish with endCopyAttachmentsFrom().

functions.name: QPDFJob::Config::addAttachment
functions.description: Begins an add-attachment block for attaching a file to the output. Returns a builder for that block.
requirements: Follow with AttConfig methods (e.g., file(), metadata options from auto_job_c_att.hh) and finish with endAddAttachment().

functions.name: QPDFJob::Config::global
functions.description: Begins a global-options configuration block and returns a builder for setting global options.
requirements: Finish the block with GlobalConfig::endGlobal() before running the job.

functions.name: QPDFJob::Config::pages
functions.description: Begins a pages selection/assembly configuration block and returns a builder for specifying page sources and ranges.
requirements: Use PagesConfig methods such as pageSpec() (and those in auto_job_c_pages.hh) and finish with endPages().

functions.name: QPDFJob::Config::overlay
functions.description: Begins an overlay configuration block. Returns a builder for specifying overlay operations.
requirements: Configure overlay options via UOConfig methods and finish with endUnderlayOverlay().

functions.name: QPDFJob::Config::underlay
functions.description: Begins an underlay configuration block. Returns a builder for specifying underlay operations.
requirements: Configure underlay options via UOConfig methods and finish with endUnderlayOverlay().

functions.name: QPDFJob::Config::encrypt
functions.signature: std::shared_ptr<QPDFJob::EncConfig> QPDFJob::Config::encrypt(int keylen, std::string const& user_password, std::string const& owner_password)
functions.description: Begins an encryption configuration block with the specified key length and passwords. Returns a builder for further encryption settings.
requirements: keylen must be a supported encryption key length for qpdf (exact allowed values not specified here).
user_password and owner_password are UTF-8 strings; empty strings may be allowed per qpdf semantics (not specified here).
Finish with EncConfig::endEncrypt() before running the job.

functions.name: QPDFJob::config
functions.description: Returns a top-level configuration object for building a job via a fluent interface. Throws QPDFUsage if an invalid configuration is created (e.g., contradictory options).
requirements: Caller must handle QPDFUsage exceptions triggered by invalid configuration states.
Use returned Config to set all desired options before calling run() or createQPDF()/writeQPDF().

functions.name: QPDFJob::run
