functions.name: QPDFOutlineObjectHelper::getCount
functions.description: Returns the raw /Count value from the outline item, or 0 if not present. A positive value indicates the outline is open; a negative value indicates it is closed. The absolute value is the number of descendant items that would be visible if this item were open.
requirements: Call on a valid QPDFOutlineObjectHelper instance created by QPDFOutlineDocumentHelper.

functions.name: QPDFOutlineObjectHelper::getTitle
functions.description: Returns the outline item's title as a UTF-8 string. Returns an empty string if no title is present.
requirements: Call on a valid QPDFOutlineObjectHelper instance created by QPDFOutlineDocumentHelper.
Caller should handle the possibility of an empty string return value when no title exists.

functions.name: QPDFPageDocumentHelper::get
functions.description: Return a shared QPDFPageDocumentHelper associated with the given QPDF. Using this instead of constructing a new helper avoids repeated, expensive validation of the AcroForm/Pages structures. Typical usage: obtain once per QPDF and reuse for page-level operations.
requirements: qpdf must reference a valid, initialized QPDF document instance.
The returned reference remains valid as long as the underlying QPDF is valid; callers should not use the helper after the QPDF is destroyed.
Thread-safety and reentrancy are unknown; do not assume concurrent use is safe.

functions.name: QPDFPageDocumentHelper::validate
functions.description: Re-validate the document’s /Pages structure. If repair is true, attempts to repair issues discovered during validation. Use after modifying the pages tree to refresh/repair internal caches.
requirements: Call after any modification that may invalidate the cached Pages structure.
If repair is false, validation errors will not be repaired; behavior on irreparable errors is unknown (may throw or leave invalid state).
May be expensive on large documents; avoid unnecessary calls.

functions.name: QPDFPageDocumentHelper::QPDFPageDocumentHelper
functions.description: Construct a page document helper bound to the given QPDF. Prefer using QPDFPageDocumentHelper::get to share a validated helper and avoid repeated validation overhead.
requirements: qpdf must be a valid, initialized QPDF instance.
The helper operates on the referenced QPDF; ensure qpdf outlives the helper.
Creating multiple helpers for the same QPDF may duplicate validation work; prefer get() unless you explicitly need a distinct instance.

functions.name: QPDFPageDocumentHelper::getAllPages
functions.description: Traverse the PDF page tree and return a snapshot vector of all /Page objects as QPDFPageObjectHelper wrappers. The returned list is not kept in sync with the document; re-call after page insertions/removals to obtain an updated list.
requirements: Returned vector reflects the state at call time only; callers must re-fetch after modifying pages.
Each element represents a valid /Page object; do not assume subsequent edits to the document are reflected in these objects without re-acquiring them.

functions.name: QPDFPageDocumentHelper::pushInheritedAttributesToPage
functions.description: Resolve page-tree inheritance by explicitly setting inherited values onto each /Page dictionary. This simplifies subsequent page manipulation by eliminating reliance on inherited values.
requirements: Call before operations that require explicit page attributes (e.g., copying pages) to avoid surprises from inherited values.
No parameters; operates on all pages in the associated QPDF.

functions.name: QPDFPageDocumentHelper::removeUnreferencedResources
functions.description: For every page, remove resource entries that are not referenced by the page’s content streams. Delegates to QPDFPageObjectHelper::removeUnreferencedResources for each page.
requirements: Operates on all pages; ensure the document is in a consistent state before calling.
May modify page resource dictionaries; callers should not rely on unused resources remaining present.

functions.name: QPDFPageDocumentHelper::addPage
functions.description: Insert a page at the beginning (first=true) or end (first=false) of the document. If newpage originates from another QPDF, this function will first ensure inherited attributes are pushed in the source, then copy the page into this document, avoiding adding the exact same page object twice by making a shallow copy if needed. Be aware this method does not manage annotations/form fields linkage across documents.
requirements: newpage must wrap a valid /Page object.
If newpage comes from a different QPDF, the function will copy it into the current document; the exact object instance passed may not be the one inserted (a shallow copy may be created).
If you intend to further modify the inserted page, retrieve it again from this document after insertion.

This function does not handle shared annotations/form fields; after cross-document insertion, callers should invoke QPDFAcroFormDocumentHelper::fixCopiedAnnotations to avoid broken interactive features.
first controls position: true inserts at the beginning; false inserts at the end.

functions.name: QPDFPageDocumentHelper::addPageAt
functions.signature: void addPageAt(QPDFPageObjectHelper newpage, bool before, QPDFPageObjectHelper refpage);
functions.description: Insert newpage before (before=true) or after (before=false) the specified refpage. Behavior for cross-document pages is the same as addPage (copying and shallow-copy avoidance).
requirements: newpage must wrap a valid /Page object (can originate from this or another QPDF).
refpage must refer to a valid /Page in the current document’s page tree; inserting relative to a page not in this document is invalid (behavior otherwise unknown).
If newpage originates from another QPDF, annotations/form fields are not automatically fixed; callers should handle them (e.g., via QPDFAcroFormDocumentHelper::fixCopiedAnnotations).
If you plan to modify the inserted page, retrieve it again after insertion.
before controls relative position: true inserts before refpage; false inserts after.

functions.name: QPDFPageDocumentHelper::removePage
functions.description: Remove the specified page from the document’s page tree.
requirements: page must refer to a valid /Page that exists in the current document’s page tree.
Removing a page alters page indices; callers should refresh any cached page lists (e.g., via getAllPages()).
Effects on annotations/form fields tied to the removed page are not described; callers should verify and fix document-level structures as needed.

functions.name: QPDFPageDocumentHelper::flattenAnnotations
functions.signature: void flattenAnnotations(int required_flags = 0, int forbidden_flags = an_invisible | an_hidden);
functions.description: For each page annotation, render the annotation’s appearance stream into the page content, merge its resources into the page, and remove the annotation. Widget annotations tied to form fields are handled specially, and the /AcroForm key is removed from the catalog when appropriate. Flags filter which annotations are processed: only annotations with all required_flags set and none of the forbidden_flags set are flattened (semantics per QPDFAnnotationObjectHelper).
requirements: required_flags and forbidden_flags are bitmasks of annotation flags as defined for QPDFAnnotationObjectHelper; defaults flatten visible, non-hidden annotations.
Flattening modifies page content streams and resources and removes annotations; this is destructive and cannot be undone via this API.
After flattening, interactive form behavior may be removed (e.g., /AcroForm removed from catalog). Ensure this is acceptable before calling.

functions.name: QPDFPageLabelDocumentHelper::get
functions.description: Return a shared (cached) page-label document helper associated with the given QPDF. Using this instead of constructing a new helper avoids repeated validation of the /PageLabels structure and improves performance. Typical usage: call once per QPDF and reuse the returned reference.
requirements: qpdf must refer to a valid, initialized QPDF document object (inferred from purpose).
The returned reference remains valid only as long as the associated QPDF object remains alive (inferred from returning a reference to a helper tied to qpdf).
Thread-safety is unknown; avoid concurrent calls on the same QPDF unless the library guarantees it (unknown).

functions.name: QPDFPageLabelDocumentHelper::validate
functions.description: Validate the document’s /PageLabels structure again. If repair is true, attempt to repair the structure when validation finds errors. Use this after programmatically modifying the /PageLabels dictionary or number tree.
requirements: May modify the underlying document if repair is true; callers that require a non-mutating validation must pass repair = false.
The helper must be associated with a valid QPDF (constructed or obtained via get).
Calling order relative to other document mutations is up to the caller; ensure no concurrent modification during validation (unknown).

functions.name: QPDFPageLabelDocumentHelper::QPDFPageLabelDocumentHelper
functions.description: Construct a page-label document helper bound to the given QPDF. Prefer using get(QPDF&) to obtain a shared instance that reuses validation results; direct construction is available when explicit lifetime management is desired.
requirements: qpdf must be a valid, initialized QPDF document object at construction time.
The QPDF instance must outlive the helper instance (ownership/lifetime inferred from reference binding).
Constructing multiple helpers for the same QPDF may cause repeated validation overhead (not an error but a performance consideration).

functions.name: QPDFPageLabelDocumentHelper::hasPageLabels
functions.description: Return true if the document defines a /PageLabels dictionary, false otherwise.
requirements: The helper must be associated with a valid QPDF document.
Result depends on the current document state; if caller has modified /PageLabels without revalidation, call validate() first for up-to-date results (inferred from documentation).

functions.name: QPDFPageLabelDocumentHelper::pageLabelDict
functions.signature: static QPDFObjectHandle QPDFPageLabelDocumentHelper::pageLabelDict(qpdf_page_label_e label_type, int start_num, std::string_view prefix)
functions.description: Create and return a dictionary object suitable for insertion into a /PageLabels number tree. The dictionary may include /S (style), /St (starting number), and /P (prefix) as appropriate for the inputs.
requirements: label_type must be a valid qpdf_page_label_e value corresponding to PDF styles: /D, /R, /r, /A, or /a (per comment/spec).
start_num should be a positive integer (typically >= 1) as required by PDF /St semantics (inferred from spec note).
prefix may be any string; empty prefix is allowed to omit fixed text.
Returned QPDFObjectHandle must be inserted in the appropriate context (e.g., as a value in the /Nums array) by the caller; this function does not perform insertion.

functions.name: QPDFPageLabelDocumentHelper::getLabelForPage
functions.description: Return a page label dictionary that represents the label applicable to the specified page index. The page need not have an explicit entry; the method computes the effective label and adjusts /St as needed so the result is suitable for that page.
requirements: page_idx is a zero-based page index (per number tree description in comments).
page_idx must be within the document’s page count (0 <= page_idx < num_pages) to avoid undefined behavior (inferred).
The helper must be associated with a valid QPDF; call validate() if the /PageLabels structure may be out of date.

functions.name: QPDFPageLabelDocumentHelper::getLabelsForPageRange
functions.signature: void QPDFPageLabelDocumentHelper::getLabelsForPageRange(long long start_idx, long long end_idx, long long new_start_idx, std::vector<QPDFObjectHandle>& new_labels)
functions.description: Append to new_labels the entries needed for a /PageLabels /Nums array to represent labels for pages in the inclusive range [start_idx, end_idx] from the original document, mapped so that start_idx corresponds to new_start_idx in the destination. Produces suitable entries even if the source document has no page labels, enabling incremental construction while merging.
requirements: start_idx and end_idx are zero-based, inclusive page indexes in the source document (per comments).
start_idx must be <= end_idx (range semantics).
All indexes must be within valid page ranges of the respective documents: 0 <= start_idx <= end_idx < source_num_pages; new_start_idx >= 0 (inferred).
new_labels must be a valid vector reference; function appends to it and does not clear existing contents.
Callers should pass ranges consistent with how pages are copied or merged to ensure correct mapping of labels.

functions.name: QPDFPageObjectHelper::QPDFPageObjectHelper
functions.description: Constructs a helper bound to a given QPDFObjectHandle representing a page (and, for many APIs, also usable with a form XObject). Use this to perform page-related queries and transformations on the provided object.
requirements: obj must reference a valid PDF dictionary representing a page object; many methods also accept a form XObject, as documented per method.
If obj does not represent a compatible object for the called method, behavior is undefined by this header (unknown: exact validation performed).

functions.name: QPDFPageObjectHelper::getAttribute
functions.description: Returns the value of the requested page/form-XObject dictionary attribute, honoring page-tree inheritance for inheritable page keys (/MediaBox, /CropBox, /Resources, /Rotate). If copy_if_shared is true and the attribute is inherited or an indirect object shared with other pages/XObjects, a shallow copy is installed on this page/XObject and returned so that subsequent modifications affect only this object.
requirements: name identifies a key in the page or form XObject dictionary (unknown: whether it must include a leading slash).
If copy_if_shared is true, the page/form-XObject dictionary may be modified by inserting a shallow copy of the attribute.
Only page objects inherit attributes via the pages tree; form XObjects do not have inheritance.

functions.name: QPDFPageObjectHelper::getMediaBox
functions.description: Returns the effective /MediaBox for the page, considering inheritance in the pages tree. If copy_if_shared is true and the value is inherited or shared (indirect), a shallow copy is stored on this page and returned.
requirements: Applies to page objects; for form XObjects, this behaves as a direct attribute lookup without inheritance.
If copy_if_shared is true, the page dictionary may be modified by inserting a shallow copy of the box.

functions.name: QPDFPageObjectHelper::getCropBox
functions.description: Returns the effective /CropBox. If not present, falls back to /MediaBox. Inheritance is honored for /CropBox and /MediaBox on pages. If copy_if_shared is true, inherited or shared values are shallow-copied onto this page. If copy_if_fallback is true, a shallow copy is created at /CropBox if the value is obtained via fallback.
requirements: On pages, /CropBox and /MediaBox may be inherited; other boxes are not.
If copy_if_shared or copy_if_fallback is true, the page dictionary may be modified with shallow copies.

functions.name: QPDFPageObjectHelper::getBleedBox
functions.description: Returns the effective /BleedBox. If absent, falls back to the effective /CropBox. Inheritance (through /CropBox or /MediaBox) is applied only as part of the fallback chain on pages. copy_if_shared shallow-copies inherited/shared sources; copy_if_fallback creates a shallow copy at /BleedBox if the value is obtained via fallback.
requirements: /BleedBox itself is not inheritable; fallback may originate from inheritable boxes on pages.
If copy_if_shared or copy_if_fallback is true, the page dictionary may be modified with shallow copies.

functions.name: QPDFPageObjectHelper::getTrimBox
functions.description: Returns the effective /TrimBox. If absent, falls back to the effective /CropBox. Inheritance is considered on pages only via the fallback chain. copy_if_shared shallow-copies inherited/shared sources; copy_if_fallback creates a shallow copy at /TrimBox if the value is obtained via fallback.
requirements: /TrimBox is not inheritable; fallback may come from inheritable boxes on pages.
If copy_if_shared or copy_if_fallback is true, the page dictionary may be modified with shallow copies.

functions.name: QPDFPageObjectHelper::getArtBox
functions.description: Returns the effective /ArtBox. If absent, falls back to the effective /CropBox. Inheritance is considered on pages only via the fallback chain. copy_if_shared shallow-copies inherited/shared sources; copy_if_fallback creates a shallow copy at /ArtBox if the value is obtained via fallback.
requirements: /ArtBox is not inheritable; fallback may come from inheritable boxes on pages.
If copy_if_shared or copy_if_fallback is true, the page dictionary may be modified with shallow copies.

functions.name: QPDFPageObjectHelper::forEachXObject
functions.signature: void QPDFPageObjectHelper::forEachXObject(bool recursive, std::function<void(QPDFObjectHandle& obj, QPDFObjectHandle& xobj_dict, std::string const& key)> action, std::function<bool(QPDFObjectHandle)> selector)
functions.description: Iterates XObjects referenced by a page or form XObject, optionally recursing into nested form XObjects. Calls action for each selected XObject, passing the object, the containing /XObject dictionary, and the resource key. If selector is provided, only XObjects for which selector returns true are visited; otherwise all are visited.
requirements: action must be a valid callable; it will be invoked for each matching XObject.
selector may be null; if non-null it must safely handle any XObject encountered.
The /XObject resources dictionary and individual XObjects may be shared across pages; callers must account for shared references if they modify passed objects.

functions.name: QPDFPageObjectHelper::forEachImage
functions.signature: void QPDFPageObjectHelper::forEachImage(bool recursive, std::function<void(QPDFObjectHandle& obj, QPDFObjectHandle& xobj_dict, std::string const& key)> action)
functions.description: Iterates only image XObjects referenced by this page or form XObject, optionally recursing into nested form XObjects. Invokes action with the image object, containing resource dictionary, and resource key.
requirements: action must be a valid callable.
If recursive is true, traversal descends into form XObjects contained within this page/XObject.

functions.name: QPDFPageObjectHelper::forEachFormXObject
functions.signature: void QPDFPageObjectHelper::forEachFormXObject(bool recursive, std::function<void(QPDFObjectHandle& obj, QPDFObjectHandle& xobj_dict, std::string const& key)> action)
functions.description: Iterates only form XObjects referenced by this page or form XObject, optionally recursing into nested form XObjects. Invokes action with the form object, containing resource dictionary, and resource key.
requirements: action must be a valid callable.
If recursive is true, traversal descends into nested form XObjects.

functions.name: QPDFPageObjectHelper::getImages
functions.description: Returns a map from XObject resource name to image object (always a stream) directly referenced by this page or form XObject. Supports inherited resources. Does not recurse into nested form XObjects; use forEachImage for recursion.
requirements: Returns an empty map if there are no images or no resources present.

functions.name: QPDFPageObjectHelper::getPageImages
functions.description: Deprecated alias that calls getImages(). Returns a map of directly referenced image XObjects for this page or form XObject.
requirements: Same requirements and behavior as getImages().

functions.name: QPDFPageObjectHelper::getFormXObjects
functions.description: Returns a map from resource key to form XObject directly referenced by this page or form XObject. Does not recurse into nested form XObjects; use forEachFormXObject to recurse.
requirements: Returns an empty map if there are no form XObjects or no resources present.

functions.name: QPDFPageObjectHelper::externalizeInlineImages
functions.description: Converts inline images in the page’s or form XObject’s content streams to external image XObjects if the inline image’s encoded size is at least min_size bytes. By default, nested form XObjects are processed; pass shallow=true to avoid recursion.
requirements: min_size is a non-negative size threshold (size_t).
If shallow is false, nested form XObjects will be processed recursively; set shallow=true to restrict to the current object only.

functions.name: QPDFPageObjectHelper::getAnnotations
functions.description: Returns annotations in the page’s /Annots array. If only_subtype is non-empty, only annotations with that subtype are included.
requirements: Call only on page objects (annotations are page-level; behavior on form XObjects is not described).
only_subtype filtering uses the subtype name as stored in annotation dictionaries (unknown: formatting of subtype string).

functions.name: QPDFPageObjectHelper::getPageContents
functions.description: Returns a vector of stream objects representing the page’s content streams, abstracting whether the page uses a single stream or an array of streams.
requirements: Call on a page object (also works for form XObjects where applicable).
Returned handles correspond to streams in the page’s Contents.

functions.name: QPDFPageObjectHelper::addPageContents
functions.description: Adds the given object as a new content stream for this page, inserting at the beginning if first is true, otherwise at the end. If the current Contents is a single stream, it is automatically converted to an array as needed.
requirements: contents must be a stream object to be valid as a content stream.
This modifies the page’s Contents; callers may coalesce afterwards with coalesceContentStreams() if a single stream is desired.

functions.name: QPDFPageObjectHelper::rotatePage
functions.description: Sets or adjusts the page’s /Rotate value. If relative is false, sets rotation to angle. If relative is true, adds angle to the existing rotation. Angle must be a multiple of 90; adding 90 rotates clockwise by 90 degrees.
requirements: angle must be a multiple of 90.
This operation modifies the page dictionary’s /Rotate value.

functions.name: QPDFPageObjectHelper::coalesceContentStreams
functions.description: If the page’s Contents is an array of streams, concatenates them into a single stream. Useful for normalizing fragmented streams (e.g., split mid-token) or after adding additional content streams.
requirements: Operates on the current page (also applicable to form XObjects where supported by the implementation).
Modifies the page’s Contents to a single stream when it was an array.

functions.name: QPDFPageObjectHelper::parseContents
functions.description: Parses the contents of a page or form XObject and delivers parse events to the provided ParserCallbacks, regardless of whether the contents is a single stream or an array.
requirements: callbacks must be a valid, non-null pointer for receiving parser events.
Callable on pages and form XObjects.

functions.name: QPDFPageObjectHelper::parsePageContents
functions.description: Deprecated alias for parseContents(). Parses the page or form XObject contents and invokes ParserCallbacks.
requirements: callbacks must be a valid, non-null pointer.
Same behavior as parseContents().

functions.name: QPDFPageObjectHelper::filterContents
functions.description: Runs the page’s or form XObject’s contents through the provided TokenFilter. If next is provided, it is used as the output target for the filter’s write methods; otherwise, any output generated by the filter is discarded. This does not automatically modify the page’s contents; use addContentTokenFilter to apply a filter to contents.
requirements: filter must be a valid, non-null pointer.
next may be null; if null, filter output is discarded.
Does not mutate the underlying page contents unless separately applied by other APIs.

functions.name: QPDFPageObjectHelper::filterPageContents
functions.description: Deprecated alias that calls filterContents(). Passes contents through the given TokenFilter and optionally to next pipeline.
requirements: filter must be non-null.
next may be null.

functions.name: QPDFPageObjectHelper::pipeContents
functions.description: Pipes the page’s or form XObject’s contents into the provided pipeline, handling both single and multiple content streams.
requirements: p must be a valid, non-null Pipeline pointer.
Does not modify page contents.

functions.name: QPDFPageObjectHelper::pipePageContents
functions.description: Deprecated alias for pipeContents(). Sends page or form XObject contents to the given pipeline.
requirements: p must be non-null.

functions.name: QPDFPageObjectHelper::addContentTokenFilter
functions.description: Attaches a token filter to the page’s or form XObject’s contents. If the contents is an array of streams, it is automatically coalesced into a single stream; the filter is then applied to that single stream.
requirements: token_filter must be a valid, non-null shared_ptr.
May coalesce multiple content streams into one as part of applying the filter.
This operation modifies how contents are filtered/serialized.

functions.name: QPDFPageObjectHelper::removeUnreferencedResources
functions.description: Analyzes the page’s or form XObject’s content streams to determine which resources are referenced, then removes any unreferenced entries from the Resources dictionary. Designed to work after pushing inherited attributes to pages and recurses into form XObjects.
requirements: Call on a page or form XObject with a Resources dictionary; if absent, the method becomes a no-op.
Modifies the Resources dictionary by removing unreferenced entries.

functions.name: QPDFPageObjectHelper::shallowCopyPage
functions.description: Creates and returns a new page object that is a shallow duplicate of this page. The returned page is an indirect object not inserted into any document structure. Content streams and indirect resources are shared with the original; copy components explicitly before modifying if you require independence.
requirements: Call on a page object.
The returned page must be added to a document via QPDF/QPDFPageDocumentHelper addPage APIs to appear in a pages tree.
If you plan to modify shared components, perform appropriate copying first to avoid affecting the source page.

functions.name: QPDFPageObjectHelper::getMatrixForTransformations
functions.description: Computes a transformation matrix whose effect matches the page’s /Rotate and /UserUnit, using the page’s TrimBox as the bounding box. If invert is true, returns the inverse matrix suitable for placing content onto this page while canceling its transformations.
requirements: Call on a page object; uses /TrimBox and any /Rotate and /UserUnit present.
If invert is true, the returned matrix represents the inverse of the page’s transformation.

functions.name: QPDFPageObjectHelper::getFormXObjectForPage
functions.description: Creates and returns a form XObject that draws this page. The new object contains shallow copies of relevant page dictionaries and coalesced content streams, and is not referenced in any resources or pages. If handle_transformations is true, the form XObject’s /Matrix is set to replicate the page’s /Rotate and /UserUnit so placement preserves original appearance.
requirements: Call on a page object.
Returned form XObject is unreferenced; insert it into a Resources dictionary and place it via content stream operators to use it.
Shallow copies imply shared indirect objects; copy components if you need isolation before editing.

functions.name: QPDFPageObjectHelper::placeFormXObject
functions.signature: std::string QPDFPageObjectHelper::placeFormXObject(QPDFObjectHandle fo, std::string const& name, QPDFObjectHandle::Rectangle rect, bool invert_transformations, bool allow_shrink, bool allow_expand)
functions.description: Returns content stream text to place the given form XObject fo, referenced by resource name name, centered within rect on this page, optionally inverting the page’s own /Rotate and /UserUnit so the placed form maintains absolute orientation. allow_shrink and allow_expand control whether the form may be scaled down to fit or up to fill the rectangle (defaults chosen for backward compatibility).
requirements: fo must be a form XObject object handle and should be present in this page’s Resources under the specified name before executing the returned content stream.
name must be a valid resource key for the form XObject in the page’s /Resources/XObject dictionary.
rect specifies the destination rectangle on the page.
If invert_transformations is true, the page’s rotation/scaling are inverted for placement.

functions.name: QPDFPageObjectHelper::getMatrixForFormXObjectPlacement
functions.signature: QPDFMatrix QPDFPageObjectHelper::getMatrixForFormXObjectPlacement(QPDFObjectHandle fo, QPDFObjectHandle::Rectangle rect, bool invert_transformations, bool allow_shrink, bool allow_expand)
functions.description: Computes and returns the transformation matrix mapping coordinates from the given form XObject fo into the specified rect on this page. Parameters have the same meaning as in placeFormXObject.
requirements: fo must be a form XObject handle.
rect defines the destination rectangle on the page.
invert_transformations, allow_shrink, and allow_expand control handling of page transformations and scaling like placeFormXObject.

functions.name: QPDFPageObjectHelper::flattenRotation
functions.description: Converts page rotation specified by /Rotate into content transformations, adjusts all page bounding boxes to preserve semantics, and removes /Rotate. If an AcroForm helper is provided, it is used to resolve and rotate any associated form fields; otherwise an internal helper is created (less efficient).
requirements: Call on a page object with /Rotate if you wish to flatten rotation; safe to call regardless.
If afdh is non-null, it must remain valid for the duration of the call.
This operation modifies content streams, page boxes, and removes /Rotate.

functions.name: QPDFPageObjectHelper::copyAnnotations
functions.signature: void QPDFPageObjectHelper::copyAnnotations(QPDFPageObjectHelper from_page, QPDFMatrix const& cm, QPDFAcroFormDocumentHelper* afdh, QPDFAcroFormDocumentHelper* from_afdh)
functions.description: Copies annotations from from_page onto this page, transforming each annotation’s rectangle by cm. Widget annotations and their form fields are copied into this document’s AcroForm dictionary. Supports copying from pages converted to form XObjects for overlay/underlay workflows. May use provided AcroForm helpers for efficiency and correctness when resolving fields.
requirements: from_page must be a valid page helper from the same or a different QPDF document.
cm defines the coordinate transformation from the source page to this page.
If afdh or from_afdh are provided, they must remain valid for the duration of the call; otherwise helpers will be created internally (less efficient).
After copying, run QPDFAcroFormDocumentHelper::fixCopiedAnnotations if you copied a page and need destination annotations to be independent, as suggested by the header comments.

functions.name: JSON::unparse
functions.description: Serializes this JSON object to a compact JSON string. Typical use is to obtain a textual representation for logging, storage, or transmission. Details of formatting (e.g., whitespace) are internal to the implementation.
requirements: Object should be a valid JSON instance (any type).
Caller must handle the returned string; function does not throw per header, error behavior is unknown.

functions.name: JSON::write
functions.signature: void JSON::write(Pipeline* p, size_t depth = 0) const
functions.description: Writes this JSON object to the provided Pipeline, supporting incremental/pretty output using the supplied depth for indentation. Use when streaming JSON to an output sink.
requirements: p must be a valid, non-null Pipeline* that accepts writes.
depth should reflect the current nesting level when producing multi-part output; 0 is suitable for top-level writes.
The Pipeline will be finished by JSON at appropriate times; callers should not call finish() for blob payloads written via JSON blobs (see makeBlob).

functions.name: JSON::writeDictionaryOpen
functions.signature: static void JSON::writeDictionaryOpen(Pipeline* p, bool& first, size_t depth = 0)
functions.description: Incrementally writes the opening delimiter for a JSON dictionary (“{”), formatted for the given depth, and initializes the per-container first-item state. Use when streaming a dictionary piece-by-piece.
requirements: p must be non-null.
Pass a fresh bool first for each container; this method ignores its current value and sets it for the new container lifecycle.
depth should be the container’s depth (parent depth + 1 for nested containers).

functions.name: JSON::writeArrayOpen
functions.signature: static void JSON::writeArrayOpen(Pipeline* p, bool& first, size_t depth = 0)
functions.description: Incrementally writes the opening delimiter for a JSON array (“[”), formatted for the given depth, and initializes the per-container first-item state.
requirements: p must be non-null.
Pass a fresh bool first for each container; this method ignores its current value and sets it for the new container lifecycle.
depth should be the container’s depth (parent depth + 1 for nested containers).

functions.name: JSON::writeDictionaryClose
functions.signature: static void JSON::writeDictionaryClose(Pipeline* p, bool first, size_t depth = 0)
functions.description: Incrementally writes the closing delimiter for a JSON dictionary (“}”) with indentation at the specified depth. Does not modify the first flag; a true value indicates an empty dictionary was closed.
requirements: p must be non-null.
first must be the same flag used for the container’s items; its value is used only to determine formatting of empty containers.
depth must match the one used for the corresponding open call.

functions.name: JSON::writeArrayClose

functions.name: JSON::writeDictionaryItem

functions.description: Writes a single "key": value pair to an open dictionary being streamed incrementally. Handles comma placement via the first flag and applies indentation based on depth.
requirements: p must be non-null.
first must be the per-container flag; this method uses it to determine comma placement and then sets it to false.

depth should be one greater than the depth of the dictionary open/close calls when writing nested structures.

functions.name: JSON::writeDictionaryKey

functions.description: Writes just the quoted key and separating colon for the next dictionary item during incremental output. It calls writeNext internally, making it suitable before writing a nested container as the value.
requirements: p must be non-null.
first must be the per-container flag; this method will update it and handle comma insertion.
key should be valid UTF-8.
Use this when you intend to immediately write a nested value (e.g., open a nested array/dictionary) at depth one greater than the parent.

functions.name: JSON::writeArrayItem
functions.signature: static void JSON::writeArrayItem(Pipeline* p, bool& first, JSON const& element, size_t depth = 0)
functions.description: Writes a single array element to an open array being streamed incrementally. Handles comma placement via the first flag and uses depth for indentation. Calls writeNext internally for nested elements.
requirements: p must be non-null.
first must be the per-container flag; this method uses it to determine comma placement and then sets it to false.
depth should be one greater than the array’s open/close calls when writing nested structures.

functions.name: JSON::writeNext
functions.signature: static void JSON::writeNext(Pipeline* p, bool& first, size_t depth = 0)
functions.description: Used when incrementally writing nested structures: emits any needed comma/whitespace for the parent container before starting a child container. Call with the parent’s first flag and the child’s depth.
requirements: p must be non-null.
first must be the parent container’s flag; this method updates it to false for subsequent items.
depth should correspond to the nested child container’s depth (parent depth + 1).

functions.name: JSON::Reactor::arrayStart

functions.name: JSON::Reactor::dictionaryItem
functions.signature: virtual bool JSON::Reactor::dictionaryItem(std::string const& key, JSON const& value) = 0
functions.description: Called when a dictionary item is encountered. If it returns true, the item is considered consumed and will not be added to the in-memory JSON, enabling streaming of large inputs. Note: when the value is a container, this callback is invoked with an empty container before its start callback.

functions.name: JSON::Reactor::arrayItem

functions.name: QUtil::random

lines: output list to be filled (existing contents are preserved/overwritten behavior not specified)
preserve_eol: when true, retain line endings

functions.name: QUtil::is_hex_digit

functions.name: QUtil::is_space

functions.name: QUtil::is_digit

requirements: c: any char

functions.name: QUtil::is_number
functions.description: Return true if s represents a number according to qpdf’s tokenizer rules.
requirements: s: non‑null, null‑terminated C string; exact accepted syntax is library‑defined

functions.name: QUtil::handle_result_code
functions.description: Internal helper: examine a qpdf_result_e and throw std::logic_error if it equals qpdf_bad_parameter, embedding context in the message. Otherwise, return normally.

functions.name: QUtil::parse_numrange
functions.signature: std::vector<int> QUtil::parse_numrange(char const* range, int max)
functions.description: Parse the qpdf numeric range syntax into a sequence of integers, supporting single values, ranges, 'z' for max, 'r<n>' for from‑end, and exclusion groups with 'x'. May throw std::runtime_error on invalid syntax.
requirements: range: non‑null C string containing the range expression
max: integer providing the value for 'z' and the base for 'r<n>' semantics; must be consistent with intended domain (exact constraints not specified)
Caller must be prepared to catch std::runtime_error on parse errors

functions.name: QUtil::call_main_from_wmain

argc: non‑negative
argv: array of UTF‑16 strings
realmain: callable entry point expecting const argv

functions.name: QUtil::get_max_memory_usage
functions.description: Return the maximum memory usage observed for the current process/threads if detectable; otherwise 0. Linux‑specific, best‑effort, intended for development/performance testing.
requirements: Platform support and accuracy are limited; do not rely on for production measurements

functions.name: QPDFCryptoProvider::getImpl
functions.description: Return an instance of a crypto provider using the default implementation. Use when you want the current default crypto backend without caring which provider it is. Not thread-safe per class documentation.
requirements: Caller must ensure no concurrent calls to provider registration/lookup methods occur (these methods are not thread-safe).
A default provider must be configured or available; exact behavior if none is set is unknown from this header.

functions.name: QPDFCryptoProvider::getImpl
functions.description: Return an instance of the crypto provider registered under the given name. Use to obtain a specific registered crypto implementation by its registration key. Not thread-safe per class documentation.
requirements: Caller must ensure no concurrent calls to provider registration/lookup methods occur (these methods are not thread-safe).
The provided name must correspond to a previously registered provider; behavior if the name is unknown is not specified in this header.
Argument 'name' must remain valid for the duration of the call (passed as const reference).

functions.name: QPDFCryptoProvider::registerImpl
functions.signature: static void QPDFCryptoProvider::registerImpl(std::string const& name, QPDFCryptoProvider::provider_fn f);
functions.description: Register a crypto implementation under the given name using a provider function. The provider function must create and return a std::shared_ptr to an instance derived from QPDFCryptoImpl. Use this to plug in custom crypto backends. Not thread-safe per class documentation.
requirements: Caller must ensure no concurrent calls to provider registration/lookup methods occur (these methods are not thread-safe).
Argument 'name' must remain valid for the duration of the call (passed as const reference).
The provider function 'f' must be callable with no arguments and return std::shared_ptr<QPDFCryptoImpl>.
The returned instance from 'f' must be of a type derived from QPDFCryptoImpl.
Behavior on duplicate registration of the same name is not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: QPDFCryptoProvider::registerImpl
functions.signature: template <typename T> static void QPDFCryptoProvider::registerImpl(std::string const& name);
functions.description: Template helper to register type T as a crypto implementation under the given name. T must derive from QPDFCryptoImpl and have a default (no-argument) constructor. Internally registers a provider function that constructs std::make_shared<T>(). Not thread-safe per class documentation.
requirements: Caller must ensure no concurrent calls to provider registration/lookup methods occur (these methods are not thread-safe).
Template parameter T must be derived from QPDFCryptoImpl.
Template parameter T must have a public constructor that takes no arguments.
Argument 'name' must remain valid for the duration of the call (passed as const reference).
Behavior on duplicate registration of the same name is not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: QPDFCryptoProvider::setDefaultProvider
functions.description: Set the crypto provider identified by 'name' as the default implementation used by getImpl(). Use to select which registered provider should be used by default. Not thread-safe per class documentation.
requirements: Caller must ensure no concurrent calls to provider registration/lookup methods occur (these methods are not thread-safe).
The provided name must correspond to a previously registered provider; otherwise behavior is not specified in this header (unknown).
Argument 'name' must remain valid for the duration of the call (passed as const reference).

functions.name: QPDFCryptoProvider::getRegisteredImpls
functions.description: Return the set of names of all currently registered crypto implementations. Useful for discovery or diagnostics. Not thread-safe per class documentation.
requirements: Caller must ensure no concurrent calls to provider registration/lookup methods occur (these methods are not thread-safe).

functions.name: QPDFCryptoProvider::getDefaultProvider
functions.description: Return the name of the current default crypto provider. Use to query which provider will be used by getImpl() without arguments. Not thread-safe per class documentation.
requirements: Caller must ensure no concurrent calls to provider registration/lookup methods occur (these methods are not thread-safe).
If no default has been set, what is returned is not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: QPDFCryptoImpl::QPDFCryptoImpl
functions.description: Default constructor for the QPDFCryptoImpl interface. Implementations of this abstract base class must supply concrete definitions for all pure virtual methods to provide cryptographic services to qpdf.
requirements: No arguments.
Object is abstract; cannot be instantiated directly unless all pure virtual methods are implemented by a derived class.

functions.name: QPDFCryptoImpl::~QPDFCryptoImpl
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the QPDFCryptoImpl interface to allow proper cleanup via base-class pointers.
requirements: Destructor must be virtual in derived classes implicitly; ensure derived implementations correctly release any allocated cryptographic context/resources in their destructors or in finalize methods.

functions.name: QPDFCryptoImpl::provideRandomData
functions.signature: virtual void QPDFCryptoImpl::provideRandomData(unsigned char* data, size_t len) = 0
functions.description: Fill the caller-provided buffer with cryptographically suitable random bytes. Used by qpdf to obtain random data.
requirements: data must point to a writable buffer of at least len bytes.
len may be zero; if nonzero, exactly len bytes must be written.
Implementation must not read from data; only write random bytes.

functions.name: QPDFCryptoImpl::MD5_init
functions.description: Initialize or reset the MD5 hashing context before hashing any data.
requirements: Call MD5_init before any MD5_update/MD5_finalize/MD5_digest for a new hash computation.
May be called multiple times to start new MD5 computations; each call resets the MD5 state.

functions.name: QPDFCryptoImpl::MD5_update
functions.signature: virtual void QPDFCryptoImpl::MD5_update(unsigned char const* data, size_t len) = 0
functions.description: Consume a block of input and update the MD5 hash state.
requirements: MD5_init must have been called prior to the first MD5_update of a computation.
data must point to at least len bytes of readable memory (can be null if len == 0).
May be called zero or more times before MD5_finalize.

functions.name: QPDFCryptoImpl::MD5_finalize
functions.description: Finalize the MD5 hash computation, performing any required padding. After finalization, the digest can be retrieved via MD5_digest.
requirements: MD5_init must have been called before finalizing.
No further MD5_update calls should be made after MD5_finalize for the current computation.
Call MD5_init again to start a new computation after finalization.

functions.name: QPDFCryptoImpl::MD5_digest
functions.description: Retrieve the 16-byte MD5 digest of the most recently finalized computation into the provided buffer.
requirements: MD5_finalize must have been called before MD5_digest.
The output parameter must be a writable buffer of 16 bytes (MD5_Digest).
Does not modify input data buffers; only writes the digest.

functions.name: QPDFCryptoImpl::SHA2_init
functions.description: Initialize or reset the SHA-2 hashing context for a given digest size specified in bits (e.g., 256/384/512).
requirements: bits must correspond to a SHA-2 variant supported by the implementation; exact accepted values are not specified in this header.
Call SHA2_init before any SHA2_update/SHA2_finalize/SHA2_digest for a new hash computation.
May be called multiple times to start new SHA-2 computations; each call resets the SHA-2 state.

functions.name: QPDFCryptoImpl::SHA2_update
functions.signature: virtual void QPDFCryptoImpl::SHA2_update(unsigned char const* data, size_t len) = 0
functions.description: Consume a block of input and update the SHA-2 hash state for the variant selected in SHA2_init.
requirements: SHA2_init must have been called prior to the first SHA2_update of a computation.
data must point to at least len bytes of readable memory (can be null if len == 0).
May be called zero or more times before SHA2_finalize.

functions.name: QPDFCryptoImpl::SHA2_finalize
functions.description: Finalize the SHA-2 hash computation, performing any required padding. After finalization, the digest can be retrieved via SHA2_digest.
requirements: SHA2_init must have been called before finalizing.
No further SHA2_update calls should be made after SHA2_finalize for the current computation.
Call SHA2_init again to start a new computation after finalization.

functions.name: QPDFCryptoImpl::SHA2_digest
functions.description: Return the digest of the most recently finalized SHA-2 computation. The exact format of the returned string (raw bytes vs. hex) is not specified here.
requirements: SHA2_finalize must have been called before SHA2_digest.
Returned string format is implementation-defined; callers must not assume hex or binary without consulting the implementation.

functions.name: QPDFCryptoImpl::RC4_init
functions.signature: virtual void QPDFCryptoImpl::RC4_init(unsigned char const* key_data, int key_len = -1) = 0
functions.description: Initialize the RC4 stream cipher context with the provided key. A key_len of -1 indicates key_data is a null-terminated string.
requirements: key_data must be a valid pointer to the key material.
If key_len == -1, key_data must reference a null-terminated byte string; otherwise, the key length is exactly key_len bytes.
Must be called before RC4_process/RC4_finalize.
Implementations must accept that RC4 is required for handling older PDFs (per header comment).

functions.name: QPDFCryptoImpl::RC4_process
functions.signature: virtual void QPDFCryptoImpl::RC4_process(unsigned char const* in_data, size_t len, unsigned char* out_data = nullptr) = 0
functions.description: Encrypt or decrypt len bytes using RC4. If out_data is null, processing occurs in place on the input buffer.
requirements: RC4_init must have been called before RC4_process.
in_data must point to at least len bytes of readable memory.
If out_data is not null, it must point to a writable buffer of at least len bytes.
If out_data is null (in-place), the memory referenced by in_data must be writable despite the const qualifier in the signature; callers must ensure the underlying buffer is mutable and not read-only.
len may be zero to perform no operation.

functions.name: QPDFCryptoImpl::RC4_finalize
functions.description: Finalize and release any resources associated with the RC4 context.
requirements: Should be called after finishing RC4 processing to clean up internal state.
No RC4_process calls should be made after finalization unless RC4_init is called again.

functions.name: QPDFCryptoImpl::rijndael_init
functions.signature: virtual void QPDFCryptoImpl::rijndael_init(bool encrypt, unsigned char const* key_data, size_t key_len, bool cbc_mode, unsigned char* cbc_block) = 0
functions.description: Initialize the Rijndael (AES) cipher context for encryption or decryption, optionally in CBC mode. The cbc_block is used for CBC mode chaining (IV/state).
requirements: encrypt selects operation: true for encryption, false for decryption.
key_data must point to key_len bytes of readable memory.
key_len must be a valid AES key size for the implementation; exact accepted values are not specified in this header.
cbc_mode selects block mode: true for CBC, false for ECB-like single-block processing.

cbc_block must point to a writable buffer of size rijndael_buf_size (16 bytes) when CBC mode is used; behavior/requirement when CBC is false is implementation-defined but the pointer is still provided by the caller.
Must be called before rijndael_process/rijndael_finalize.

functions.name: QPDFCryptoImpl::rijndael_process
functions.signature: virtual void QPDFCryptoImpl::rijndael_process(unsigned char* in_data, unsigned char* out_data) = 0
functions.description: Process one AES block using the initialized context, writing the result to out_data. In CBC mode, chaining uses/updates cbc_block internally.
requirements: rijndael_init must have been called before rijndael_process.
in_data must point to a readable buffer of size rijndael_buf_size (16 bytes).
out_data must point to a writable buffer of size rijndael_buf_size (16 bytes).
Caller must invoke this once per 16-byte block; buffering or partial blocks are not handled by this interface.

functions.name: QPDFCryptoImpl::rijndael_finalize
functions.description: Finalize and release resources associated with the Rijndael (AES) context.
requirements: Should be called after finishing all rijndael_process calls to clean up internal state.
No rijndael_process calls should be made after finalization unless rijndael_init is called again.

functions.name: RandomDataProvider::~RandomDataProvider
functions.description: Virtual destructor for RandomDataProvider. Enables safe deletion of derived instances via a base-class pointer and ensures proper cleanup of resources in subclasses. Usage: destroy a RandomDataProvider (typically a subclass instance) when it is no longer needed.
requirements: The object must be a valid, fully constructed RandomDataProvider (or subclass) instance when destroyed.
Do not access the object after the destructor has been called (no use-after-free).
If deleted through a base-class pointer, the dynamic type must be a subclass of RandomDataProvider with a correctly defined destructor.

functions.name: RandomDataProvider::provideRandomData
functions.signature: virtual void provideRandomData(unsigned char* data, size_t len) = 0;
functions.description: Pure virtual method that fills a caller-provided buffer with random data. Subclasses must implement this to supply len bytes of random data into data. Intended use: callers provide a writable buffer and request a specific number of random bytes. Strength/quality (e.g., cryptographic) is unspecified in this header.
requirements: Must be called on a valid, initialized instance of a subclass that implements this pure virtual method.
data must point to a writable buffer of at least len bytes.
len specifies the exact number of bytes the implementation should write to data.
Behavior for len == 0 is unspecified; callers should avoid passing zero length unless the implementation documents support.
The function does not return a status; implementations are expected to either fully populate the buffer or signal failure via exceptions or other documented mechanism (unspecified here).

functions.name: qpdf::global::limit_errors
functions.description: Returns the number of times a global limit was exceeded. Read-only counter for diagnostics/monitoring.
requirements: No input arguments required.
Read-only value; there is no corresponding setter.
May throw a C++ exception if the underlying qpdf_global_get_uint32 call fails (via QUtil::handle_result_code).

functions.name: qpdf::global::options::inspection_mode
functions.description: Gets whether restrictive inspection mode is currently enabled.
requirements: No input arguments required.
May throw a C++ exception if the underlying qpdf_global_get_uint32 call fails (via QUtil::handle_result_code).

functions.name: qpdf::global::options::inspection_mode
functions.description: Enables restrictive inspection mode when passed true. Passing false is not supported and is currently a no-op. Must be set before creating any QPDF object.
requirements: Call before any QPDF object is created for the setting to take effect.
Passing true enables inspection mode; passing false has no effect (no-op).
Affects global process-wide state.
May throw a C++ exception if the underlying qpdf_global_set_uint32 call fails (via QUtil::handle_result_code).

functions.name: qpdf::global::options::default_limits
functions.description: Returns whether optional default limits are currently enabled.
requirements: No input arguments required.
May throw a C++ exception if the underlying qpdf_global_get_uint32 call fails (via QUtil::handle_result_code).

functions.name: qpdf::global::options::default_limits
functions.description: Disables all optional default limits when passed false. Once disabled, optional default limits cannot be re-enabled. Passing true has no effect. Explicitly set limits remain unchanged; some safety-related limits cannot be disabled (only adjusted).
requirements: Passing false disables optional default limits and cannot be undone in the current process.
Passing true has no effect (no-op).
This call affects global process-wide state; ensure this is acceptable for all users in the process.
May throw a C++ exception if the underlying qpdf_global_set_uint32 call fails (via QUtil::handle_result_code).

functions.name: qpdf::global::limits::parser_max_nesting
functions.description: Gets the maximum nesting depth allowed while parsing objects. This safety limit cannot be disabled by default_limits(false).
requirements: No input arguments required.
May throw a C++ exception if the underlying qpdf_global_get_uint32 call fails (via QUtil::handle_result_code).

functions.name: qpdf::global::limits::parser_max_nesting
functions.description: Sets the maximum nesting depth allowed while parsing objects. This safety limit cannot be disabled by default limits.
requirements: value is an unsigned 32-bit integer; exact valid range is not documented (unknown).
May throw a C++ exception if the underlying qpdf_global_set_uint32 call fails (via QUtil::handle_result_code).

functions.name: qpdf::global::limits::parser_max_errors
functions.description: Gets the maximum number of errors permitted while parsing objects. A value of 0 means no maximum is imposed.
requirements: No input arguments required.
May throw a C++ exception if the underlying qpdf_global_get_uint32 call fails (via QUtil::handle_result_code).

functions.name: qpdf::global::limits::parser_max_errors
functions.description: Sets the maximum number of errors permitted while parsing objects. Set to 0 to impose no maximum.
requirements: value is an unsigned 32-bit integer; 0 means no maximum.
May throw a C++ exception if the underlying qpdf_global_set_uint32 call fails (via QUtil::handle_result_code).

functions.name: qpdf::global::limits::parser_max_container_size
functions.description: Gets the maximum number of top-level items allowed in a container when parsing with an undamaged xref table and parsable objects. Default is 4,294,967,295.
requirements: No input arguments required.
May throw a C++ exception if the underlying qpdf_global_get_uint32 call fails (via QUtil::handle_result_code).

functions.name: qpdf::global::limits::parser_max_container_size
functions.description: Sets the maximum number of top-level items allowed in a container when parsing with an undamaged xref table and parsable objects.
requirements: value is an unsigned 32-bit integer; exact valid range beyond type width is not documented (unknown).
May throw a C++ exception if the underlying qpdf_global_set_uint32 call fails (via QUtil::handle_result_code).

functions.name: qpdf::global::limits::parser_max_container_size_damaged
functions.description: Gets the maximum number of top-level items allowed in a container when the xref table or object is damaged, and when parsing xref streams. Default is 5,000.
requirements: No input arguments required.
May throw a C++ exception if the underlying qpdf_global_get_uint32 call fails (via QUtil::handle_result_code).

functions.name: qpdf::global::limits::parser_max_container_size_damaged
functions.description: Sets the maximum number of top-level items allowed in a container when the xref table or object is damaged; also applies when parsing trailer dictionaries and xref streams. Default is 5,000.
requirements: value is an unsigned 32-bit integer; exact valid range beyond type width is not documented (unknown).

functions.description: Gets the maximum number of filters permitted when decoding streams. If exceeded for a stream, that stream is treated as unfilterable. Default is 25.
requirements: No input arguments required.

requirements: value is an unsigned 32-bit integer; exact valid range beyond type width is not documented (unknown).
May throw a C++ exception if the underlying qpdf_global_set_uint32 call fails (via QUtil::handle_result_code).

functions.name: qpdf_silence_errors
functions.description: Signals that the caller will explicitly check for errors so the library won’t print error messages to stderr for functions that don’t return error codes. Use early after qpdf_init.

functions.name: qpdf_get_qpdf_version

functions.name: qpdf_init
functions.description: Allocates and returns a qpdf_data handle used for all subsequent operations.
requirements: The returned handle must be released with qpdf_cleanup

functions.name: qpdf_cleanup
functions.description: Frees resources associated with a qpdf_data handle and invalidates it. Does not free stream data buffers returned via malloc (free those separately).
requirements: *qpdf must be a handle previously returned by qpdf_init or NULL
After return, the handle is invalid; do not reuse
Caller must have freed any malloc-allocated buffers (e.g., from qpdf_oh_get_stream_data/qpdf_oh_get_page_content_data)

functions.name: qpdf_has_error
functions.description: Returns whether the current qpdf_data has a pending error to be retrieved by qpdf_get_error.

functions.description: Returns and clears the current error. The returned pointer becomes invalid after the next call to this function, qpdf_next_warning, or qpdf_cleanup.
requirements: qpdf must be valid

functions.name: qpdf_more_warnings
functions.description: Returns whether there are unretrieved warnings.
requirements: qpdf must be valid

functions.name: qpdf_next_warning
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the next warning or NULL if none. May invalidate any previous error/warning pointer per documentation.
requirements: qpdf must be valid

functions.description: Runs the second stage of a two-stage job (wrapping QPDFJob::writeQPDF), writing out the provided qpdf_data. Returns the qpdf exit code as with command-line invocation. The caller is responsible for cleaning up the qpdf_data after this call.
requirements: j must be a valid qpdfjob_handle that corresponds to the job used to create the qpdf_data
qpdf must be a qpdf_data object (typically obtained from qpdfjob_create_qpdf)
Caller must call qpdf_cleanup on qpdf after qpdfjob_write_qpdf returns to free associated resources
Return value is a qpdf exit code compatible with qpdf_exit_code_e; callers should handle nonzero as failure per qpdf semantics

functions.name: qpdfjob_register_progress_reporter
functions.signature: void qpdfjob_register_progress_reporter(qpdfjob_handle j, void (*report_progress)(int percent, void* data), void* data);
functions.description: Registers a custom progress reporter callback for the job. The callback is invoked only if progress reporting is otherwise enabled (e.g., via --progress or corresponding JSON). The data pointer is passed through to the callback.
requirements: j must be a valid qpdfjob_handle
report_progress must be a valid function pointer if progress reporting is desired
The callback may be called only when progress is requested (per the --progress option or JSON "progress")

functions.name: qpdflogger_default_logger
functions.description: Returns a handle to the process-wide default QPDF logger. Use this when you want to direct logging without creating a new logger. The returned handle is a lightweight handle to an underlying shared logger object; when you are finished with the handle, call qpdflogger_cleanup to release the handle (the underlying logger remains alive while referenced elsewhere).
requirements: Call qpdflogger_cleanup on the returned handle when finished with it to release the handle.
Do not assume this destroys the underlying logger; it is shared and may persist.

functions.name: qpdflogger_create
functions.description: Creates a new logger and returns a handle to it. This is used when you want an independent logger (separate from the default logger). Cleaning up the handle does not destroy the underlying shared logger object until no longer referenced.
requirements: Call qpdflogger_cleanup on the returned handle when finished with it to release the handle.
Do not assume this destroys the underlying logger; it is shared and may persist.

functions.name: qpdflogger_cleanup
functions.description: Releases and cleans up a logger handle. This destroys the handle but not the underlying logger object (which is shared and will be cleaned up automatically when no longer in use). Pass the address of the handle you wish to clean up.
requirements: l must be a valid, non-null pointer to a qpdflogger_handle obtained from qpdflogger_default_logger or qpdflogger_create (or passed back from related APIs).
Cleaning up affects only the handle; the underlying logger remains until no references remain.

functions.name: qpdflogger_set_info
functions.signature: void qpdflogger_set_info(qpdflogger_handle l, enum qpdf_log_dest_e dest, qpdf_log_fn_t fn, void* udata);
functions.description: Configures the destination for informational-level log messages for the given logger. You can route info logs to the default destination, stdout, stderr, discard, or a custom callback. If a custom destination is selected, the provided callback will be invoked with data and length; it should return 0 on success.
requirements: l must be a valid logger handle.
dest must be one of: qpdf_log_dest_default, qpdf_log_dest_stdout, qpdf_log_dest_stderr, qpdf_log_dest_discard, qpdf_log_dest_custom.
If a custom log function is used, the function must conform to qpdf_log_fn_t and return 0 on success (as documented).
Behavior when fn is NULL is unknown; provide a valid function if using qpdf_log_dest_custom.
udata is an opaque pointer passed back to the callback; no constraints are specified.

functions.name: qpdflogger_set_warn
functions.signature: void qpdflogger_set_warn(qpdflogger_handle l, enum qpdf_log_dest_e dest, qpdf_log_fn_t fn, void* udata);
functions.description: Configures the destination for warning-level log messages for the given logger. Supports default, stdout, stderr, discard, or a custom callback. Custom callbacks receive message bytes and length and should return 0 on success.
requirements: l must be a valid logger handle.
dest must be one of: qpdf_log_dest_default, qpdf_log_dest_stdout, qpdf_log_dest_stderr, qpdf_log_dest_discard, qpdf_log_dest_custom.
If a custom log function is used, the function must conform to qpdf_log_fn_t and return 0 on success (as documented).
Behavior when fn is NULL is unknown; provide a valid function if using qpdf_log_dest_custom.
udata is an opaque pointer passed back to the callback; no constraints are specified.

functions.name: qpdflogger_set_error
functions.signature: void qpdflogger_set_error(qpdflogger_handle l, enum qpdf_log_dest_e dest, qpdf_log_fn_t fn, void* udata);
functions.description: Configures the destination for error-level log messages for the given logger. Supports default, stdout, stderr, discard, or a custom callback. For custom destinations, the callback is invoked with message bytes and length and should return 0 on success.
requirements: l must be a valid logger handle.
dest must be one of: qpdf_log_dest_default, qpdf_log_dest_stdout, qpdf_log_dest_stderr, qpdf_log_dest_discard, qpdf_log_dest_custom.
If a custom log function is used, the function must conform to qpdf_log_fn_t and return 0 on success (as documented).
Behavior when fn is NULL is unknown; provide a valid function if using qpdf_log_dest_custom.
udata is an opaque pointer passed back to the callback; no constraints are specified.

functions.name: qpdflogger_set_save
functions.signature: void qpdflogger_set_save(qpdflogger_handle l, enum qpdf_log_dest_e dest, qpdf_log_fn_t fn, void* udata, int only_if_not_set);
functions.description: Sets the destination used by the logger’s save pipeline (i.e., where logged output is saved). You can direct save output to default, stdout, stderr, discard, or a custom callback. If only_if_not_set is non-zero, the save destination will be changed only if it is not already set.
requirements: l must be a valid logger handle.
dest must be one of: qpdf_log_dest_default, qpdf_log_dest_stdout, qpdf_log_dest_stderr, qpdf_log_dest_discard, qpdf_log_dest_custom.
If a custom log function is used, the function must conform to qpdf_log_fn_t and return 0 on success (as documented).
Behavior when fn is NULL is unknown; provide a valid function if using qpdf_log_dest_custom.
only_if_not_set: pass a non-zero value to avoid overwriting an already-set save pipeline; pass 0 to force setting.
udata is an opaque pointer passed back to the callback; no constraints are specified.

functions.name: qpdflogger_save_to_standard_output
functions.description: Convenience function to set the logger’s save pipeline to standard output. If only_if_not_set is non-zero, the save destination is changed only if it is not already set.
requirements: l must be a valid logger handle.
only_if_not_set: pass a non-zero value to avoid overwriting an already-set save pipeline; pass 0 to force setting.

functions.name: qpdflogger_equal
functions.description: Compares two logger handles for equality (intended primarily for testing). Returns a non-zero value if the handles refer to the same underlying logger and zero otherwise (inferred from name and typical C conventions; exact return semantics beyond non-zero/zero are not documented).
requirements: l1 and l2 must be valid logger handles.
Return value semantics beyond zero/non-zero are not explicitly documented; treat any non-zero as equal and zero as not equal.
